teile.einleitung: A building zone is an area in which you may build houses, factories or shops. Outside the building zones, building in Switzerland is strongly restricted. This is meant to use the land sparingly and protect the landscape.
wichtigste: Building zones decide where building is allowed.
The rules are in the Federal Spatial Planning Act (RPG).
In 2022 there were around 234,000 hectares of building zones in Switzerland, a good 5 per cent of the country's area.
46 per cent of the building zones were residential zones in 2022.
Building zones may be large enough for at most 15 years of need.
Anyone who makes a profit through rezoning must give up at least 20 per cent of it.

abschnitte.text: Every municipality has a **zoning plan**. It says which land may be used for what. In **building zones** building is allowed, but in agricultural zones or in forest generally it is not. There are different kinds of building zones: **residential zones**, work zones, mixed zones and centre zones. In 2022, 46 per cent of all building zones were residential zones.

abschnitte.titel: Figures from the building zone statistics
abschnitte.text: According to the **building zone statistics 2022**, there were 234,337 hectares of building zones in Switzerland. That is a good 5 per cent of the country's area. For each person living in a building zone it was around **282 m²** in 2022, compared with 309 m² in 2012. So the population grew while the area stayed about the same. Depending on the calculation, **10 to 16 per cent** of the building zones were still not built on.

abschnitte.titel: Rules in the Spatial Planning Act
abschnitte.text: The **Spatial Planning Act (RPG)** says: building zones should match the expected need of **15 years**. If they are too big, they must be reduced. When land is taken out of the building zone, it is called **dezoning** or rezoning back. Depending on the case, the owner must then be compensated. Free areas in existing building zones should be used first before new land is zoned.

If farmland becomes building land, its value rises sharply. This is called **rezoning as building land** (Einzonung). From this profit, the **added value**, at least **20 per cent** must be given up. With the money, for example, compensation for dezoning can be paid.

Even in the building zone you need a **building permit**. For this the building must fit the zone, which is called **in conformity with the zone**. In addition, the plot must be **serviced**. Servicing includes an access road and pipes for water, energy and sewage.

gewusst: A hectare is as big as a square of 100 by 100 metres, so a little bigger than a football pitch.
In 2013 the Swiss voters accepted a change to the Spatial Planning Act that is meant to prevent building zones that are too big.

teile.einleitung: The Saint Bernard is a very large dog with white and reddish-brown patched fur. It comes from the Great St Bernard, an Alpine pass in the Valais. There the dogs used to help find lost people in the snow.
wichtigste: The Saint Bernard is named after the Great St Bernard.
It is regarded as the Swiss national dog.
Saint Bernards are among the largest and heaviest breeds of dog.
The most famous Saint Bernard was called Barry and lived from 1800 to 1814.
Barry is said to have rescued more than 40 people.
The Fondation Barry in Martigny breeds Saint Bernards today.

abschnitte.text: On the **Great St Bernard** a **hospice** has stood since the Middle Ages. This is a house where travellers get shelter and help. The canons of the hospice kept big dogs. With their good noses the dogs found people who had got lost in the fog and snow. From these dogs the breed of **Saint Bernard** came about.

The most famous Saint Bernard was called **Barry**. He lived from **1800 to 1814** and worked for many years at the hospice. According to tradition he rescued **more than 40 people**. The exact number differs depending on the source. After his death Barry was preserved by a taxidermist. Today he stands in the **Natural History Museum of Bern**.

Saint Bernards are among the **largest and heaviest** breeds of dog. They can weigh more than 60 kilograms. Their coat is **white with reddish-brown patches** or large markings. There is a short-haired and a long-haired variety. Saint Bernards are regarded as calm and friendly.

The Saint Bernard comes from Switzerland and is regarded as the **Swiss national dog**. Today smaller, lighter dogs are mostly used for searching in the snow. The **Fondation Barry** in **Martigny** in the Valais goes on breeding Saint Bernards. In the **Barryland** you can visit the dogs.

gewusst: The picture of the Saint Bernard with a little barrel around its neck is an invention of painters, the dogs did not really wear such barrels.
In summer you can also visit Saint Bernards at the top of the Great St Bernard.

teile.einleitung: Bellinzona is the main town of the canton of Ticino. The city lies in the valley of the River Ticino, where important routes across the Alps come together. It is famous for its three medieval castles.
wichtigste: Bellinzona is the capital of the canton of Ticino.
The three castles have been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 2000.
The largest castle is called Castelgrande and used to bear the name Uri.
The Federal Criminal Court has its seat in Bellinzona.
Since 2017, 13 former municipalities together form the city of Bellinzona.
The big carnival is called Rabadan.

abschnitte.text: Above the city stand three castles: **Castelgrande**, **Montebello** and **Sasso Corbaro**. Together with the city walls they used to block the valley. Anyone who wanted to go south over the Alpine passes came past Bellinzona. After 1500 the Original Cantons ruled the area. The castles therefore received the names **Uri**, Schwyz and Unterwalden. The largest, Castelgrande, was called Uri. Since 2000 the castles have belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

Bellinzona is the **main town of the canton of Ticino**. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament meet here. Since 2004 the **Federal Criminal Court** has also had its seat in Bellinzona. It judges certain crimes for which the Confederation is responsible. So not every federal authority is in Bern.

In **2017** Bellinzona merged with twelve neighbouring municipalities. Since then 13 former municipalities form the new city. As a result Bellinzona has over 40,000 inhabitants. Such **municipal mergers** happen in Switzerland again and again, because large municipalities can often carry out their tasks more easily.

Every **Saturday morning** a big **market** takes place in the old town. Traders sell vegetables, cheese, cured meats and crafts from Ticino. In winter Bellinzona celebrates the **Rabadan**. It is one of the biggest carnivals in Switzerland and takes place every year before Ash Wednesday.

gewusst: The castles of Bellinzona are lit up in the evening and can be seen from far away.
Castelgrande stands on a rocky hill in the middle of the city, and a lift leads up through the rock.

teile.einleitung: The Titlis is a high mountain near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. It is 3,238 metres high and has a glacier on which there is snow all year round.
wichtigste: The Titlis is 3,238 metres high.
It lies near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden, on the border with the canton of Bern.
On the Titlis there is a glacier with an ice cave.
Several cable cars lead up from Engelberg.
The last one is called the Rotair, and its cabin rotates.
At the top there is a suspension bridge over the abyss.

abschnitte.text: At **3,238 metres** the Titlis is one of the highest mountains in central Switzerland. Its summit is covered by a **glacier**. That is why there is snow up there even in summer. Like most glaciers in the Alps, the Titlis glacier is also getting smaller because of warmer temperatures.

From **Engelberg** you travel up the mountain in several stages. On the way you pass **Trübsee**. The last section leads on the **Titlis Rotair** to the top station on the Klein Titlis. Its cabin turns once completely round on itself during the ride. So every passenger sees the mountains all around.

In the **ice cave** you walk along a passage in the middle of the glacier ice. It is cold there even in summer. Outside, the **Titlis Cliff Walk** leads across a deep gorge. This **suspension bridge** is considered one of the highest in Europe. In the snow you can go sledging or glide over the glacier on a chairlift.

**Engelberg** is a holiday resort in a valley in the canton of Obwalden. Well known is the large **Engelberg Abbey**, which was founded as early as the Middle Ages. In winter many guests come to ski, in summer to walk. The Titlis attracts visitors from all over the world.

gewusst: The summit of the Titlis lies exactly on the border between Obwalden and Bern.
On the Titlis you can play in the snow even in midsummer.

teile.einleitung: Zug is the main town of the canton of Zug. The city has the same name as the canton and lies on the shore of Lake Zug. It has a lovely old town and is an important place for business.
wichtigste: Zug is the main town of the canton of Zug.
City and canton have the same name.
The city lies on the north-eastern shore of Lake Zug.
The landmark is the Zytturm (Clock Tower) in the old town.
Many international companies have their seat in Zug.
The Zug cherry cake is well known.

abschnitte.text: The city of **Zug** lies on **Lake Zug**, on the slopes of the **Zugerberg**. From the shore you can see the **Rigi** and the Alps in fine weather. The lovely **sunsets** over the lake are well known. A **funicular** leads up the Zugerberg, and at the top you can walk and enjoy the view.

Zug has a well-preserved **old town** with old houses and narrow lanes. The landmark is the **Zytturm**, the Clock Tower. It has a blue and white roof in the colours of the canton and a large **clock**. In **1887** part of the suburb on the shore slid into the **lake**. This disaster is called the **Vorstadt disaster** (the “suburb disaster”).

In the canton of Zug the **taxes** are comparatively **low**. That is why many **companies** have settled here, including from abroad. People from many countries work in Zug. Because many firms dealing in **digital currencies** have settled here, people also speak of the “**Crypto Valley**”.

Around Zug many **cherry trees** grow. Among other things, **Kirsch**, a cherry brandy, is made from the cherries. World-famous is the **Zug cherry cake**. It consists of sponge, buttercream and crunchy nut layers and is soaked with Kirsch. In the lake there also lives a special fish, the **Zuger Rötel**.

gewusst: The Zytturm in Zug shows not only the time but also the course of the moon and the day of the week.
Despite its small area, the canton of Zug is an important business location in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Waldenburg Railway is a railway in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. It runs from Liestal through the Waldenburg valley to Waldenburg and, until 2021, had the narrowest gauge in Switzerland at 75 centimetres.
wichtigste: The Waldenburg Railway runs from Liestal to Waldenburg.
It opened in 1880.
Until 2021 it had a gauge of only 75 centimetres.
That was the narrowest gauge in Switzerland.
After the conversion it runs on metre gauge.
Today BLT operates the railway.

abschnitte.text: The **Waldenburg Railway** opened in **1880**. It links **Liestal**, the main town of the canton of Basel-Landschaft, with **Waldenburg**. The route runs through the narrow **Waldenburg valley** and is about 13 kilometres long. In the past it ran with steam locomotives, later by electricity.

The **gauge** is the distance between the two rails. On the Waldenburg Railway it was only **75 centimetres**. That was the narrowest gauge of all public railways in Switzerland. Normal railways have 143.5 centimetres, many mountain railways one metre. The narrow track was cheap to build and fitted well in the narrow valley.

The old installations had grown old. So from **2021** the railway was completely renewed. In the process the gauge was widened to **one metre**. There are new tracks, new stops and modern trains. Today **BLT** (Baselland Transport) runs the railway as line 19.

gewusst: An old steam locomotive of the Waldenburg Railway is called “Gedeon Thommen”, after a watch manufacturer from Waldenburg.
The old Waldenburg Railway ran on its narrow track for over 140 years.

teile.einleitung: The Seelisberg Tunnel is a long motorway tunnel in central Switzerland. It links Nidwalden with the canton of Uri and is an important part of the north-south route through Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Seelisberg Tunnel is part of the A2 motorway.
It runs from Beckenried in Nidwalden to Seedorf in Uri.
It is around 9 kilometres long.
It opened in 1980.
The tunnel passes under the Seelisberg mountain, on the shore of Lake Lucerne.

abschnitte.text: The **Seelisberg Tunnel** is a tunnel on the **A2 motorway**, which runs from Basel to Chiasso. It begins at **Beckenried** in the canton of **Nidwalden** and ends at **Seedorf** in the canton of **Uri**. At around **9 kilometres** it is one of the longest road tunnels in Switzerland. It has **two tubes**, one for each direction of travel. So cars never drive in oncoming traffic.

The tunnel passes through the mountain near the village of **Seelisberg**. This lies on the southern shore of **Lake Lucerne**. In the past, cars heading south had to take the winding **Axenstrasse** or a boat. With the tunnel the journey became much faster and safer. Beyond Seedorf the road continues towards the Gotthard.

The Seelisberg Tunnel was built in the **1970s** and opened in **1980**. The **Gotthard road tunnel** opened in the same year. In the tunnel there are **emergency exits**, telephones and ventilation systems. Large fans make sure that exhaust fumes are blown out.

gewusst: Before the tunnel was built there was no motorway between Nidwalden and Uri.
Thousands of cars and lorries drive through the tunnel every day.

teile.einleitung: The Aar Massif is a large mountain core in the Swiss Alps. It consists of very old, hard rock such as granite and gneiss. Well-known areas are the Grimsel and the Bernese Oberland.
wichtigste: The Aar Massif consists mainly of granite and gneiss.
It is a central massif of old European basement rock.
The Central Aare Granite is around 300 million years old.
On the Grimsel Pass lies the largest body of granite in Switzerland.
In the west the massif continues in the Mont Blanc Massif.
The Gotthard Base Tunnel begins in the Aar Massif.

abschnitte.text: The Aar Massif belongs to the **crystalline basement**. It consists mainly of **gneisses** and **granites**, with schists and amphibolite as well. These rocks are much older than the Alps themselves. When the Alps were formed, the old basement was lifted up. Experts call it an **external crystalline massif**.

abschnitte.titel: The Aare Granite at the Grimsel
abschnitte.text: The **Central Aare Granite** solidified around 300 million years ago deep in the Earth's crust. It is the largest body of granite in Switzerland. Over around 500 square kilometres it comes to the surface, for example at the **Grimsel Pass**, near the Göscheneralp and in the Reuss Valley. The smoothly polished granite slabs at the Grimsel come from the glaciers of the Ice Age.

On the northern edge a cover of younger **sediments** from the Jurassic, Cretaceous and early Tertiary lies on the crystalline rock. The **Eiger** and the **Titlis**, for example, are made of it. At the **Jungfrau** the crystalline rock was pushed slightly north over these limestones. That is why old gneiss lies there on top of younger limestone.

South-west of **Leuk** the Aar Massif dips beneath other rock layers. It continues in the **Mont Blanc Massif** and the **Aiguilles Rouges Massif**. The **Gotthard Base Tunnel** begins at Erstfeld in the Aar Massif. After that it crosses the Tavetsch Intermediate Massif and the Gotthard Massif and ends in the gneisses of the Leventina.

gewusst: The rock of the Aare Granite is around 300 million years old, much older than the Alps.
The Gotthard Base Tunnel is like a journey through several rock worlds of the Alps.

teile.einleitung: The University of St Gallen is a university in the city of St Gallen. It is often called HSG for short. It is especially well known for business and management.
wichtigste: The University of St Gallen is called HSG for short.
It was founded in 1898 as a commercial academy.
It is especially well known for economics and management.
You can also study law, international affairs and other subjects there.
Students come to St Gallen from many countries.

abschnitte.text: The institution was founded in **1898** as a **commercial academy**. At that time St Gallen was a rich city that traded **embroidery** and fabrics all over the world. Young people were to learn how to run trade and business. In time the small school became a **university**. The abbreviation HSG comes from its earlier German name, **Hochschule St. Gallen**.

The HSG is especially well known for **economics**. This includes subjects such as **business administration**, that is, how to run a company, and **national economics**, which deals with the economy of a whole country. Many of its programmes do well in international rankings. But you can also study **law**, international affairs and other subjects.

The university lies on the **Rosenberg** above the city of St Gallen. The buildings are modern and decorated with a lot of **art**. Works by well-known artists stand right in the corridors and lecture halls. There are also newer buildings, for example a learning centre for students.

At the HSG, young people from Switzerland and from **many other countries** study. Many courses are held in **English**. The university works closely with universities all over the world. Many students spend part of their studies abroad.

gewusst: Every year the St Gallen Symposium takes place at the HSG, a meeting of young people with experts from business and politics.
The abbey district of St Gallen with the famous Abbey Library is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

t147qpl2.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden shows an upright black bear on a white ground. Next to the bear are the letters V and R.
wichtigste: In the coat of arms of Appenzell Ausserrhoden stands a black bear.
The ground is white.
Next to the bear are the letters V and R.
V and R stand for “Usser Rhoden”.
The letters distinguish the coat of arms from that of Innerrhoden.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Appenzell Ausserrhoden** a **black bear** stands upright on its hind legs. The ground is **white**. To the left and right of the bear are the letters **V** and **R**. They mean **“Usser Rhoden”** (in dialect), that is, the outer Rhoden.

A **Rhode** was formerly a district in the Appenzell region. In **1597** the land of Appenzell split into two parts. The reason was above all faith: the outer Rhoden became **Reformed** (Protestant), the inner ones stayed **Catholic**. This is how Ausserrhoden and Innerrhoden came about, which are now two cantons of their own.

Both Appenzells have the bear in their coat of arms. It comes from the time when the area belonged to the **Abbey of St Gallen**. So that the coats of arms can be told apart, Ausserrhoden added the letters **V** and **R**. The V is the old way of writing the letter U.

gewusst: In the past the letter U was often written like a V, so “VR” in the coat of arms stands for “Usser Rhoden”.
The bear in the Appenzell coat of arms goes back to the legend of Saint Gallus, who is said to have been helped by a bear.

teile.einleitung: The Vereina Tunnel is a railway tunnel of the Rhaetian Railway in the canton of Graubünden. It links Klosters in the Prättigau with the Lower Engadine and opened in 1999.
wichtigste: The Vereina Tunnel is in the canton of Graubünden.
It links Klosters with the Lower Engadine.
The tunnel is around 19 kilometres long.
It opened in 1999.
Cars are loaded onto the train and travel with it.
It belongs to the Rhaetian Railway.

abschnitte.text: The **Vereina Tunnel** is around **19 kilometres** long. It runs under the mountains from **Klosters** in the Prättigau to Sagliains near Susch and Lavin in the **Lower Engadine**. It opened in **1999**. The tunnel belongs to the **Rhaetian Railway**, which runs on narrow metre gauge in Graubünden.

If you want to go to the Engadine by car, you can load it onto the **car train**. You drive your car onto an open wagon and stay in it during the journey. After about 20 minutes you are on the other side. So you do not have to drive over a high pass. That is especially handy in winter.

Before it was built, the way into the Lower Engadine led over the **Flüela Pass**. This pass is over 2,300 metres high and is often closed in winter. Thanks to the tunnel, the Engadine can be reached easily all year round. Besides car trains, normal **passenger trains** also run through the tunnel. They link, for example, Landquart with Scuol.

During construction the workers had to drill and blast through hard rock. The tunnel is mostly **single-track**. In the middle there is a point where trains can pass each other. For the Rhaetian Railway the Vereina Tunnel was one of the biggest construction projects in its history.

gewusst: The Vereina Tunnel is one of the longest tunnels in the world for metre-gauge trains.
Both car trains and passenger trains of the Rhaetian Railway run through the Vereina Tunnel.

teile.einleitung: The St Gallen bratwurst is a famous speciality from eastern Switzerland. The pale sausage is made mainly from veal and is popular throughout Switzerland.
wichtigste: The St Gallen bratwurst is a white sausage made mainly from veal.
It comes from the canton of St Gallen and is known throughout Switzerland.
It is traditionally eaten with a Bürli.
Many people in St Gallen prefer to eat it without mustard.
The name is protected: only sausages made to the set recipe may be called this.

abschnitte.text: The **St Gallen bratwurst** is pale, almost white. It is made mainly from **veal**. Pork, bacon, **milk** and spices are added. The milk makes the sausage meat fine and pale. The sausage is first scalded and then fried on the grill or in a pan.

A **Bürli**, a small, crusty bread roll, goes with the St Gallen bratwurst. At stalls you often simply get the sausage in your hand with a Bürli. Many people in St Gallen think that a good bratwurst needs **no mustard**. The mustard would drown out the delicate flavour. Of course, if you like, you may still take mustard.

As early as the **Middle Ages** there were rules for butchers in St Gallen. They set out how sausages had to be made. Today the St Gallen bratwurst is a **protected geographical indication**. This means that only sausages from the region, made to the set recipe, may carry this name. In this way the quality stays the same.

Every autumn the **OLMA** takes place in St Gallen, a big trade fair for farming and food. There you can get the **OLMA bratwurst**, which is especially large. Many visitors come for the sausage too. The bratwurst is a real piece of **eastern Swiss culture**.

gewusst: A document from the year 1438 already contains rules from the St Gallen butchers for bratwursts.
The St Gallen bratwurst is also sold at many Swiss festivals and sporting events.

teile.einleitung: The Vogel Gryff is an old custom in Kleinbasel in the canton of Basel-Stadt. Every year in January three figures dance through the streets: the Vogel Gryff, the Leu and the Wilde Maa.
wichtigste: The Vogel Gryff takes place every year in January in Kleinbasel.
The three figures are called Vogel Gryff, Leu and Wilde Maa.
The Vogel Gryff is a griffin, the Leu a lion.
The Wilde Maa travels down the Rhine on a raft.
Three old honorary societies stand behind the custom.
During the dance the figures turn their backs on Grossbasel.

abschnitte.text: Three figures appear at the Vogel Gryff. The **Vogel Gryff** is a **griffin**, a mythical creature with the head of an eagle. The **Leu** is a lion. The **Wilde Maa** is a wild man with a small tree in his hand. Each figure belongs to one of the three **honorary societies** of Kleinbasel.

The day begins with the Wilde Maa's journey downstream. He stands on a **raft** and travels down the **Rhine**. Drummers and cannon shots accompany him. Then he steps ashore and meets the other two figures. Together they walk through the streets of Kleinbasel.

To the sound of drums the three figures dance in many places in **Kleinbasel**. A special moment is the dance on the **Mittlere Brücke** (Middle Bridge). There the figures turn their backs on Grossbasel on the other side of the Rhine. This is an old joke between the two parts of the city. Companions collect money for people in need.

The custom takes place every year on one day in **January**. The date alternates between the three honorary societies. For many people in Kleinbasel it is a festival day. Children like watching the figures, though some also feel a little respect for them.

gewusst: During the dance on the Middle Bridge the figures deliberately turn their backs on Grossbasel.
The Vogel Gryff is not a carnival custom but a festival day of its own for the people of Kleinbasel.

teile.einleitung: The Wildspitz is the highest point of the canton of Zug. It lies on the ridge of the Rossberg on the border with the canton of Schwyz and is about 1,580 metres high.
wichtigste: The Wildspitz is about 1,580 metres high.
It is the highest point of the canton of Zug.
It lies on the Rossberg.
The border between Zug and Schwyz runs over the summit.
At the top stands a mountain inn with a wide view.
In 1806 the Goldau landslide started from the Rossberg.

abschnitte.text: The **Wildspitz**, at about **1,580 metres**, is the highest point in the canton of Zug. It lies on the long ridge of the **Rossberg**. The **cantonal border** with the canton of Schwyz runs over the summit. That is why the mountain belongs to both cantons. Compared with the Alps it is rather low, but it towers above its surroundings.

From the summit you can see far across the land. Below lie **Lake Zug**, **Lake Ägeri** and **Lake Lauerz**. Opposite rise the **Rigi** and the **Mythen**. In clear weather you can also see the peaks of the **Alps**. On the Wildspitz stands a **mountain inn** where walkers can stop for a meal.

In **1806** a huge mass of **rock and earth** broke away from the Rossberg. It fell into the valley and buried the village of **Goldau** and further hamlets. It was one of the worst natural disasters in Switzerland, and many people lost their lives. Today the **Goldau Nature and Animal Park** grows on the area of the landslide.

gewusst: You can only reach the Wildspitz on foot, as there is no railway to the summit.
The place where the 1806 landslide broke away can still be seen clearly on the Rossberg today.

teile.einleitung: Old-age provision makes sure that people have money to live on even after retirement. In Switzerland it rests on three pillars. These include the AHV, the pension fund and private saving.
wichtigste: Old-age provision rests on three pillars: state, occupational and private.
The AHV has existed since 1948 and is the first pillar.
The three-pillar principle has been in the Federal Constitution since 1972.
The pension fund has been compulsory since 1985.
With AHV 21 the reference age of 65 applies to women and men.
In 2024 the voters accepted the 13th AHV pension.

abschnitte.text: On 3 December 1972 the people and the cantons put the **three-pillar principle** into the Federal Constitution. The **first pillar** is the state AHV (old-age and survivors' insurance). The **second pillar** is occupational provision, that is, the pension fund. The **third pillar** is private saving. Together they are meant to make a good life possible in old age.

The **Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance** (AHV) was accepted by the people in 1947. On 1 January 1948 the first **pensions** were paid out. People who work pay part of their wages into the AHV. The money goes straight to today's pensioners, which is called a **pay-as-you-go system**. If the pension is not enough, there are **supplementary benefits**.

Since 1 January 1985 **occupational provision** has been compulsory for employees. The basis is the **BVG** law. Employees and employers pay into a **pension fund**. There money is saved up for each person, which is called a **funded system**.

The third pillar is **private saving**. With **Pillar 3a** you can pay in up to a maximum amount every year. You may **deduct** this amount from your taxable income. In return the money is tied up until shortly before retirement. Free saving is called Pillar 3b.

The **AHV 21** reform was narrowly accepted in 2022. From 2025 the **reference age** of women rises in steps of three months from 64 to 65 years. On 3 March 2024 the people and the cantons said yes to a **13th AHV pension**. From 2026 it is paid out once a year. How the AHV is to be financed in future is often discussed in politics.

gewusst: The term “reference age” replaces the earlier word “retirement age”.
The three pillars of old-age provision are regarded worldwide as a Swiss special feature.

teile.einleitung: On 2 September 1806 a huge mass of rock broke away on the Rossberg in the canton of Schwyz. It buried the village of Goldau and other settlements. The Goldau landslide is one of the worst natural disasters in Swiss history.
wichtigste: The landslide happened on 2 September 1806.
The mass of rock broke away at the Gnipenspitze on the Rossberg.
Almost 40 million m³ of nagelfluh fell into the valley.
457 people lost their lives.
In Lake Lauerz a flood wave about 20 m high arose.
Afterwards there was the first nationwide fundraising campaign in Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: Why the mountain started to slide
abschnitte.text: The **Rossberg** consists of layers of **nagelfluh** and **marl**. Nagelfluh is a rock made of cemented pebbles, marl a soft, clayey rock. The layers slope towards the valley. In the Ice Age an arm of the **Reuss Glacier** had worn away the foot of the slope, so that the support was missing. After a lot of rain, water got in through clefts and softened the marl. On this slippery layer the nagelfluh slid down into the valley.

The break-off began at the **Gnipenspitze** on the south flank of the Rossberg. Almost **40 million m³** of rock slid around 1,000 m down into the valley and covered about 6.5 km². That is more than ten times as much as in the Bondo rockslide of 2017. The fall lasted **less than three minutes**. For most of the inhabitants escape was therefore impossible.

In the landslide **457 people** died, and 323 head of cattle also lost their lives. Part of the fallen mass plunged into **Lake Lauerz**. Eyewitnesses reported a wave about **20 m high**. The lake also lost around a seventh of its area.

After the disaster, money was collected for the first time in **the whole of Switzerland** for the victims of a natural disaster. The Goldau landslide was also the first to be **studied scientifically**. After the Basel earthquake of 1356 it is regarded as the greatest documented natural disaster in Switzerland.

In the deposition area huge **boulders** still lie today. Right among these boulders is the **Goldau Nature and Animal Park**. There live, for example, deer, wolves and bears. On the Rossberg you can still see the pale break-off scar today.

gewusst: Some boulders in the Goldau animal park are as big as a house.
Goldau is today an important railway junction on the Gotthard line.

teile.einleitung: The Wickelfisch is a waterproof floating bag in the shape of a fish. In Basel people pack their clothes into it and let themselves drift down the Rhine with it in summer.
wichtigste: The Wickelfisch is a waterproof bag.
It looks like a fish.
You pack clothes, a mobile phone or keys into it.
Then you roll it shut at the top so that no water gets in.
The bag floats and you can hold on to it.
It is very popular for swimming in the Rhine in Basel.

abschnitte.text: The **Wickelfisch** is made of strong, **waterproof** fabric. It has the shape of a **fish**. You put your things inside and **roll up** the opening several times. That is where the name comes from, since “wickeln” means to wrap or roll. Then the bag is closed with a fastener. This way everything inside stays dry.

abschnitte.titel: Swimming in the Rhine in Basel
abschnitte.text: On warm summer days many people swim in the **Rhine** in **Basel**. They get into the water upstream and let the **current** carry them. Further down they get out again. They take the Wickelfisch with them so that they have dry clothes afterwards. The fish also helps with **swimming**, because it floats on top.

The Rhine is a big river with a **strong current**. So you should only swim if you can **swim well**. Stay close to the bank and keep away from **ships** and bridge piers. The Wickelfisch is **not a life jacket**, but it helps you to rest. Children swim only with adults.

gewusst: Many tourists buy a Wickelfisch as a souvenir of Basel.
The Wickelfisch comes in many bright colours.

teile.einleitung: The southern side of the Alps is the area south of the main Alpine ridge, above all Ticino. There the climate is mild and sunny, but it can also rain very heavily. Palms, chestnuts and lakes shape the landscape.
wichtigste: Southern Ticino has a mild, sunny Insubrian climate.
With an annual mean of around 13 °C, Lugano is the warmest measuring site in Switzerland.
Sweet chestnuts shape the forests of the lower altitudes.
North foehn brings dry, clear weather to Ticino.
In autumn there is often heavy downpour.
Ticino is one of the hail hotspots of Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In southern Ticino and at the lakes of northern Italy the **Insubrian climate** prevails. It is mild, sunny and at the same time rich in rainfall. **Lugano** has an annual mean of around 13 °C (reference period 1991 to 2020) and is the warmest measuring site in Switzerland. The Alps protect the area from cold air from the north. From 1961 to 1990 the mean was still 11.6 °C, so it has risen by around 1.4 °C.

At lower altitudes the **sweet chestnut** shapes the forests. The Romans introduced it, and for a long time it was an important food. The **windmill palm** comes from Asia and was planted as an ornamental plant. Because of the mild winters it is now spreading more and more in the forests.

In **northerly stau** the air rains itself out on the northern side of the Alps. On the southern side it sinks, becomes dry and warm. This downslope wind is called **north foehn**. It brings Ticino windy, clear weather with a wide view.

In autumn the **Mediterranean** is still warm and supplies a lot of moisture. Southerly winds push this air against the Alps. There it rises and rains out heavily. That is why in Ticino, especially in autumn, there are **heavy downpours**. In addition, Ticino, along with the Napf area and the Jura, is one of Switzerland's **hail hotspots**.

Not everywhere in the south is it warm. The **Upper Engadine**, as a high valley, lies at around 1,800 metres, about 1,500 metres higher than Lugano. That is why it is much colder there. In Switzerland temperature depends above all on **height above sea level**.

gewusst: In Ticino palms grow outdoors, only a few hours from glaciers.
Chestnuts used to be so important in Ticino that they were called the “bread of the poor”.

teile.einleitung: The Great Aletsch Glacier in the Valais is the largest glacier in the Alps. It is around 20 kilometres long. Together with the Jungfrau, it belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: The Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps.
It lies in the canton of the Valais on the southern side of the Bernese Alps.
It is about 20 kilometres long and gets shorter every year.
At the Konkordiaplatz several streams of ice flow together.
Since 2001 it has been part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage Site.
The ice flows slowly down the valley, up to about 200 metres a year.

abschnitte.text: The **Great Aletsch Glacier** is the largest glacier in the whole of the Alps. It has more ice than any other Alpine glacier. It begins high up at the Jungfrau and flows down into the **Valais** on the southern side of the Bernese Alps. At around 20 kilometres, it is also the longest Alpine glacier.

At the **Konkordiaplatz** several glaciers meet. There the ice is several hundred metres thick. From here the Aletsch Glacier flows down the valley as a broad stream. On its surface you can see dark stripes of rock, the **moraines**.

Glacier ice is heavy and moves very slowly **down the valley**. At the Aletsch it is up to about 200 metres a year. But because it is getting warmer, more ice melts than newly arrives at the top. That is why the glacier becomes **shorter** and thinner every year.

From the **Eggishorn** near Fiesch you can see far over the long stream of ice. It can also be seen well from the Riederalp and the Bettmeralp. Above the glacier lies the **Aletsch Forest**. There **Swiss stone pines** grow that are several hundred years old.

The **Jungfrau-Aletsch** area was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** in 2001. It was the first natural World Heritage Site in the Alps. In this way the glaciers, mountains and forests of this area are especially protected.

gewusst: Some Swiss stone pines in the Aletsch Forest are many centuries old.

teile.einleitung: William Tell is the best-known legendary hero of Switzerland. According to the legend, he came from Bürglen in the canton of Uri. He is famous above all for the shot at the apple.
wichtigste: William Tell is a figure from an old legend.
He is said to have come from Bürglen in the canton of Uri.
According to the legend, he had to shoot an apple from his son's head.
He hit the apple with his crossbow.
The story is set at the time when the Confederation was founded.
Friedrich Schiller made the legend world-famous in 1804 with a play.

abschnitte.text: The legend tells of a strict **bailiff** called **Gessler**. In **Altdorf** he had a hat put on a pole. Everyone had to greet the hat. **Tell** did not. As a punishment he had to shoot an **apple** from the head of his son **Walter** with his **crossbow**. Tell hit the apple, and nothing happened to his son.

Gessler had Tell taken prisoner all the same. On **Lake Uri** the ship ran into a storm, and Tell was able to **escape** ashore. In the **Hohle Gasse** (Hollow Way) near Küssnacht he waited for Gessler and killed him with an arrow. In the legend this counts as the beginning of the **liberation** of central Switzerland from foreign rulers.

Whether William Tell really lived, nobody knows. The story was only written down around **200 years later**, for example in the **White Book of Sarnen**. Similar stories of a shot at an apple also exist in other countries. That is why most historians regard Tell as a **legendary figure**.

In **1804** the German poet **Friedrich Schiller** wrote the play “William Tell”. Later **Gioachino Rossini** composed an opera about it. In **Altdorf** the well-known **Tell Monument** has stood since **1895**. In **Bürglen** the **Tell Museum** tells of the legend and its traces.

gewusst: On the five-franc coin, the “Fünfliber”, a herdsman is shown whom many take for Tell.
In the Tell Play in Interlaken, Schiller's play has been performed in the open air for over 100 years.

teile.einleitung: The Valais Blacknose sheep is an old breed of sheep from the Upper Valais. It has a white, curly fleece but a black face, black ears and black patches on its legs.
wichtigste: The Valais Blacknose sheep comes from the Valais.
Its fleece is white and curly.
Face, nose and ears are black.
Knees and feet also have black patches.
The sheep have spiral horns.
They are well adapted to life in the mountains.

abschnitte.text: The **Valais Blacknose sheep** is easy to recognise. Its **fleece** is thick, white and curly. The **face** with the nose and the **ears**, by contrast, are black. It also has black patches on its knees and feet. Both the rams and the females have spiral **horns**.

The breed comes from the **Upper Valais**, above all from the area around Visp. The sheep are strong and sure-footed. In summer they graze on high **alpine pastures** in the mountains. Their thick fleece protects them from cold and wind. That is why they are well adapted to the harsh climate.

In the past the sheep were kept mainly for **wool** and meat. Today they are also very popular for their funny looks. Many people call them the most beautiful sheep in the world. They are often seen in photos and on postcards. They are now also bred in other countries.

gewusst: Valais Blacknose sheep are often called “the cutest sheep in the world” and are even in demand abroad.

t1968cjs.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Fribourg

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Fribourg is divided horizontally into two halves. The upper half is black, the lower half white.
wichtigste: The Fribourg coat of arms is divided horizontally.
It is black at the top and white at the bottom.
The flag of the canton has the same colours.
The canton has been part of the Confederation since 1481.
The main town is the city of Fribourg.

abschnitte.text: The **coat of arms of the canton of Fribourg** is very plain. It is divided **horizontally** into two halves of equal size. The **upper half is black**, the **lower white**. The canton's flag looks like this too. Where the colours come from exactly is not known for certain.

The city of **Fribourg** was founded in the 12th century by the **Zähringen** family. It lies on a rock above the **Sarine**. The city has a large medieval old town with the **Cathedral of St Nicholas**. The city's coat of arms shows a castle, but the canton carries only black and white.

Fribourg joined the Confederation in **1481**. The canton is **bilingual**: in the larger part people speak French, in the other German. The Sarine roughly forms the language border, which people jokingly call the “Röstigraben” (the “rösti ditch”).

gewusst: The black and white of the Fribourg coat of arms can also be seen on the shirts of the ice hockey club Fribourg-Gottéron.

t19cdtxp.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen

teile.einleitung: In the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen a black ram, that is, a male sheep, leaps on a yellow ground. The ram fits the name “Schaffhausen” well, because “Schaf” means sheep.
wichtigste: In the Schaffhausen coat of arms is a black ram.
A ram is a male sheep.
The ground is yellow or golden.
The ram leaps on its hind legs.
The coat of arms is a canting coat of arms, it fits the name.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Schaffhausen** you can see a **black ram**. A ram is a male sheep. It stands on its hind legs and seems to be **leaping**. The ground is **yellow**; in the language of heraldry it is called golden. The ram has strong, curved horns.

A **canting coat of arms** is a coat of arms that shows the name of a place as a picture. At the word **“Schaffhausen”** you think of a sheep, since “Schaf” is German for sheep. That is why the ram fits so well. But whether the name really comes from the sheep is not certain. Some think it comes from “Schiff” (ship), because many ships used to dock on the Rhine.

The canton of **Schaffhausen** lies almost entirely north of the **Rhine** and borders Germany. It joined the Confederation in **1501**. Near the city lie the **Rhine Falls**, the largest waterfall in central Europe. Above the old town stands the round fortress of **Munot**.

gewusst: On the coat of arms of the city of Schaffhausen the ram steps out of a tower, while in the cantonal coat of arms it leaps free.

teile.einleitung: The Spalentor is an old town gate in Basel. It once belonged to the Basel town wall and is regarded as one of the most beautiful town gates in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Spalentor stands in the city of Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt.
It was built around 1400 as part of the outer town wall.
It is one of three surviving town gates in Basel.
The gate has a colourful tiled roof and figures on its façade.
The road to Alsace led through the gate.

abschnitte.titel: A gate in the town wall
abschnitte.text: In the Middle Ages **Basel** was surrounded by a high **town wall**. Anyone who wanted to enter the town had to go through one of the **town gates**. The **Spalentor** was built around **1400**. It guarded the road that led west into **Alsace**. In the evening the gates were closed so that nobody could enter unseen.

The Spalentor consists of a tall, square **tower** and two round side towers. In the passage a heavy **portcullis** could be lowered. In front of it there used to be a ditch. The mighty wooden gates can still be seen today. In this way the people of Basel could defend their town against attackers.

The Spalentor is not only strong but also beautiful. Its roof is covered with **colour-glazed tiles** that form a pattern. On the outside stand **stone figures**, including a figure of **Mary** with the child. There are also coats of arms of the city of Basel. Today the gate is a **landmark** of Basel.

In the 19th century Basel grew rapidly. The town walls were no longer needed and were mostly pulled down. Only a few parts remained standing. Besides the Spalentor, the **St Alban Gate** and the **St Johann Gate** have also been preserved. Today trams run close past the Spalentor.

gewusst: The Spalentor is one of the cultural properties of national significance.
From the Spalentor the Spalenvorstadt, with many old houses, leads into the old town.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss National Park in the Engadine is the only national park in Switzerland. Here nature has been allowed to develop freely for over a hundred years, without people interfering.
wichtigste: The Swiss National Park lies in the canton of Graubünden, in the Engadine and the Val Müstair.
It was founded in 1914 and is the oldest national park in the Alps.
It covers around 170 square kilometres.
In the park nature is strictly protected: you must not leave the paths.
There you can watch deer, chamois, ibex and marmots.
The visitor centre is in Zernez.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss National Park** was founded on **1 August 1914**. It was the first national park in the Alps. The idea was to leave a piece of land entirely to nature. Since then there has been no hunting, no fishing, no logging and no grazing of livestock. Fallen trees stay where they are and become food for fungi and beetles.

Many large wild animals live in the park. Especially well known are the **red deer**, which you can hear roaring in autumn. There are also **chamois**, **ibex** and many **marmots**. **Golden eagles** circle in the sky, along with the **bearded vulture**, which has been reintroduced in the Alps. With binoculars you can often spot the animals from far away.

So that the animals are left in peace, **strict rules** apply in the park. You may only walk on the marked paths. Dogs are forbidden, as are bikes away from the roads. You must not pick flowers, take stones away or light fires. Staying overnight is only allowed in the huts provided.

The national park is also a large **open-air laboratory**. For decades researchers have been observing how forest, meadows and wildlife change without human influence. In **Zernez** stands the **visitor centre** with an exhibition. The road over the **Ofen Pass** runs through the park. Many hiking trails invite you to go on outings.

gewusst: The Swiss National Park is strictly protected, far more strictly than most other parks in Switzerland.
In the Val Trupchun you can often watch whole herds of deer in autumn.

teile.einleitung: Basel is the third largest city in Switzerland and lies in the far north-west of the country. Here Switzerland, France and Germany meet. The city on the Rhine is known for its museums, its industry and its long history.
wichtigste: Basel lies on the Rhine, which makes a big bend here: the Rhine knee.
The Rhine divides the city into Grossbasel and Kleinbasel.
Through the Rhine port Switzerland is linked by ship to the North Sea.
Chemicals and pharmaceuticals are the city's most important branches of industry.
The EuroAirport lies on French soil.
Basel has many famous museums, such as the Museum Tinguely and the Fondation Beyeler in Riehen.

abschnitte.titel: The city at the Rhine knee
abschnitte.text: At Basel the **Rhine** changes direction: it no longer flows west but north. This bend is called the **Rheinknie** (Rhine knee). On the left of the river lies **Grossbasel** (Greater Basel) with the old town and the Minster. On the right, northern side lies **Kleinbasel** (Lesser Basel). The oldest bridge is the **Mittlere Brücke** (Middle Bridge): as early as the 13th century a bridge stood here, and the present stone bridge dates from 1905.

Switzerland has no coast, but it has the **Rhine ports** at Basel. From here ships travel down the Rhine as far as **Rotterdam** on the North Sea. On this route, for example, oil, grain and **containers** are transported. That is why the port is important for supplying the whole country.

abschnitte.titel: Chemicals, pharma and an airport in France
abschnitte.text: In Basel large **chemical and pharmaceutical companies** have their seats. They make medicines, for example, and are important employers for the whole region. Many people commute every day from France and Germany to Basel. The airport also crosses the border: the **EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg** lies near Saint-Louis in France, but has a Swiss customs sector of its own.

Basel has a great many museums. On the bank of the Rhine stands the **Museum Tinguely**. It shows the moving machine sculptures of the artist **Jean Tinguely**, opened in 1996 and was designed by Mario Botta. In Riehen near Basel lies the **Fondation Beyeler**. Its building is by the architect Renzo Piano, and it shows works of classical modern art.

Well known is the **Basler Läckerli**, a hard gingerbread biscuit with honey, almonds, candied orange peel and candied lemon peel. Also famous is the **Basler Fasnacht** (Basel Carnival), which parades through the old town with drums and piccolos. Since 2017 it has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.

gewusst: In summer many people in Basel let themselves drift through the city on the Rhine, carrying their clothes in a waterproof bag.
In the middle of Basel there is a point in the Rhine, the Dreiländereck (tri-country corner), where Switzerland, France and Germany meet.

teile.einleitung: Schwyz is the main town of the canton of the same name in central Switzerland. The canton is one of the founding places of the Swiss Confederation and gave its name to the whole country.
wichtigste: The main town of the canton of Schwyz is also called Schwyz.
The town lies at the foot of the two Mythen peaks.
Together with Uri and Unterwalden, Schwyz is one of the three original cantons.
The names “Switzerland” and “Swiss” come from the name Schwyz.
In the Federal Charters Museum in Schwyz lies the Federal Charter of 1291.

abschnitte.titel: A main town by the mountain
abschnitte.text: The main town of the canton of Schwyz has the same name as the canton: **Schwyz**. It lies in a basin between Lake Lauerz and Lake Lucerne. Behind the town rise the two rocky peaks **Grosser Mythen** and **Kleiner Mythen**. In the town centre stand the parish church, the **town hall** and many old mansions. The cantonal government and the cantonal council meet here.

With **Uri** and **Unterwalden**, Schwyz is one of the three **original cantons**. In 1291 they made an alliance, which is called the **Federal Charter**. This valuable document is kept in the **Federal Charters Museum** in Schwyz. There you can look at it together with old flags. The Confederation later grew to include many other places.

Because the people of Schwyz played an important role early on, all the Confederates soon came to be called “**Schwyzers**”. From this came the name **Switzerland** (“Schweiz”). The canton's flag is red with a small white cross in the upper corner. The **Swiss cross** on the national flag goes back to this emblem.

The canton of Schwyz includes well-known places such as **Einsiedeln** with its abbey, **Küssnacht** and **Lachen** on Lake Zurich. In the district of **Ibach** in the municipality of Schwyz, the famous **Swiss army knives** by Victorinox are made. The canton has mountains, lakes and a lot of farming. In winter many people go skiing in the areas around the Mythen.

gewusst: The Grosser Mythen is 1,898 metres high and can be climbed on a steep hiking trail.
In dialect, people also say “Schwyz” for the whole of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach in the canton of Lucerne looks after the birds of Switzerland. It researches how they are doing and works to protect them.
wichtigste: The Swiss Ornithological Institute has its headquarters in Sempach on Lake Sempach.
It was founded in 1924 and is a non-profit foundation.
It researches native birds and bird migration.
It works to protect endangered bird species and their habitats.
A visitor centre shows young and old the world of birds.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Ornithological Institute** counts and observes the birds across the whole of Switzerland. Many volunteers report which species they have seen and where. In this way we know which birds are becoming more common and which are becoming rarer. The results appear, for example, in a **breeding bird atlas**, a large map of birdlife. The institute also researches **bird migration** in autumn and spring.

An important method is **ringing**. A bird is given a light ring with a number on its leg. If it is found later in another place, we know where it flew. This is how it was discovered that many migratory birds from Switzerland spend the winter in Africa. Today tiny devices that record the route are also used.

Many birds need hedges, old trees, wetlands or flower meadows. The institute advises municipalities, farmers and authorities on how to preserve such **habitats**. It also helps with projects for endangered species. In its **care station**, injured birds are looked after and, where possible, released again.

In Sempach there is a modern **visitor centre** run by the institute. There you can learn a lot about birds in an exhibition, listen to their songs and watch them outside in the garden. The centre lies on the shore of **Lake Sempach**. Many school classes visit it.

gewusst: Around 200 different bird species breed in Switzerland.
Some migratory birds from Switzerland fly thousands of kilometres to Africa and back every year.

teile.einleitung: The Zäuerli is a slow natural yodel without words from the Appenzell region. It is especially well known through the Silvesterchläuse in Appenzell Ausserrhoden, who sing it together.
wichtigste: The Zäuerli is a natural yodel without text.
It comes from Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
Several singers sing it together in several voices.
The Silvesterchläuse sing Zäuerli when they go from house to house.
In Appenzell Innerrhoden a similar yodel is called “Rugguusseli”.

abschnitte.text: A **natural yodel** does without text. The singers sing only syllables and sounds and switch quickly between chest voice and head voice. The Zäuerli is slow and solemn and often sounds a little wistful. Usually one person sings the melody first, and the others accompany with deep, long-held notes. In this way a full, **many-voiced** sound comes about.

The Zäuerli is best known at the **Silvesterchlausen** in Appenzell Ausserrhoden, for example in Urnäsch. The Chläuse go from farm to farm on 31 December and on **13 January**, the old New Year's Eve according to the former calendar. They wear large **bells** and rolls of bells. In front of each house they stand in a circle and sing a Zäuerli. Then they shake their bells again and move on.

The Zäuerli belongs to the rich **folk music** of the Appenzell region. It is also sung at work on the alp, in the pub or at festivals. In neighbouring Appenzell Innerrhoden a similar yodel is known, the **Rugguusseli**. Both are passed on from generation to generation.

gewusst: Many Zäuerli are not learned from sheet music but by listening and singing along.
The Silvesterchläuse celebrate New Year's Eve twice: on 31 December and on 13 January.

teile.einleitung: The Black Madonna of Einsiedeln is a famous figure of Mary in the canton of Schwyz. It stands in the Chapel of Grace in the monastery church of Einsiedeln. People have made pilgrimages to it for centuries.
wichtigste: The Black Madonna stands in the monastery church of Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It shows Mary with the infant Jesus.
Its face and hands are dark.
It stands in the Chapel of Grace inside the church.
Einsiedeln is the best-known place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.
The monastery belongs to the Benedictine order.

abschnitte.text: The **Black Madonna** is a carved wooden figure. It shows **Mary** holding the infant Jesus in her arm. The present figure dates from the 15th century. It usually wears a magnificent robe, which is changed according to the church festival. The face and hands are coloured dark.

It is thought that the figure became dark over the years from the **smoke** of many candles and oil lamps. When it was restored later, it was deliberately left dark. People knew and revered it that way. That is why it is still called the Black Madonna.

**Einsiedeln Abbey** was founded in the 10th century. Before that the hermit **Meinrad** is said to have lived here, which is where the name of the place comes from (“Einsiedler” means hermit). The present large **Baroque church** was built in the 18th century. The **Chapel of Grace** with the Madonna stands in the middle of the church.

A **pilgrimage** is a journey to a holy place, often on foot. Every year a great many pilgrims come to Einsiedeln. They pray before the Madonna or light a candle. Einsiedeln also lies on the **Way of St James**, which leads all the way to Santiago de Compostela in Spain.

gewusst: In front of the abbey there is a large square with a fountain of Mary, from which many pilgrims drink.
There are also famous Black Madonnas in other places in Europe, such as Altötting in Bavaria.

teile.einleitung: The Zytturm is a clock tower in the old town of Zug and the landmark of the city. Its roof is covered with blue and white tiles, the colours of the canton of Zug.
wichtigste: The Zytturm stands in the old town of Zug.
It used to belong to the city fortifications.
Its roof shines blue and white like the Zug coat of arms.
On the tower there is an old clock with a special dial.
It is regarded as the landmark of Zug.

abschnitte.titel: A tower of the city wall
abschnitte.text: The Zytturm came about in the **Middle Ages** as part of the first **fortifications** of Zug. It was a gate tower through which you entered the city. Later the tower was raised and got its present appearance. When the city grew larger, it lost its task as a defensive tower.

Especially striking is the pointed **tiled roof**. The tiles are blue and white and form a pattern. Blue and white are the **cantonal colours** of Zug, which also appear in the Zug coat of arms. That is why you recognise the tower from far away.

The name comes from the dialect: **Zyt** means time. So the Zytturm is a time tower. Since the 16th century it has carried a **clock**. Besides the normal dial there is a special dial, which also shows details such as the phase of the moon.

gewusst: Zyt means time in dialect, which is why clock towers in Switzerland are often called Zytturm or Zytglogge.
A passage under the Zytturm still leads into the old town today.

teile.einleitung: Lake Biel lies at the southern foot of the Jura between Biel/Bienne and the canton of Neuchâtel. It is one of the three Jura lakes. On its shores lie vineyards, old little towns and St Peter's Island.
wichtigste: Almost the whole of Lake Biel belongs to the canton of Bern, a small piece in the west to Neuchâtel.
In French it is called Lac de Bienne.
St Peter's Island has been joined to the shore since the first Jura Water Correction.
Jean-Jacques Rousseau lived on the island for a few weeks in 1765.
The Aare flows into the lake through the Hagneck Canal.
A lot of wine grows on the slopes of the north shore.

abschnitte.text: In the south-west of the lake lies **St Peter's Island**. Today it is really a **peninsula**, because a narrow strip of land joins it to the shore at Erlach. This came about as follows: during the **first Jura Water Correction** in the 19th century the lake level was lowered by around 2.5 metres. As a result the strip of land emerged. In **1765** the philosopher **Jean-Jacques Rousseau** lived on the island for a few weeks. He later wrote that he had been very happy there.

In the past there were often **floods** and marshy areas in the Seeland. So the **Aare** was diverted: since the Jura Water Correction it has flowed through the **Hagneck Canal** into Lake Biel. In the lake it deposits its mud, and the water flows out again at Nidau. In this way the Seeland became drier and more fertile.

On the sunny **Jura slopes** of the north shore many **vines** grow. Mainly **white wine** is grown there. The wine village of **Ligerz** lies in the middle of the vineyards and has a museum about wine-growing. On the south-west shore lies the little town of **Erlach** at the foot of the Jolimont, with a castle above the small old town.

Almost the whole of Lake Biel belongs to the **canton of Bern**. Only a small piece in the west belongs to **Neuchâtel**. At the north-eastern end lies **Biel/Bienne**, the largest bilingual city in Switzerland. That is why the lake also has two names: **Bielersee** and **Lac de Bienne**. With Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Murten it forms the three **Jura lakes**, which are joined by canals.

gewusst: In summer passenger boats run from Lake Biel through the Zihl Canal as far as Lake Neuchâtel.
On Lake Biel remains of Stone Age pile dwellings were found, which belong to the UNESCO World Heritage.

teile.einleitung: The Bernina Railway links St Moritz in the Engadine with Tirano in Italy. It runs over the Bernina Pass and is the highest railway crossing of the Alps. Since 2008, together with the Albula Railway, it has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: The Bernina Railway has run along the whole route since 1910.
It crosses the Alps at over 2,200 metres above sea level.
The terminus in Italy is Tirano in the Valtellina.
It runs on 1,000 volts direct current.
The panoramic Bernina Express runs from Chur or St Moritz to Tirano.
Poschiavo is the main town of the Val Poschiavo.

abschnitte.text: The Bernina Railway was opened bit by bit from **1908**. Since **5 July 1910** it has run continuously from St Moritz to Tirano. Today it belongs to the **Rhaetian Railway**. Together with the Albula Railway, it has been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage** since 2008. The railway runs on narrow gauge, so the rails lie closer together than on normal railways.

At the **Bernina Pass** the railway runs at over 2,200 metres above sea level. No other railway crosses the Alps so high. It passes the Lago Bianco and has a view of glaciers. On the southern side it runs through the Italian-speaking **Val Poschiavo** with the main town **Poschiavo**. There the railway has a large station and a workshop.

The railway is very steep, without any cogwheel at all. It runs on **1,000 volts direct current**. The rest of the Rhaetian Railway network, by contrast, uses **alternating current**. That is why the Bernina Railway needs vehicles of its own or ones that can run on both kinds of current.

In **Tirano** in the Valtellina the line ends. There the narrow-gauge railway meets the Italian railway. Shortly before the station the train runs like a **tram** right across a street and a square, past a pilgrimage church. The cars then have to wait.

The **Bernina Express** is a panoramic train with large windows. It runs from **Chur** or **St Moritz** over the Bernina Pass to Tirano. From Tirano the **Bernina Express Bus** runs along Lake Como to **Lugano**. In this way you can make a round trip through Graubünden and Ticino.

gewusst: At Brusio the railway goes once round in a circle on a round viaduct in order to lose height.
The Bernina Railway is among the steepest railways in the world that run without a cogwheel.

teile.einleitung: The Stadtlounge (City Lounge) is a special square in the city of St Gallen. It is covered in a red surface and looks like a giant living room in the open air.
wichtigste: The Stadtlounge lies in the Bleicheli district of the city of St Gallen.
The ground, benches and even a table are covered in red plastic.
The artist Pipilotti Rist designed it together with the architect Carlos Martinez.
The Stadtlounge opened in 2005.
The square is meant to feel like a living room for everyone.

abschnitte.text: The **Stadtlounge** is a square in the **Bleicheli district** of St Gallen. The ground is covered with a soft **red surface** made of plastic. The red carpet also stretches over benches and over a large **table**. So the square looks like a **living room** under the open sky. That is why many people also call it the “red square”.

The Stadtlounge was designed by the artist **Pipilotti Rist** and the architect **Carlos Martinez**. Pipilotti Rist grew up in the Rhine Valley in the canton of St Gallen and is internationally known, above all for her video art. Above the square hang large, round **lights** that look like floating lamps. They bathe the square in soft light in the evening. The Stadtlounge opened in **2005**.

The Stadtlounge is meant to be a place to **linger**. You can sit down, take a break or meet friends. Around the square stand office buildings, shops and restaurants. For tourists the Stadtlounge is a popular photo spot. It shows how art can change a part of a city.

gewusst: For the Stadtlounge a whole street space was designed like an indoor room.
The soft surface feels quite different from ordinary asphalt.

teile.einleitung: The Simplon Tunnel is a railway tunnel under the Simplon. Since 1906 it has linked the Valais with Italy, and when it opened it was the longest tunnel in the world.
wichtigste: The Simplon Tunnel links Brig in the Valais with Iselle in Italy.
It opened in 1906.
It is almost 20 kilometres long.
When it opened it was the longest tunnel in the world.
It consists of two tubes; the second was finished in 1921.

abschnitte.text: The **Simplon Tunnel** runs under the mountains by the **Simplon Pass**. It begins in **Brig** in the canton of the **Valais** and ends in **Iselle** in **Italy**. The tunnel is just under **20 kilometres** long. It is part of an important railway line that links northern Europe with Milan by way of Switzerland. Trains take about a quarter of an hour to pass through.

Construction began in **1898** from both sides at the same time. The workers struggled with great **heat** in the mountain and with water breaking in. To cool the tunnel, cold water was channelled in. Many workers came from Italy. People also lost their lives in the heavy work.

When it opened in **1906**, the Simplon Tunnel was the **longest tunnel in the world**. It held this record for several decades. Next to the first tube a second was built, which was finished in **1921**. In this way a track in each tube can carry trains in one direction. The border between Switzerland and Italy runs right through the middle of the tunnel.

A road also runs over the **Simplon Pass**, built as long ago as the time of **Napoleon**. In winter the journey there can be difficult. So **car trains** also run through the Simplon Tunnel between Brig and Iselle. You drive your car onto a railway wagon and are pulled through the mountain.

gewusst: Inside the Simplon Tunnel it became so hot during construction that work was only possible with cooling.
The famous Simplon-Orient-Express also used to run through the Simplon Tunnel.

teile.einleitung: Lake Brienz lies in the Bernese Oberland between Brienz and Interlaken. Its water often shines turquoise green and is very clean. It is the deepest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Brienz is about 14 km long and just under 3 km wide.
It is up to 260 m deep.
It lies at about 564 m above sea level, somewhat higher than Lake Thun.
Glacier streams give it its turquoise-green colour.
On the south shore the Giessbach Falls plunge into the lake in 14 steps.
Brienz is famous for wood carving.

abschnitte.text: Lake Brienz is about **14 kilometres** long and just under 3 kilometres wide. At its deepest point it measures around **260 metres**. That makes it the deepest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland. Lake Thun and Lake Lucerne are only a good 210 metres deep. Its steep shores also fall away steeply under the water.

The water often has a **turquoise-green** colour. Glacier streams bring fine **rock dust** into the lake, which colours the light in this way. Lake Brienz has few **nutrients** in the water and is regarded as one of the cleanest lakes in Switzerland. From the east the Aare flows into the lake. The **Lütschine** brings the water from the valleys of Lauterbrunnen and Grindelwald and flows in at Bönigen.

abschnitte.titel: From Lake Brienz to Lake Thun
abschnitte.text: Lake Brienz lies at about **564 m above sea level** and so a few metres higher than **Lake Thun**. That is why the water flows through the Aare at **Interlaken** from Lake Brienz into Lake Thun. The name Interlaken means “between the lakes”.

In the village of **Brienz** there have long been many **wood carvers**. There is also a school for **wood sculpture** there. From Brienz the **Brienz Rothorn Railway** runs with steam locomotives up the **Brienzer Rothorn**. From the top you can see far over the lake and the mountains.
On the south shore the **Giessbach Falls** plunge in **14 steps** right down into the lake. Beside them stands an old **grand hotel**. A historic funicular goes up from the boat landing.

gewusst: The Brienz Rothorn Railway is a rack railway that to this day runs largely on steam.
In Lake Brienz live fish such as whitefish, which are caught by professional fishermen.

teile.einleitung: The Stoosbahn is a funicular in the canton of Schwyz. It runs from Schwyz up to the car-free mountain village of Stoos and is considered the steepest funicular in the world.
wichtigste: The Stoosbahn opened in December 2017.
It links the valley station Schlattli near Schwyz with the village of Stoos.
Its steepest gradient is 110 per cent.
The cabins are round like barrels and rotate during the journey.
This way passengers always stand upright, however steep the track is.
It replaced an older funicular from 1933.

abschnitte.text: A **funicular** runs on rails along the ground. A strong **steel cable** pulls the cars up the mountain. Often two cars are attached to the same cable: when one goes up, the other comes down. In this way they balance each other and save energy.

A gradient of **100 per cent** means that for every metre of track you rise one metre. That corresponds to an angle of 45 degrees. At its steepest point the Stoosbahn is even steeper, namely **110 per cent**. That is why it is considered the **steepest funicular in the world**. Along the route it also passes through tunnels and over bridges.

The cars consist of several round cabins that look like **drums**. Because the gradient changes along the way, the cabins rotate slowly. This keeps the floor level at all times. So passengers do not have to hold on to a sloping wall.

**Stoos** lies on a sunny terrace high above the basin of Schwyz. The village is **car-free** and can only be reached by cable railways. In winter many people come to ski, in summer to walk. Well known is the ridge walk from the Klingenstock to the Fronalpstock with a view of Lake Lucerne.

gewusst: The building work took many years because the route is so steep and hard to reach.
There are no cars on Stoos, so it is especially quiet there.

teile.einleitung: Lake Uri is the southernmost arm of Lake Lucerne and lies in the canton of Uri. It is surrounded by steep rock walls and is one of the places closely linked with the founding story of Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Uri is the southernmost part of Lake Lucerne.
It stretches from Brunnen to Flüelen.
At Flüelen the Reuss flows into the lake.
On the western shore lies the Rütli meadow.
On the eastern shore the Axenstrasse runs along the cliffs.
The hiking trail “Swiss Path” runs around the lake.

abschnitte.text: Lake Uri is the southernmost arm of **Lake Lucerne**. It lies between Brunnen in the canton of Schwyz and **Flüelen** in the canton of Uri. On both sides steep rock walls and high mountains rise straight out of the water. At Flüelen the **Reuss** flows into the lake. That is why Lake Uri looks almost like a fjord.

On the western shore lies the **Rütli meadow**. According to tradition, representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden met there for the Rütli Oath. On the eastern shore stands **Tell's Chapel** at the Tellsplatte. It recalls the legend of William Tell, who is said to have leapt here from the boat of his enemies. Both places are easy to reach by boat.

On the eastern shore the **Axenstrasse** runs from Brunnen to Flüelen. It is partly cut into the rock and runs through tunnels and galleries. The hiking trail **“Swiss Path”** runs around Lake Uri. It was opened in 1991 for the 700th anniversary of the Confederation. Each canton has a stretch of path of its own.

The **foehn**, a warm, strong downslope wind from the south, often blows across Lake Uri. Then the lake can become very choppy. For sailors and windsurfers that is exciting, but for small boats it is dangerous. In strong foehn, storm lights on the shore warn people on the water.

gewusst: The Rütli meadow was bought in 1859 with donations from all over Switzerland and then given to the Confederation.
On the Swiss Path the stretches are as long as the canton has inhabitants: the more inhabitants, the longer the stretch.

teile.einleitung: A mountain village lies high in the mountains, often in a side valley or on a steep slope. In Switzerland there are many such villages, from famous holiday resorts to small hamlets. Life there is lovely, but also shaped by nature.
wichtigste: Juf in the Avers Valley is regarded as the highest settlement in Switzerland inhabited all year round.
Zermatt at the foot of the Matterhorn is car-free.
In the Middle Ages the Walser founded many high-lying settlements.
Protection forests protect mountain villages from avalanches and rockfall.
Many young people move from mountain villages to the valley or to cities.
Rockslides and glacier collapses can threaten villages, as in Bondo and Blatten.

abschnitte.text: The village of **Juf** in the Avers Valley in Graubünden lies at 2,126 metres above sea level. It is regarded as the highest settlement in Switzerland that is inhabited all year round. Many high-lying settlements were founded in the Middle Ages by the **Walser**. They migrated from the Upper Valais and settled in Graubünden and other Alpine valleys.

In the course of the year many mountain farmers move higher up with their cattle. Between the farm in the valley and the alp lies the **Maiensäss**, a group of huts at middle height. There the cattle graze in spring and autumn. In summer they then go to the **alp**.

**Zermatt** at the foot of the Matterhorn is car-free: visitors arrive by train, and in the village electric taxis run. The Engadine village of **Guarda** is known through the children's book “Schellen-Ursli” (“Ursli and his bell”). The book is by Selina Chönz, the pictures by Alois Carigiet. Typical of Guarda are the painted **Engadine houses**.

Mountain villages are exposed to dangers such as **avalanches**, rockfall and debris flows. A **protection forest** above the village must not be felled because it protects the village. Even so, disasters happen. In 2017, after a rockslide at the Piz Cengalo, debris flows reached the village of **Bondo** in the Bergell. In May 2025 the Birch Glacier broke off and buried **Blatten** in the Lötschental. The village had been evacuated beforehand.

In many mountain villages jobs are lacking, and the distances are long. That is why many young people move to the valley or to the cities. This is called **depopulation** (out-migration). As a result some villages lose inhabitants. Tourism, good transport links and working over the internet can help people to stay.

gewusst: Many mountain villages have their own building styles, in the Engadine for example thick walls and small windows against the cold.
In Zermatt even the luggage carts and delivery vans are mostly electric.

teile.einleitung: In August 2005 it rained very heavily for days on the northern slope of the Alps. Rivers and lakes burst their banks, and many places were flooded. It was one of the most expensive natural events in the history of Switzerland.
wichtigste: A Vb weather pattern brought extreme, lasting rain in August 2005.
The damage in Switzerland came to around 3 billion francs.
Engelberg could only be reached by helicopter.
Lake Lucerne rose around two metres above its normal level.
Klosters, Interlaken and the Muotathal were also badly affected.
Afterwards the Confederation improved warnings about natural hazards with the OWARNA project.

abschnitte.text: The cause was a **Vb weather pattern** (pronounced “five b”). A low-pressure area moved north-east across the **Adriatic**. It carried moist air from the Mediterranean in an arc around the Alps. From the north this air was pushed against the mountains, rose and rained out. This is how a great deal of rain fell on the **northern slope of the Alps** for days.

Many rivers swelled enormously. The **Engelberger Aa** destroyed the road and the railway line, and **Engelberg** could only be reached by helicopter. At Brunnen the **Muota** carried around 21 times as much water as normal. In the Prättigau the Landquart burst its banks, and in **Klosters** the water stood up to three metres high in places.

The lakes also rose sharply. **Lake Lucerne** stood around two metres above its normal level, and in **Lucerne** parts of the old town were under water. **Lake Thun** exceeded its damage limit by almost a metre. In **Interlaken**, between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz, low-lying districts were flooded.

The damage was first estimated at 2.5 billion and later at around **3 billion francs**. A large part concerned **buildings** and **infrastructure** such as roads, bridges and railway lines. Sadly, people also lost their lives. In Engelberg rail traffic stopped until a new bridge opened in December.

After the flood the Confederation started the **OWARNA** project. This stands for optimising warning and alerting in the case of natural hazards. Among other things, it led to a joint **natural hazards platform** of the Confederation. In addition, many dams and protective structures were strengthened.

gewusst: The “V” in Vb is a Roman five: it refers to an old classification of the tracks of low-pressure areas.
In 2005 the Muota carried around 21 times as much water as usual at Brunnen.

teile.einleitung: The Titlis Rotair is an aerial cable car near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. What makes it special: the cabin turns completely around once during the ride.
wichtigste: The Rotair runs from Stand to the top station on the Klein Titlis.
