During the ride the cabin turns once through 360 degrees.
It opened in 1992.
It was the first rotating aerial cable car in the world.
On the way it glides over the Titlis glacier.

abschnitte.text: In the Rotair you stand on a **rotating floor**. During the ride it turns slowly all the way round, that is, through **360 degrees**. So nobody has to fight for the best place at the window. Every passenger sees in turn the rock walls, the glacier and the valley of Engelberg.

The Rotair is the last stage on the way from **Engelberg** to the Titlis. It starts at the **Stand** station and runs up to the top station on the **Klein Titlis**, at over 3,000 metres. On the way it glides over the **glacier** and over deep crevasses in the ice. The ride lasts only a few minutes.

When the Rotair opened in **1992**, it was the **first rotating aerial cable car in the world**. Later, similar rotating cable cars were also built in other places. The Rotair attracts many guests from all over the world.

gewusst: The name Rotair is made up of “rotation” and “air”.
Many people have room in the cabin at the same time.

teile.einleitung: The World Economic Forum, WEF for short, is a foundation with its seat near Geneva. It is best known for its annual meeting, which takes place every January in Davos in the canton of Graubünden.
wichtigste: The World Economic Forum is abbreviated WEF.
It was founded in 1971 by Klaus Schwab.
Its seat is in Cologny near Geneva.
The annual meeting mostly takes place in January in Davos.
Politicians and business leaders from all over the world meet there.
During the meeting Davos is guarded particularly closely.

abschnitte.text: The **World Economic Forum** is a **foundation**. It was founded in **1971** by the business professor **Klaus Schwab**. Its seat is in **Cologny** on Lake Geneva. The WEF wants to bring together people from **politics**, **business**, **science** and society so that they can talk about important questions.

Every year in **January** thousands of guests come together in **Davos**. Among them are heads of government, bosses of large companies and experts. They discuss, for example, **climate**, **health**, **technology** and the **world economy**. Many talks also take place behind closed doors.

Because so many important guests come, Davos is well **guarded** during the meeting. The **police** and the **Swiss Army** help with this. The airspace above Davos is monitored, and some roads are closed. For the village this means a great deal of effort every year.

Supporters say that the WEF is an important place where people from all over the world **talk to one another**. Critics think that **rich and powerful** people have too much influence there. Again and again there are **demonstrations** against the meeting. So the WEF is often discussed in Switzerland, and opinions differ.

gewusst: Davos lies at over 1,500 metres and is one of the highest towns in Europe.
During the WEF many guests travel to Davos by helicopter or by train.

teile.einleitung: The Zibelemärit is a big market in the old town of Bern. It takes place every year on the fourth Monday in November. What is sold is mainly onions, which are called “Zibele” in Bernese German.
wichtigste: The Zibelemärit takes place in Bern.
It is always on the fourth Monday in November.
“Zibele” is Bernese German for onions.
Farmers sell onions, often plaited into elaborate braids.
There are onion tarts, cheese tarts and hot drinks.
Many people throw confetti and hit each other with small plastic hammers.

abschnitte.text: At the **Zibelemärit** hundreds of **market stalls** stand in the **old town of Bern**. Farmers from the surrounding area sell **onions** and **garlic** there. Many onions are plaited into lovely **braids** or tied into wreaths. Other things such as vegetables, pottery and toys are also offered.

The market starts **very early in the morning**, while it is still dark. Many people come even before sunrise. Then it is cold, and people warm themselves with **mulled wine**, tea or **coffee**. To eat there are **onion tarts**, **cheese tarts** and onion soup.

At the Zibelemärit things are lively. Children and young people throw **confetti** into the crowd. Many carry small **plastic hammers** with which they playfully tap others on the head. In the afternoon the whole old town is colourful with confetti. For many people in Bern the day is a little **folk festival**.

How the Zibelemärit began is not known exactly. A **legend** tells that after a great **fire** the city received help from Fribourg and, as thanks, allowed a market. But this is not proved. What is certain is that the market already existed in the **19th century**. It is one of the best-known markets in Switzerland.

gewusst: Many tonnes of onions are sold at the Zibelemärit every year.
Afterwards many people decorate their kitchen with the onion braids.

teile.einleitung: The Sitter is a river in eastern Switzerland. It rises in the Alpstein, flows through the village of Appenzell and past St Gallen, and finally joins the Thur.
wichtigste: The Sitter rises in the Alpstein.
It flows through the village of Appenzell.
Then it flows past the town of St Gallen to the west.
At Bischofszell it joins the Thur.
Many high bridges cross the Sitter.

abschnitte.text: The **Sitter** begins in the **Alpstein**, the mountain range around the **Säntis**. Several mountain streams come together there, including water from the area of the **Seealpsee**. At **Weissbad** the streams unite to form the Sitter. Then the river flows through the village of **Appenzell**, the main town of Appenzell Innerrhoden.

After Appenzell the Sitter has cut deep into the terrain. This has created narrow, steep valleys called **Tobel** (ravines). To cross them, many high **bridges** were built. Well known are the bridges over the **Sittertobel** near St Gallen, which carry roads and railway lines. On a bridge trail you can visit many of them on foot.

West of the town of **St Gallen** the Sitter flows on to the north. The **Urnäsch**, a river from the Appenzell Hinterland, also flows into it. At **Bischofszell** in the canton of Thurgau the Sitter flows into the **Thur**. The Thur in turn flows into the **Rhine**. In this way the water from the Alpstein finally reaches the North Sea.

gewusst: Around St Gallen there are so many bridges that a hiking trail of its own leads to them.
On hot summer days many people swim in the Sitter.

t1gssnpe.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Uri

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Uri is one of the best known in Switzerland. It shows a black bull's head on a yellow ground, which is called the Uristier (“bull of Uri”). Uri is one of the three founding cantons of the Confederation.
wichtigste: The Uri coat of arms is yellow, that is, golden.
In the middle you can see a black bull's head.
The bull has a red tongue and a red nose ring.
This animal is called the Uristier.
Together with Schwyz and Unterwalden, Uri is one of the founding cantons of 1291.
The main town of the canton of Uri is Altdorf.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: The background of the coat of arms is **yellow**. On it a **black bull's head** looks straight ahead. It has a **red tongue** and a **red ring** through its nose. In the past strong bulls were led by such a nose ring. The coat of arms is very simple and can therefore be recognised well from far away.

The bull has been the sign of Uri since the Middle Ages. It is often said that the name **Uri** recalls the **aurochs** (in German “Ur”), a wild kind of cattle. Whether that is true is not certain. What is certain is that the bull's head already appears on very old **seals** of the land of Uri.

In the past the people of Uri went into battle with a large **war horn**. Like the heraldic animal, it was called the “Bull of Uri”. Its loud note was meant to give courage and to call their own people together. In pictures from old **chronicles** too you can see men of Uri with the bull coat of arms on their banners.

Uri lies in the valley of the **Reuss** between **Lake Uri** and the **Gotthard**. According to tradition, in **1291** Uri made an alliance with Schwyz and Unterwalden. From it the Confederation later grew. You can see the coat of arms on the cantonal flag and on car number plates with the letters **UR**.

gewusst: In Altdorf stands the famous Tell Monument, because William Tell is regarded as the legendary hero of Uri.
The bull of Uri is also the mascot of many clubs and sports teams in Uri.

teile.einleitung: Toblerone is a triangular chocolate that was invented in Bern in 1908. It is known all over the world, and many people think of mountain peaks when they see its shape.
wichtigste: Toblerone was invented in Bern in 1908.
Its inventors were Theodor Tobler and Emil Baumann.
The chocolate contains honey and almond nougat.
The name combines “Tobler” with “torrone”, an Italian nougat.
The shape is made up of many small triangles.
A bear is hidden in the logo, the heraldic animal of Bern.

abschnitte.text: **Theodor Tobler** ran a chocolate factory in Bern. Together with his cousin **Emil Baumann** he developed a new chocolate in **1908**. It contained **honey** and **almond nougat**. The new kind was given the name **Toblerone**, from “Tobler” and the Italian word **“torrone”** for nougat.

Toblerone is shaped in a row of **triangles** and comes in a triangular pack. Many people think of the **Swiss mountains** when they see it. For a long time the **Matterhorn** was shown on the pack. How exactly the shape came about is told in different ways.

A **bear** is hidden in the Toblerone logo. You can see it if you look closely at the mountain shape in the picture. The bear is the **heraldic animal** of the city of Bern. In this way the pack recalls the place where the chocolate was invented.

Today Toblerone is sold in over a hundred countries, especially often at **airports**. For many years the brand has belonged to large international food companies. In recent years part of the production has been moved abroad. Because the chocolate therefore no longer comes entirely from Switzerland, the Matterhorn disappeared from the pack from 2023.

gewusst: Toblerone is still made in Bern today.
Toblerone comes in many sizes, from very small to very large bars.

teile.einleitung: The Thur is a river in eastern Switzerland. It rises in the Toggenburg, flows through the cantons of St Gallen, Thurgau and Zurich and joins the Rhine. The canton of Thurgau is named after it.
wichtigste: The Thur rises in the uppermost Toggenburg in the canton of St Gallen.
It flows through St Gallen, Thurgau and Zurich.
It flows into the Rhine.
The canton of Thurgau takes its name from the Thur.
The Thur does not flow through a large lake, so its water level can rise quickly.

abschnitte.text: The Thur begins in the mountains near the **Säntis** in the upper **Toggenburg**. It flows north through the whole valley. Then it turns west and crosses the **canton of Thurgau**. It flows past places such as **Bischofszell** and **Weinfelden**. In the Zurich Weinland it finally joins the **Rhine**.

The name **Thurgau** means roughly “area on the Thur”. A **Gau** was formerly a word for a landscape or region. The river flows right across the canton. That is why it is still important for Thurgau today. The main town of the canton is **Frauenfeld**.

Many large Swiss rivers flow through a **lake**. The lake takes in a lot of water during heavy rain. The Thur has no such lake. So after thunderstorms or during the snowmelt its water often rises very **quickly**. In the past there were therefore repeated **floods**. Today embankments and wider river beds protect the villages.

In many places the Thur was once forced into a straight bed. Today in some places it is given **more room** again. This is called **renaturation**. It creates gravel banks, floodplains and habitats for fish, birds and plants. You can also walk and cycle well along the bank.

gewusst: In the Toggenburg, near Unterwasser, there are the Thur waterfalls.
At Bischofszell the Sitter flows into the Thur.

teile.einleitung: The Council of States is one of the two chambers of the Swiss Parliament. The cantons are represented in it. Together with the National Council it forms the Federal Assembly.
wichtigste: The Council of States has 46 members.
20 cantons elect two members each.
Six cantons with half a cantonal vote elect one member each, for example Nidwalden.
The Council of States represents the cantons, the National Council the people.
Both chambers have equal say.
The members are elected every four years.

abschnitte.text: The Swiss Parliament is called the **Federal Assembly**. It consists of the **National Council** with 200 members and the **Council of States** with 46 members. In the National Council larger cantons get more seats. In the Council of States, however, every canton counts for roughly the same. In this way small cantons also have a strong voice. This arrangement has existed since the Federal Constitution of 1848.

Most cantons send **two members** to the Council of States. Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden have **one seat** each. They used to be called **half-cantons**; today people speak of cantons with half a cantonal vote. So Zurich, with a great many inhabitants, has the same number of seats as the small canton of Uri.

How the members of the Council of States are elected is decided by each canton itself. In most cantons the person who gets the most votes wins. This is called the **majority system**. Some cantons, such as Jura and Neuchâtel, elect by a different procedure. Elections are held every four years, usually together with the National Council.

abschnitte.titel: What the Council of States does
abschnitte.text: The Council of States debates **laws** and the federal budget. A new law only takes effect if **both chambers** agree. If they disagree, the matter goes back and forth between them. Together the National Council and Council of States also elect the members of the **Federal Council**. The Council of States meets in the Federal Palace in Bern.

gewusst: The Council of States is often called the “small chamber” and the National Council the “large chamber”.
When the Parliament was set up in 1848, the US Senate served as a model.

teile.einleitung: Sion, called Sitten in German, is the main town of the canton of the Valais. The old town in the Rhône valley is known for its two castle hills and its long history.
wichtigste: Sion (German: Sitten) is the main town of the Valais.
The town lies in the Rhône valley.
Above the old town stand the two hills of Valère and Tourbillon.
On Valère stands a church with one of the oldest playable organs in the world.
In Sion people mainly speak French.
Sion has been the seat of a bishop for many centuries.

abschnitte.text: **Sion** is the main town of the canton of the **Valais**. In German the town is called **Sitten**. It lies in the middle of the broad valley of the **Rhône**. The Valais government and the cantonal parliament, the **Grand Council**, work here. Most people in Sion speak **French**, because the town lies in the French-speaking part of the canton.

Two rocky hills rise above the old town. On one stands the **Basilica of Valère**, a fortified church from the Middle Ages. On the other lie the ruins of **Tourbillon Castle**. The two hills are the landmark of Sion. From the top you have a wide view over the Rhône valley and the vineyards.

In the Basilica of Valère there is a special **organ**. It dates from the Middle Ages and is regarded as one of the **oldest playable organs in the world**. Concerts take place there every summer. Part of the **Valais History Museum** is also housed in the building.

Sion is one of the oldest towns in Switzerland. People were already living here in Roman times. Since the early Middle Ages Sion has been the seat of the **bishop** of the Valais. Around the town, many **vines** grow on sunny slopes. The Valais is the biggest wine-growing canton in Switzerland.

gewusst: The Valais is one of the sunniest regions of Switzerland, which is why apricots also thrive there.
The football club FC Sion has won the Swiss Cup very many times.

teile.einleitung: The Bise is a cold, dry wind from the north-east. It blows across the Central Plateau between the Jura and the Alps. On Lake Geneva it is often strongest.
wichtigste: The Bise blows from the north-east to the east.
It arises with high pressure in the north and low pressure in the Mediterranean region.
The Jura and the Alps act like a funnel and speed up the wind.
On Lake Geneva the Bise is usually strongest.
In winter it feels especially cold.
With an overcast sky it is called the Black Bise.

abschnitte.titel: Where does the Bise come from?
abschnitte.text: The Bise arises in a particular **weather pattern**. If a **high** lies over northern Europe and a **low** over the Mediterranean region, air flows into Switzerland from the north-east. Air always flows from high to low pressure. The Bise brings **continental air** from the north-east of Europe. This air is mostly dry.

abschnitte.titel: The funnel between the Jura and the Alps
abschnitte.text: The **Central Plateau** lies between the **Jura** and the **Alps**. Towards the south-west the two mountain ranges move closer and closer together. The air is thereby squeezed and speeded up, like water in a **nozzle**. That is why the Bise is usually strongest on **Lake Geneva**. In French too it is called “la bise”.

In winter the air of the Bise is **cold and dry**. The wind makes it feel even colder than the thermometer shows. Usually it is **sunny** with a Bise. With the **Black Bise**, by contrast, the sky is overcast, often with **high fog**. In summer the Bise often brings fine but cooler weather.

In **February 2012** a very strong Bise blew on Lake Geneva in great cold. In **Versoix** it whipped lake water onto the shore, trees and parked cars. The water froze at once into **thick layers of ice**. The iced-over cars and benches looked like sculptures and were photographed all over the world.

gewusst: The Mistral is a different wind: it blows in the Rhône Valley in southern France.
In a strong Bise there are sometimes high waves on Lake Geneva like on the sea.

t1kqys5o.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Geneva

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Geneva shows half a black eagle on a yellow ground on the left and a golden key on a red ground on the right. Both signs tell of the city's history.
wichtigste: The Geneva coat of arms is divided vertically.
On the left is half a black eagle on yellow.
On the right is a golden key on red.
The eagle recalls the Holy Roman Empire.
The key recalls Saint Peter and the bishop.
The motto “Post tenebras lux” often stands above the coat of arms.

abschnitte.text: The **Geneva coat of arms** is divided vertically into two halves. On the left side is **half a black eagle** on a **yellow** ground. The eagle wears a crown. On the right side stands a **golden key** on a **red** ground. Together they look as if the eagle were holding the key.

The **eagle** comes from the coat of arms of the **Holy Roman Empire**. In the Middle Ages Geneva belonged to this empire. The **key** is the sign of **Saint Peter**, to whom the cathedral of Geneva is dedicated. It also recalls the bishops who once ruled over the city.

Above the coat of arms often stands the Latin motto **“Post tenebras lux”**. It means “After darkness, light”. The motto became important at the time of the **Reformation**, when **John Calvin** worked in Geneva. Geneva only joined the Confederation in **1815**.

gewusst: The Geneva eagle is cut in half because it has to share the coat of arms with the key.
Because of the Reformation, Geneva is sometimes called the “Protestant Rome”.

teile.einleitung: The Federal Palace in Bern is the seat of Parliament and the Federal Council. Here the laws of Switzerland are discussed and passed. The magnificent building with its green dome stands high above the Aare.
wichtigste: The parliament building was built from 1894 to 1902 and inaugurated in 1902.
The National Council and the Council of States meet in two different chambers.
In the Dome Hall stands a statue of the three Confederates.
In the glass dome you can see the coats of arms of the cantons.
On the Bundesplatz 26 water jets spray, one for each canton.
Right next to it stands the Swiss National Bank.

abschnitte.text: The **parliament building** was built from **1894 to 1902** and ceremonially opened in **1902**. Here the **National Council** and the **Council of States** meet. Together they form Parliament, the **Federal Assembly**. Each council has its own chamber. The **Federal Council**, the government of Switzerland, also has its rooms in the Federal Palace.

Under the large dome lies the **Dome Hall**. There stands a large statue of the **three Confederates**. It recalls the **Rütli Oath** and the founding of the Confederation. Above, in the **glass dome**, shine colourful **coats of arms of the cantons**. In the middle is the Swiss coat of arms.

In front of the Federal Palace lies the **Bundesplatz** (Federal Square). Out of the ground spray **26 jets of water**, one jet for each canton. Children like to play in them in summer. Every **Tuesday and Saturday** a **market** takes place here, with vegetables, fruit and flowers. On the Bundesplatz also stands the large building of the **Swiss National Bank**. Among other things, it looks after the money of Switzerland, the franc.

The Federal Palace stands on a hill above the **Aare**. From the **Bundesterrasse** behind the building you look down on the river. In clear weather you can even see the mountains of the Bernese Oberland in the distance. A small funicular, the Marzilibähnli, links the terrace with the Marzili district on the river.

gewusst: You can visit the Federal Palace on free guided tours when Parliament is not sitting.
Parliament normally sits four times a year for three weeks, which is called a session.

teile.einleitung: Rock crystal is clear, transparent quartz. In the Swiss Alps especially beautiful and large crystals are found. The people who search for them are called Strahler (crystal hunters).
wichtigste: Rock crystal is colourless quartz with the formula SiO2.
On the Mohs scale quartz has a hardness of 7.
Alpine crystals grow in clefts in granite and gneiss.
Smoky quartz turns brown to black through natural radiation in the rock.
Crystal seekers are called Strahler in Switzerland.
In 2005 a famous giant crystal cleft was opened on the Planggenstock in the canton of Uri.

abschnitte.text: Rock crystal is **quartz** in its pure, colourless form. Quartz consists of silicon and oxygen, and the chemical formula is **SiO2**. Its crystals have six sides and a point. On the **Mohs scale**, which measures the hardness of minerals, quartz has a hardness of **7**. It scratches glass and steel, but is scratched by topaz and corundum.

When the Alps were forming, cracks opened in the rock, so-called **tension clefts**. Through these clefts in the **granite** and **gneiss**, hot, mineral-rich solutions flowed. As they slowly cooled, quartz separated out. Over a very long time the crystals grew from it.

Not every quartz is clear. **Smoky quartz** is brown to black. Its colour comes from **natural radioactive radiation** from the surrounding granite. It changes the crystal lattice, in which aluminium atoms are built in. Almost black, opaque smoky quartz is called **morion**. Other kinds of quartz are yellow citrine, violet amethyst and rose quartz.

In Switzerland crystal seekers are called **Strahler**. The name comes from the old word “Strahl” for rock crystal. Strahler climb in the mountains to rock clefts and carefully take the crystals out. In many cantons you need a permit for this.

In September **2005** the Strahler Franz von Arx and Paul von Känel opened a huge cleft on the **Planggenstock** above the Göscheneralp in the canton of Uri. It lies at around 2,600 metres above sea level in the granite of the **Aar Massif**. In summer 2006 they recovered the crystals. The largest group weighs around **300 kilograms**, and its middle crystal is 107 cm long. Today it stands in the **Natural History Museum of Bern**.

gewusst: In total the Natural History Museum of Bern shows almost 2 tonnes of rock crystal from the Planggenstock.
In the past people believed that rock crystal was ice that had frozen so hard that it would never melt again.

teile.einleitung: On 18 October 1356 a mighty earthquake shook the city of Basel. It is the strongest known earthquake in central Europe north of the Alps. Afterwards a great fire destroyed large parts of the city.
wichtigste: The Basel earthquake happened on 18 October 1356, St Luke's Day.
Experts estimate its magnitude at about 6 to 7.
The choir of Basel Minster collapsed.
After the quake a great fire broke out that is said to have lasted several days.
Around Basel about 40 castles were damaged or destroyed.
Many people had already left the city after a first foreshock.

abschnitte.text: On the afternoon of **18 October 1356** there was a first tremor. Many people were frightened and left the city. In the night the heaviest tremors followed. Because many were already outside, probably fewer people died than you would expect from such a strong quake. Experts suspect the source a few kilometres **south of Basel**, roughly under Reinach BL.

At that time there were no measuring instruments yet. Today experts estimate the strength from the reports and the damage. The **magnitude** was probably around **6 to 7**. Magnitude is a measure of how much energy an earthquake releases. It is the strongest known quake in central Europe north of the Alps.

Many houses and churches were damaged. At the **Minster** the choir collapsed. Even worse was the fire afterwards: hearth fires and lamps set the **timber houses** alight. The **great fire** is said to have raged for several days. In the surrounding countryside too there was great damage: about **40 castles** were damaged or destroyed, up to a distance of around 50 kilometres.

Today too there are earthquakes in Switzerland, but they are mostly weak. The **Swiss Seismological Service** at ETH Zurich records them and assesses the danger. The earthquake hazard is highest in the **Valais**. After that come the Basel region, Graubünden and central Switzerland. That is why there are building regulations so that new buildings withstand earthquakes better.

gewusst: The Basel earthquake is often used as a comparison when experts ask what a similar quake would do today.
After the quake the people of Basel rebuilt their city and the Minster.

t1lhxj9s.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Schwyz

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Schwyz is entirely red, with a small white cross at the top left. Switzerland and its flag take their name from Schwyz.
wichtigste: The Schwyz coat of arms is red.
At the top left is a small white cross.
In the past the coat of arms was entirely red, without a cross.
Switzerland gets its name from the canton of Schwyz.
The Swiss flag is related to the Schwyz coat of arms.

abschnitte.text: The **coat of arms of the canton of Schwyz** is **red**. In the corner **at the top left** stands a small **white cross**. The canton's flag looks the same. In the Middle Ages the Schwyz flag was still entirely red. The small cross was only added later.

Schwyz is one of the three **Original Cantons**, together with Uri and Unterwalden. Abroad, all the Confederates were soon called **“Schwyzer”**. In this way the whole of **Switzerland** got its name from the canton of Schwyz. The red Swiss flag with its white cross also recalls the Schwyz coat of arms.

In the main town of **Schwyz** stands the **Federal Charters Museum**. There lies the **Federal Charter of 1291**. It is regarded as one of the most important documents of the early Confederation. Old flags from Swiss history are also on display there.

gewusst: The Swiss cross of the national flag is much larger and stands in the middle, while the Schwyz cross is small and stands in the corner.

t1ls0xb3.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Vaud

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Vaud is divided into white and green. In the white part is an inscription in French. It recalls how Vaud became a free canton.
wichtigste: The Vaud coat of arms is white at the top and green at the bottom.
In the white field, in golden letters, is “LIBERTÉ ET PATRIE”.
In English that means “Freedom and Fatherland”.
From 1536 to 1798 Vaud belonged to Bern.
Since 1803 Vaud has been a canton of its own.
The main town of Vaud is Lausanne.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: The coat of arms is **divided horizontally**. The upper half is **white**, the lower **green**. In the white field, in **golden letters**, are the words “LIBERTÉ ET PATRIE”. It is one of the few cantonal coats of arms in Switzerland with an **inscription**. That is why you recognise it at once.

The inscription means “**Freedom and Fatherland**” in English. For a long time Vaud was a **subject territory** of Bern. The people there could not decide for themselves about their land. In **1798** Vaud declared itself independent of Bern. The inscription recalls this newly won freedom.

At the liberation of 1798 many people of Vaud wore **green badges** as a sign of freedom. For a short time there was the **Lemanic Republic** with a green flag. The green stayed in the coat of arms afterwards. In **1803**, through the Act of Mediation, Vaud became a canton of Switzerland with equal rights.

Vaud lies in the west of Switzerland on **Lake Geneva** and reaches to the **Jura** and into the Alps. People speak **French** there. Well known are the **Lavaux vineyards** on Lake Geneva. On car number plates are the letters **VD** for “Vaud”, the French name of the canton.

gewusst: The vine terraces of Lavaux have been part of UNESCO's World Heritage since 2007.
The International Olympic Committee has its seat in Lausanne.

teile.einleitung: The Water Tower is an octagonal stone tower that stands in the middle of the Reuss in Lucerne. Together with the Chapel Bridge, it is the best-known landmark of the city.
wichtigste: The Water Tower stands in the Reuss in Lucerne.
It has eight corners and is built of stone.
It was built around the year 1300, before the Chapel Bridge.
It was part of the city's fortifications.
Later it served as an archive, a treasury and a prison.
Next to it the wooden Chapel Bridge crosses the river.

abschnitte.text: The **Water Tower** does not stand on the bank but **in the middle of the Reuss**. It has an **octagonal** ground plan and thick walls of stone. At the top it carries a pointed roof of red tiles. It was built around the year **1300**. That makes it older than the Chapel Bridge beside it.

In the Middle Ages the tower belonged to the **city wall** of Lucerne. It protected the city from the water side. Later important **documents** and the **city treasure** were kept in it. At times the tower was also a **prison**. Today it is not open to the public.

Next to the tower the **Chapel Bridge** crosses the Reuss. It is one of the oldest covered **wooden bridges** in Europe. Under its roof hang old **paintings** from the history of Lucerne. In **1993** a large part of the bridge burned down. It was rebuilt afterwards, and the Water Tower was left standing after the fire.

Together, bridge and tower are one of the **most photographed sights** in Switzerland. Many visitors from all over the world come to Lucerne to see them. Behind them lies **Lake Lucerne**, from which the Reuss flows out. The picture of the tower and the bridge is found on many postcards.

gewusst: The Water Tower is older than the Chapel Bridge, which was only built on to it later.
The name Chapel Bridge comes from the nearby St Peter's Chapel.

teile.einleitung: Alpine solar plants are large photovoltaic installations in the mountains. They supply a lot of electricity especially in winter, when Switzerland urgently needs it. Since 2022 the Confederation has supported such large installations.
wichtigste: The support package of 2022 is called Solarexpress.
The Confederation pays at most 60 per cent of the investment costs.
Installations producing 10 gigawatt hours a year or more are supported.
The support ends at a total of 2 terawatt hours a year.
In the mountains the installations lie above the fog and use the light reflected from snow.
Cold increases the efficiency of solar cells.
In 2023 the voters of the Valais rejected a cantonal solar decree.

abschnitte.text: In winter there is often **high fog** over the Central Plateau, while the mountains lie in the sun. In addition, **snow** throws a lot of light back, which is called a high **albedo**. **Cold** also helps: at low temperatures silicon solar cells work more efficiently. That is why installations in the Alps produce clearly more electricity in winter than in the lowlands.

Many alpine installations use **bifacial modules**. They are sensitive to light on both sides. They are often set up steeply so that the snow slides off. In this way light reflected from the snow also hits the **back** and produces extra electricity.

Because of a threatened **electricity shortage**, in autumn 2022 Parliament urgently passed a support package. It became known as the **Solarexpress**. The Confederation pays a one-off sum of at most **60 per cent** of the investment costs. Only installations producing **10 gigawatt hours** a year or more are supported. The support ends as soon as the installations together produce **2 terawatt hours** a year, about 2.5 per cent of Swiss electricity production.

A well-known example is **AlpinSolar** by Axpo in the canton of Glarus. On the **Muttsee dam** at around 2,500 metres, almost 5,000 modules were installed. They supply around 3.3 gigawatt hours of electricity a year. About **half** of it is produced in the winter half-year, whereas for installations on the Central Plateau it is usually only a quarter to a third.

Supporters see in alpine installations a chance for secure **winter electricity**. Critics worry about the **landscape** and nature in the mountains. In the Valais the people voted on 10 September 2023 on a decree that was meant to speed up the procedures. Just under 54 per cent rejected it. The federal support still applied, however.

gewusst: On cold, sunny winter days in the mountains, solar modules work better than on hot summer days in the lowlands.
AlpinSolar uses an existing dam, so no new land had to be built on.

teile.einleitung: Tell's Chapel stands right on the shore of Lake Uri near Sisikon in the canton of Uri. It recalls the legend of William Tell, who is said to have saved himself here by leaping out of a boat.
wichtigste: Tell's Chapel stands at the Tellsplatte near Sisikon.
Lake Uri is the southernmost part of Lake Lucerne.
According to the legend, Tell leapt here from the boat of the bailiff Gessler.
The present chapel was built in the 19th century.
Inside, large murals show scenes from the Tell legend.

abschnitte.text: According to the legend, **William Tell** was taken prisoner after shooting the apple from his son's head. The bailiff **Gessler** wanted to take him across the lake by boat. A violent **storm** blew up, and Tell was put at the helm. He steered the boat close to the shore and leapt onto a **ledge of rock**. This spot is now called the **Tellsplatte**.

A small chapel already stood at the Tellsplatte centuries ago. The present **Tell's Chapel** was built in the 19th century. Inside, the artist **Ernst Stückelberg** painted large **murals**. They show the shot at the apple, Tell's leap and further scenes from the legend. The chapel stands so close to the water that you can also see it clearly from a boat.

Many visitors come by **boat** across Lake Uri. Others walk the **Swiss Path**, a hiking trail around Lake Uri. From the Axenstrasse a footpath leads down to the chapel. Opposite, on the other shore of the lake, lies the **Rütli meadow**.

Whether William Tell really lived has not been proved. Most experts regard him as a **legendary figure**. Even so, he is an important figure for Switzerland. He stands for courage and for the desire for **freedom**. Tell's Chapel is therefore a well-known place of remembrance.

gewusst: The Tellsplatte is a popular stop for boats on Lake Uri.
The story of Tell's leap became famous worldwide through Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell”.

teile.einleitung: Lake Walen lies in eastern Switzerland between the canton of St Gallen and the canton of Glarus. It is surrounded by steep mountains, above all by the Churfirsten on the northern shore.
wichtigste: Lake Walen lies between the cantons of St Gallen and Glarus.
The northern shore belongs to the canton of St Gallen.
Part of the southern shore belongs to the canton of Glarus.
On the northern shore the Churfirsten rise steeply.
The village of Quinten can only be reached by boat or on foot.
The lake lies between Weesen and Walenstadt.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Walen** lies between **Weesen** in the west and **Walenstadt** in the east. It is about 15 kilometres long and quite narrow. On the northern shore the **Churfirsten** rise almost vertically like a rock wall. On the southern shore too the mountains are high and steep. The water often shimmers green or turquoise.

The lake belongs to two cantons. The **northern shore** belongs entirely to the canton of **St Gallen**. On the **southern shore** one part lies in the canton of **Glarus**, for example near Mühlehorn; the rest belongs to St Gallen. So the canton of Glarus shares Lake Walen with St Gallen.

On the northern shore lies the little village of **Quinten**. It has no road and can only be reached by **boat** or on foot. Because it lies sheltered from the Churfirsten and sunny, the climate there is mild. That is why even **vines** and figs grow in Quinten. Nearby the **Seerenbach Falls** tumble over the rocks.

Because the northern shore is so steep, the railway and motorway run along the **southern shore**. The A3 motorway runs there through many tunnels and galleries. The railway line from Zurich to Chur also runs along the lake. From the train you have a lovely view of the Churfirsten.

gewusst: The Seerenbach Falls near Betlis are among the highest waterfalls in Switzerland.
Because of its mild climate Quinten is sometimes called the “Riviera of eastern Switzerland”.

teile.einleitung: Willisauer Ringli are a hard biscuit in the shape of a ring. They come from the little town of Willisau in the canton of Lucerne and are known all over Switzerland.
wichtigste: Willisauer Ringli are small, hard rings.
They are made mainly from sugar and flour.
They come from Willisau in the canton of Lucerne.
Because they are so hard, people often suck them for a long time.
They have been made since the 19th century.
They keep for a long time.

abschnitte.text: The **Willisauer Ringli** are small, flat **rings** with a hole in the middle. They consist mainly of **sugar** and **flour**, with flavourings added. The biscuit is very **hard**. That is why many people do not bite into it but **suck** it slowly. You should be careful so that no tooth is damaged.

**Willisau** is a little town in the **Lucerne Hinterland**. The Ringli have been baked there since the **19th century**. They became so well known that today they make the name of the town known all over the country. Besides the Ringli, Willisau is also known for its **jazz festival**.

Because the Ringli are **dry and hard**, they keep for a long time. That is why they make a good **gift** and food for walks. In the past visitors often brought them home from Willisau as a **souvenir**. Today you can buy them in many shops in Switzerland.

gewusst: Willisau has a well-preserved old town with town gates from the Middle Ages.
There are also Ringli with chocolate or other flavours.

teile.einleitung: Trogen is a small village in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Although it has only a few inhabitants, the cantonal courts sit here. Trogen is also known for its beautiful houses and the Pestalozzi Children's Village.
wichtigste: Trogen lies in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
The cantonal courts have their seat in Trogen.
The government and parliament meet in Herisau.
Until 1997 the Landsgemeinde was held alternately in Trogen and Hundwil.
In Trogen stands the Pestalozzi Children's Village, founded in 1946.

abschnitte.text: Appenzell Ausserrhoden does not have a single main town for everything. The **government** and **parliament** are in **Herisau**. The canton's **courts** sit in **Trogen**. So two municipalities share the tasks that elsewhere are held by a single main town. This has to do with the history of the canton.

In the past, those entitled to vote in Ausserrhoden decided matters at the **Landsgemeinde**. This is an assembly in the open air, at which people vote by raising a hand. It was held alternately in **Trogen** and in **Hundwil**. In **1997** those entitled to vote decided to abolish the Landsgemeinde. Today voting is done at the ballot box.

On the **Landsgemeindeplatz** in Trogen stand large, magnificent houses. Many of them were built by the **Zellweger** family. They became rich in the 18th century through the **linen trade** and fabrics. The houses show how prosperous the place was at that time. Trogen also has a **cantonal school**.

After the **Second World War** the **Pestalozzi Children's Village** was founded in Trogen in **1946**. Here children from countries affected by war found a home. It is named after the educator **Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi**. Today the foundation works for education and peaceful coexistence.

gewusst: The Trogenerbahn takes you directly from St Gallen to Trogen.
The Pestalozzi Children's Village lies on a hill above the village.

teile.einleitung: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes is a famous meat dish from Zurich. It consists of finely sliced veal in a cream sauce and is often served with rösti.
wichtigste: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes carries the name of the city of Zurich.
It is made from veal cut into fine strips.
The sauce consists of cream, often with white wine and mushrooms.
It is usually served with rösti.
In Zurich German it is called “Züri Gschnätzlets”.

abschnitte.text: **Zürcher Geschnetzeltes** is one of the best-known dishes in Switzerland. In Zurich German it is called **Züri Gschnätzlets**. You find it on the menu in many restaurants in Switzerland. Abroad too, many people know this dish as a Swiss speciality.

**Schnetzeln** means cutting meat into small, thin strips or slivers. For Zürcher Geschnetzeltes you use **veal**. The strips are fried only briefly and hot in the pan so that they stay tender. Sometimes veal kidneys are added too.

After frying, you sweat **onions** and usually **mushrooms** too. Then you deglaze with white wine and a little stock. At the end **cream** is added, and the sauce is cooked down until nicely creamy. The meat is only put back into the sauce at the end so that it does not turn tough.

The classic side dish is a crispy **rösti** made of grated potatoes. It goes well with the creamy sauce. Some people also eat noodles or rice with it. Together, Geschnetzeltes and rösti are a typical Sunday meal for many.

gewusst: Rösti and Zürcher Geschnetzeltes together are regarded as one of the best-known Swiss dishes of all.
Meat that cooks too long in the sauce becomes tough. That is why it is only added again at the end.

teile.einleitung: Internal migration means that people change their place of residence within a country. They move, for example, from a village to a city or from one canton to another. In doing so they do not cross the national border.
wichtigste: Internal migration is a change of residence within one state.
Push factors drive people away, pull factors attract them.
In the 19th century there was a strong flight from the land to the industrial towns.
In peri-urbanisation, rural municipalities grow through commuters.
Since the late 1990s cities such as Zurich have been gaining inhabitants again.
In Switzerland different taxes also play a role.

abschnitte.text: Why do people move? Experts distinguish **push factors** and **pull factors**. Push factors drive people away, for example a **lack of jobs** where they live. Pull factors attract them to a new place, such as good schools, jobs or a lovely flat. Mostly both work together.

abschnitte.titel: Flight from the land in the 19th century
abschnitte.text: During **industrialisation** many factories came into being. In cities and industrial towns there were new jobs. That is why numerous people left the rural areas. This movement is called **rural exodus**. As a result the cities grew strongly.

abschnitte.titel: From the city edge to the countryside
abschnitte.text: In the 20th century many families moved from the cities to the surrounding municipalities. Later rural municipalities far outside the **agglomerations** grew too. This is called **peri-urbanisation**. The new residents often work in the centres and commute every day. This leads to more traffic and to **urban sprawl** in the landscape.

Since the late 1990s core cities such as **Zurich** have been growing again. This development is called **re-urbanisation**. One reason is that old industrial areas were converted into residential and work districts. Sometimes this leads to **gentrification**: after renovations rents rise, wealthier people move in, and former residents have to move away.

In Switzerland **cantons and municipalities** set their tax rates themselves. The **tax burden** is therefore not the same everywhere. Households with high earnings often move to municipalities with low taxes. Many people, however, do not move at all but become **commuters**. Commuting is not internal migration, because the place of residence stays the same.

gewusst: In Switzerland a large part of the working population commutes to another municipality for work.
The opposite of internal migration is external migration, in which people move abroad or come from abroad.

teile.einleitung: The voting age sets the age from which you may vote and take part in elections. In Switzerland it is mostly 18 years, but in the canton of Glarus even 16-year-olds can have a say.
wichtigste: The voting age is the age from which you may vote and elect.
For federal votes in Switzerland it is 18 years.
In 2007 Glarus became the first canton to introduce a voting age of 16.
This was decided by the Landsgemeinde in Glarus.
In Glarus young people from 16 can have a say on cantonal and municipal questions.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland citizens can often **vote** on issues and **elect** their representatives. The **voting age** sets the age from which you may do this. For **federal** votes and elections it is **18 years**. Until **1991** it was still 20 years. Then the people and the cantons agreed to lower it to 18.

In the canton of **Glarus** a special voting age applies. At the **Landsgemeinde** (open-air assembly) in **2007**, those entitled to vote decided to lower the age to **16 years**. Glarus was thus the **first canton** in Switzerland with a voting age of 16. So young people can have a say on cantonal and municipal questions from the age of 16. For federal votes, the age of 18 applies to them too.

The **Landsgemeinde** is an old form of direct democracy. Once a year those entitled to vote gather in the open air on the Zaunplatz in **Glarus**. They vote by holding up their **voting card**. Today the Landsgemeinde exists only in Glarus and in **Appenzell Innerrhoden**. So in Glarus even 16-year-olds can raise their hand in the middle of the square.

Whether people should vote as early as 16 is debated again and again in Switzerland. **Supporters** say that young people are affected by many decisions and should have a say early. **Opponents** say that the rights and duties of adulthood should go together, that is, from 18. Several cantons have voted on it, and the results have differed.

gewusst: Women in Switzerland have only been able to vote and stand in elections at federal level since 1971.
Even in Glarus you can only be elected to an office from the age of 18.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Science Center Technorama in Winterthur is a hands-on museum. Instead of just looking at things, you can experiment and marvel for yourself.
wichtigste: The Technorama stands in Winterthur in the canton of Zurich.
It opened in 1982.
There are hundreds of experiments to try out.
The themes range from light and magnetism to water and perception.
It is one of the largest science centres in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: At the Technorama the rule is: **please touch!** At many stations you press, turn or pull things yourself. In this way you discover how **physics**, **chemistry** and **nature** work. Short texts explain what is happening. You learn by trying things out yourself, not by listening.

There are areas on **light and colours**, on **magnetism** and **electricity** and on **water**. You can, for example, create whirlpools in water or see shadows in bright colours. Other stations show how easily our eyes can be fooled. Such **optical illusions** are very popular with children and adults.

Besides the experiments there are **demonstrations**. Experts show experiments that you could not do on your own. Well known are the demonstrations with **high voltage**, in which big sparks crackle. School classes also often visit the Technorama to learn more about the natural sciences.

**Winterthur** is the second-largest city in the canton of Zurich. The city was long an important place for industry and mechanical engineering. Today it is also known for its many **museums**. The Technorama is among the most visited of them.

gewusst: At the Technorama there are also experiments outdoors in the park.
Many stations work entirely without electricity, using only water, light or gravity.

teile.einleitung: Stein am Rhein is a small town in the canton of Schaffhausen. It is famous for its old town with brightly painted house façades and is one of the most beautiful places in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Stein am Rhein lies in the canton of Schaffhausen on the Rhine.
Here the Rhine flows out of the Untersee, part of Lake Constance.
In the old town many houses are painted with colourful pictures.
Hohenklingen Castle stands above the little town.
In 1972 Stein am Rhein was the first place to receive the Wakker Prize.

abschnitte.titel: A little town on the Rhine
abschnitte.text: **Stein am Rhein** lies in the canton of **Schaffhausen**. At this spot the **Rhine** flows out of the **Untersee**, the western part of Lake Constance. The little town is small but very old. Its medieval **old town** is well preserved. Many visitors arrive by boat from Schaffhausen or from Lake Constance.

Best known is the **Rathausplatz** (town hall square). All around stand old **half-timbered houses** and town houses. Many of them are decorated with large, colourful **façade paintings**. The pictures show stories from the Bible, from history and from legends. Many houses also have beautiful **oriel windows** and names of their own, for example “Zum weissen Adler” (“At the White Eagle”).

On the bank of the Rhine stands the former **St Georgen Monastery**. Today it is a museum and shows how the monks lived in the past. High above the little town towers **Hohenklingen Castle**. From there you have a lovely view of Stein am Rhein, the Rhine and the Untersee. You can walk up on foot.

In **1972** Stein am Rhein became the first place ever to receive the **Wakker Prize**. This prize is awarded by the **Swiss Heritage Society** to municipalities that take particularly good care of their townscape. The residents make sure that the old houses are preserved. That is why Stein am Rhein is regarded as one of the most beautiful little towns in Switzerland.

gewusst: Part of Stein am Rhein lies on the other side of the Rhine; a bridge links the two banks.
The Wakker Prize has been awarded every year to a Swiss municipality since 1972.

teile.einleitung: After Lausanne, Yverdon-les-Bains is the second largest city in the canton of Vaud. It lies at the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel and is known for its thermal baths.
wichtigste: Yverdon-les-Bains is the second largest city in Vaud.
It lies at the southern end of Lake Neuchâtel.
People speak French there.
The city is known for its warm thermal water.
The Romans already had a settlement here.
The famous educator Pestalozzi once taught in the castle.

abschnitte.text: **Yverdon-les-Bains** lies at the **southern end of Lake Neuchâtel** in the canton of **Vaud**. People speak **French** here. After **Lausanne**, Yverdon is the **second largest city** of the canton. The city is an important junction for railway and roads. Around the city there are fields and nature reserves on the lakeshore.

The addition “**les-Bains**” means “the baths”. In Yverdon **warm water** comes out of the ground. It contains many **minerals**. The **Romans** already used this spring for bathing. Today there is a large **thermal bath** where people come to relax.

In the middle of the city stands a **castle** from the **Middle Ages**. It was built by the **House of Savoy**. At the beginning of the 19th century the famous educator **Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi** ran a **school** here. Children from many countries learned with him. Pestalozzi wanted children to learn with **head, heart and hand**.

People lived here more than **2,000 years ago**. The **Romans** called the place **Eburodunum**. Remains of their settlement have been found. On the lakeshore near Yverdon there are also **rows of stones** from the New Stone Age, which people set up thousands of years ago.

gewusst: In Yverdon there is a museum of science fiction, the “Maison d'Ailleurs”.
A monument to Pestalozzi stands on the square in front of the castle.

teile.einleitung: The Zugerberg is the local mountain of the city of Zug. A funicular takes you quickly up to a wide plateau with meadows, woods and bogs.
wichtigste: The Zugerberg lies directly east above the city of Zug.
Its highest point is about 1,000 metres above sea level.
The Zugerberg Railway is a funicular.
At the top there are many hiking trails and farms.
From there you can see across Lake Zug to the Rigi, Pilatus and the Alps.

abschnitte.text: The Zugerberg rises right behind the city of Zug. It is not a pointed peak but a long ridge with a **plateau**. Its highest point is at around 1,000 metres above sea level. For many people from Zug it is a popular destination for an outing after school or work.

The **Zugerberg Railway** goes up the Zugerberg. It is a **funicular**: the carriage runs on rails and is pulled up the steep slope by a strong cable. You reach the valley station by bus from the city. The railway has been running since the beginning of the 20th century.

At the top many **hiking trails** wait, through meadows and woods. There are farms with cows and small **raised bogs** that are protected. In winter, if there is enough snow, you can go sledging or cross-country skiing on narrow trails. Anyone who walks to the viewpoint is rewarded with a lovely view.

From the Zugerberg you can see the whole of **Lake Zug** and the city of Zug. Opposite stand the Rigi and Pilatus. In clear weather the view reaches to the snow-covered **Alps**. On the other side too you can look down to Lake Ägeri.

gewusst: From the Zugerberg on clear days you can see both lakes of Zug: Lake Zug and Lake Ägeri.
The funicular overcomes a large difference in height in a few minutes.

teile.einleitung: After Zurich, Winterthur is the second largest city in the canton of Zurich. The city lies north-east of Zurich and has over 100,000 inhabitants. It is known for its industry, its museums and its many gardens.
wichtigste: Winterthur is the second largest city in the canton of Zurich.
It lies north-east of the city of Zurich.
Winterthur has over 100,000 inhabitants.
It is one of the largest cities in Switzerland.
In the past Winterthur was an important industrial city.
Today it is known for its many museums.

abschnitte.text: **Winterthur** lies about 20 kilometres **north-east of Zurich**. With over **100,000** inhabitants, it is the **second largest city in the canton of Zurich**. In the whole of Switzerland it is one of the largest cities. Local people often say “**Winti**” for short. The old town has many lanes where you can go shopping.

In the 19th and 20th centuries Winterthur was an important **industrial city**. Large companies such as **Sulzer** built machines, engines and locomotives here. Thousands of people worked in the **factories**. Today many old factory halls have been converted. Inside them there are now flats, schools and offices.

Winterthur also calls itself a **city of museums**. In the past rich families collected **art** and gave it to the city. That is why there are several **art museums**. Especially popular with children is the **Swiss Science Center Technorama**. There you can try out many experiments yourself.

Winterthur has many **parks** and **gardens** and is therefore also called the “**garden city**”. In the city there is a **university of applied sciences** with many students. Nearby stands **Kyburg Castle**, a large castle from the Middle Ages. It once belonged to the Counts of Kyburg and is now a **museum**.

gewusst: The coat of arms of Winterthur shows two red lions on a white ground.
In the Technorama you can see, for example, an artificial lightning bolt and a tornado made of mist.

teile.einleitung: Valère is a fortified church on a hill above Sion, the capital of the Valais. Together with the castle ruin of Tourbillon on the neighbouring hill, it is the landmark of the town.
wichtigste: Valère stands on a hill above Sion in the canton of the Valais.
The fortified church was built in the Middle Ages.
On the neighbouring hill stands the castle ruin of Tourbillon.
Valère and Tourbillon are the landmark of Sion.
In Valère stands one of the oldest playable organs in the world.
Today part of the Valais History Museum is housed in Valère.

abschnitte.text: Two rocky hills rise above the old town of **Sion**. On one stands the fortified church of **Valère**, on the other the castle ruin of **Tourbillon**. You can see them from far away in the **Rhône valley**. That is why they are the landmark of the capital of the Valais. A footpath leads up from the old town.

Valère is a **fortified church**: a church protected by walls like a castle. It was built in the 12th and 13th centuries. In the past, canons lived here, that is, clergy of the church of Sion. Inside there are old wall paintings and wood carvings. Especially well known is the **organ**, which was built in the 15th century and is still played today.

On the higher hill stands **Tourbillon**. The castle was built around 1300 for the Bishop of Sion. In 1788 it was gutted by fire in a great fire in the town. Since then it has been a **ruin**. From the top there is a wide view over the Valais.

Part of the **Valais History Museum** is now housed in Valère. There you can see objects from the history of the canton. In summer, organ concerts take place in the church. Many school classes and tourists visit the two hills.

gewusst: The organ of Valère is regarded as one of the oldest organs in the world that can still be played.
Between the two hills lies a small saddle, over which you can walk from Valère to Tourbillon.

teile.einleitung: Alpine farming means: in summer farmers take their animals to pastures high in the mountains. There the cows eat fresh grass, and alpine cheese is made from the milk. This tradition has existed in Switzerland for a very long time.
wichtigste: An alp is a mountain pasture for the summer.
In early summer the cows go up to the alp at the Alpaufzug.
The herdsman (Senn) makes alpine cheese from the fresh milk.
Dairy cows are milked twice a day.
The cows wear bells so that you can hear them.
Typical breeds are Braunvieh and Eringer.

abschnitte.text: An **alp** is a pasture in the mountains. In **summer** cows, young cattle or goats graze there. Down in the valley the farmer can make hay for the winter in this time. In early summer the animals go up at the **Alpaufzug**, and in autumn they come back at the **Alpabzug**.

On the alp the **Senn** (herdsman) or **Sennerin** (herdswoman) works. They make **alpine cheese** from the fresh milk. The **Zusenn** (assistant herdsman) helps with milking, herding and cheese-making. Often these are young people who learn the work on the alp this way. Dairy cows are usually milked **twice** a day, in the morning and in the evening.

On the alp the cows eat fresh **grass** and many **mountain herbs**. This gives the milk and the cheese a special taste. The cows often wear a **bell** around the neck. When they walk, the bell sounds, and so you can hear where the animals are grazing.

**Braunvieh** (“brown cattle”) is one of the most common breeds of cow in Switzerland. It is strong and well adapted to the mountains. In the Valais lives the **Eringer** cow. It is black or dark brown. In cow fights the Eringer cows measure their strength, and the winner is called the **queen**.

Alpine farming keeps the mountain pastures open. Without animals many pastures would turn into forest over time. That is why the **Confederation** supports the farmers with payments for summering, which is what the summer time of the animals on the alp is called.

gewusst: At the Eringer cow fights in the Valais, one cow is crowned “queen”.
Alpine cheese may only be called that if it is made in summer directly on the alp.

teile.einleitung: Basel Zoo is the oldest zoo in Switzerland. The people of Basel affectionately call it “Zolli”. It lies in the middle of the city, not far from Basel SBB station.
wichtigste: Basel Zoo is called “Zolli”.
It opened in 1874.
It is the oldest zoo in Switzerland.
It lies in the middle of the city of Basel.
Animals from all continents live there.
The Zolli is known for rhinoceroses, okapis and great apes.

abschnitte.text: **Basel Zoo** opened in **1874**. That makes it the **oldest zoo in Switzerland**. The people of Basel affectionately call it the “**Zolli**”. It lies **in the middle of the city** on the bank of the little river Birsig, not far from the station. Many families come here regularly.

In the Zolli live animals from **all continents**. It is known for its **Indian rhinoceroses**, **okapis** and **pygmy hippopotamuses**. In the **Monkey House** live gorillas, chimpanzees and orangutans. In the **Vivarium** you can see fish, penguins and reptiles. With many species, **young animals** are born again and again in the Zolli.

A modern zoo does not only want to show animals. It also helps to **protect endangered species**. For this the Zolli works together with other zoos all over the world. It also supports **conservation projects** in the wild. In addition, visitors learn a great deal about animals and their habitats.

gewusst: The Zolli is one of the most popular destinations for outings in Switzerland.
The Zolli is so close to the station that you can be there on foot from the train in a few minutes.

teile.einleitung: The Zytglogge is a medieval tower in the old town of Bern and one of the best-known landmarks of the city. It is famous for its astronomical clock and the figures that move shortly before every full hour.
wichtigste: The Zytglogge stands in the old town of Bern.
It used to be a city gate.
The astronomical clock dates from the 16th century.
Shortly before every full hour figures move.
The old town of Bern is part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

abschnitte.titel: From city gate to clock tower
abschnitte.text: The Zytglogge was built in the **13th century**. At that time it was the western **city gate** of Bern. As the city grew, the tower soon lay in the middle of the city. Later it also served as a prison. After a great city fire in 1405 it was rebuilt and given a clock.

In the 16th century the clockmaker **Kaspar Brunner** built a new clockwork with an **astronomical clock**. It shows not only the time but also the day of the week, the month, the star sign and the phase of the moon. The name comes from Bernese German: **Zyt** means time and **Glogge** means bell. So a Zytglogge is a time bell.

A few minutes before every full hour the **figure display** begins. A cockerel crows, a jester rings little bells, and a procession of small **bears** goes round. The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern. The figure **Chronos**, the god of time, turns an hourglass. At the end a golden figure at the top strikes the hours on the bell with a hammer.

In front of the Zytglogge many **tourists** gather every day to see the figure display. On guided tours you can even climb inside and look at the old clockwork. The tower belongs to the **old town of Bern**, which has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage since 1983.

gewusst: The clockwork in the Zytglogge has been running for almost 500 years.
In German people say “der Zytglogge” (masculine), although “Glogge” means bell and is feminine.

teile.einleitung: Swissminiatur is an open-air park in Melide in the canton of Ticino. There you can see Switzerland in miniature: famous buildings, railways and landscapes as models.
wichtigste: Swissminiatur lies in Melide on Lake Lugano.
It opened in 1959.
The park shows over a hundred models from all over Switzerland.
The models are built at a scale of 1 to 25.
Small trains and boats run through the park.

abschnitte.text: In Swissminiatur stand models of well-known buildings from all parts of the country. They include castles, churches, bridges and railway stations. A **scale of 1 to 25** means that one metre on the real building is four centimetres in the model. So in one afternoon you can walk through the whole of Switzerland.

Many small **model trains** run through the park on long tracks. They show how important the **railway** is for Switzerland. There are also cable cars and boats in miniature. Between the models, flowers and small trees grow so that everything looks like a real landscape.

**Melide** lies on the shore of **Lake Lugano**, not far from Lugano. Here the causeway runs from Melide to Bissone across the lake, carrying a road and a railway line. Swissminiatur is usually open from spring to autumn. It is one of the well-known destinations for outings in Ticino.

gewusst: Swissminiatur has existed for over 60 years.
Because the models stand outside all year round, they have to be looked after and repaired regularly.

teile.einleitung: The population of Switzerland has been growing for many decades. At the end of 2024 over 9 million people lived in the country. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO) counts every year how many people are born, die, move in or move away.
wichtigste: At the end of 2012 Switzerland for the first time had over 8 million inhabitants.
In 2024 the population grew by around 86,600 people and passed 9 million.
The growth comes mainly from immigration.
In 2024 there was only a small surplus of births of around 6,200 people.
The birth rate in 2024 was around 1.3 children per woman.
Switzerland has around 220 inhabitants per km².

abschnitte.text: The FSO counts the **permanent resident population**. This includes all Swiss citizens and all foreigners with a permit for at least **12 months**. People who are only in Switzerland for a short time count as the non-permanent resident population. At the end of **2012** Switzerland for the first time counted over **8 million** inhabitants. By the end of 2024 around another million had been added.

In 2024 there were around 212,700 **immigrations** and around 125,600 **emigrations**. The difference is called the **net migration**. It was about 87,000 people. The population grew in 2024 by around **86,600 people**, that is, by about 1 per cent. So the growth came almost entirely from immigration.

In 2024 there were around 78,000 births and 71,800 deaths. So the **surplus of births** was only about 6,200 people. It was last that low in **1918**, the year of the Spanish flu. The **birth rate** fell to around **1.3 children per woman**, the lowest value ever measured. For a population to stay the same size without immigration, about 2.1 would be needed.

Not all cantons grow equally fast. In 2024 **Schaffhausen** grew most, by 1.8 per cent, followed by Fribourg and the Valais with 1.5 per cent each. Ticino and Appenzell Ausserrhoden grew the least. The **population density** is around **220 inhabitants per km²**. On the Central Plateau people live much more densely, in the Alps much less densely.

gewusst: Around 1900 only about 3.3 million people lived in Switzerland.
Because people are living longer and longer, the share of older people in the population is rising, which is important for the AHV, for example.

teile.einleitung: The Toggenburg is a valley region in the canton of St Gallen. The Thur flows through the valley. The area is known for its mountains, its folk music and hiking.
wichtigste: The Toggenburg is in the canton of St Gallen.
The Thur rises in the uppermost Toggenburg and flows through the whole valley.
Above the valley stand the Churfirsten and the Säntis.
Wildhaus is the birthplace of the reformer Huldrych Zwingli.
The Toggenburg is known for natural yodelling and folk music.

abschnitte.text: The Toggenburg stretches from the area around **Wildhaus** in the south to near **Wil** in the north. The **Thur** flows through the valley. Important places are **Wattwil**, **Lichtensteig** and **Ebnat-Kappel**. The little town of Lichtensteig has a well-preserved old town. In the upper part lie villages such as Unterwasser and Alt St Johann.

In the south of the valley stand the **Churfirsten**, a row of seven peaks. On the other side they fall steeply to **Lake Walen**. In the north the **Säntis** rises in the Alpstein. In winter you can go **skiing** in the Toggenburg, in summer walking. Cable cars take you, for example, up the Chäserrugg.

The Toggenburg is known for **natural yodelling**, singing without words. Instruments such as the **Halszither** (a kind of zither) are also part of the tradition. Near Alt St Johann and Wildhaus there is the **Klangwelt Toggenburg** (Toggenburg Sound World) with sound trails to try out. In summer the farmers solemnly drive their cattle up to the alp.

In **Wildhaus** the reformer **Huldrych Zwingli** was born in **1484**. You can still visit his birthplace today. For a long time the Toggenburg belonged to the abbey of St Gallen. Since 1803 it has been part of the canton of St Gallen. In the past the valley was also known for **textile production**.

gewusst: The Toggenburg goat is a breed of goat named after the valley.
The Churfirsten look gentle from the north but like a steep wall from the south.

teile.einleitung: Rail 2000 was a large programme to improve the Swiss railway network. The trains were not meant to run as fast as possible but in such a way that the connections work. The people approved the concept in 1987.
wichtigste: The people accepted Rail 2000 on 6 December 1987.
The principle is: as fast as necessary, not as fast as possible.
The first stage started with the timetable change in December 2004.
The heart is the new line from Mattstetten to Rothrist.
Thanks to ETCS Level 2 the trains run there at 200 km/h.
The journey time from Bern to Zurich fell to 56 minutes.

abschnitte.text: On 6 December 1987 the people accepted the credit for **Rail 2000** with 57 per cent. The principle was: **“As fast as necessary, not as fast as possible.”** The journey times were meant to be exactly short enough for the connections at the big stations to work. High speed at any price was not the aim.

In big stations, the **junctions**, trains arrive from all directions shortly before the full or half hour. Shortly afterwards they leave again. This way you can **change trains** quickly. For this to work, the journey time between two junctions must be just under an hour or half an hour. That is why individual lines were speeded up on purpose.

The heart of the first stage is the **new line** between **Mattstetten** and **Rothrist**. It is built for 200 km/h. The train protection system **ETCS Level 2** makes this possible: the driver sees the permission to proceed directly in the **cab**, and signals beside the track are no longer needed. From December 2007 trains ran there at 200 km/h, and the journey from Bern to Zurich took only **56 minutes** instead of 69.

With the timetable change of 12 December 2004 the **first stage** went into operation. It was one of the biggest timetable changes in the history of the **SBB**. In 1992 Parliament had approved up to 7.4 billion francs for it. Around 5.9 billion francs, at 1994 prices, were finally accounted for.

After Rail 2000, in 2009 Parliament decided the programme **Future Development of Rail Infrastructure**, **ZEB** for short. This improved the junction principle further. Later came the strategic development programmes **STEP**. In this way the rail network is expanded step by step.

gewusst: With Rail 2000 the trains did not run as fast as possible but exactly suited to the timetable pattern.
On the new line there are no ordinary signals beside the track any more, everything appears in the cab.

teile.einleitung: Lake Sihl lies near Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. It is the largest reservoir in Switzerland by area and supplies water for generating electricity.
wichtigste: Lake Sihl lies near Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It is the largest reservoir in Switzerland by area.
The River Sihl was dammed in the 1930s.
With the water, the Etzel power station generates electricity, mainly for the railways.
In summer you can swim in Lake Sihl; in winter it often freezes over.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Sihl** is not a natural lake but a **reservoir**. It was created when the **River Sihl** was held back by a dam. The lake was fully filled in **1937**, so around 90 years ago. It is the **largest reservoir by area** in Switzerland. Because it lies on a high plateau, it is not very deep.

The water of Lake Sihl is used for the **Etzel power station**. Through a tunnel and pipes it flows down to **Altendorf** on Lake Zurich. On the way it drops a great height and drives **turbines**. This produces **electricity**, which is used above all for **SBB** trains. Hydropower is an important source of electricity in Switzerland.

Many families had to leave their homes for the reservoir. Farms, houses and parts of villages disappeared under the water. The people were resettled, which was hard for many of them. So that you can cross the lake, bridges were built, for example at **Willerzell**. Not far away lies the famous **Einsiedeln Abbey**.

Today Lake Sihl is a popular place for outings. In summer you can **swim**, sail, windsurf and barbecue on the shore. Walking and cycling paths lead around the lake. In winter the lake freezes over in cold years. Then you can sometimes go **ice skating** on it, but only if the authorities have declared the ice safe.

gewusst: Lake Sihl lies at almost 900 metres above sea level, higher than Lake Zurich.
When a lot of water is needed for electricity in winter, the water level of the lake drops noticeably.

teile.einleitung: UEFA is the football association of Europe. It organises major tournaments such as the Champions League and the European Championship. Its headquarters are in Nyon on Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud.
wichtigste: UEFA is short for “Union des Associations Européennes de Football”.
UEFA was founded in Basel in 1954.
Its headquarters are in Nyon in the canton of Vaud.
Its members are the national football associations of Europe.
It organises the Champions League and the European Championship.
Tournaments for women and juniors are also part of it.

abschnitte.text: **UEFA** is an **umbrella organisation**. Its members are not clubs but the national **football associations** of the European countries. The **Swiss Football Association** belongs to it too. UEFA is one of six continental confederations. It belongs to the world football body **FIFA**, which has its headquarters in Zurich.

The best-known club competition is the **UEFA Champions League**. There the best clubs in Europe play against each other. Besides it there is the **Europa League** and other competitions. For national teams UEFA organises the **European Championship**. The women's European Championship and tournaments for juniors are also part of it.

UEFA was founded in **Basel** in **1954**. At first it had its seat in Paris, later in Bern. Since the 1990s it has been in **Nyon** in the canton of Vaud. Its headquarters stand there right on **Lake Geneva**. The draws for many tournaments also take place here.

UEFA sets out how its competitions are run. It trains referees and supports the development of young players. It distributes money from the tournaments to its member associations. It also campaigns against racism and violence in stadiums.

gewusst: Several large sports federations have their seat in Switzerland, for example the International Olympic Committee in Lausanne.
In 2008 Switzerland, together with Austria, hosted the men's European Football Championship.

teile.einleitung: The Vallée de Joux is a high valley in the Vaud Jura, near the border with France. It is world-famous for its watchmaking workshops, where fine and complicated watches have been made for centuries.
wichtigste: The Vallée de Joux lies in the Jura in the canton of Vaud.
The valley lies at about 1,000 metres above sea level.
In the valley lies the Lac de Joux, the largest lake in the Jura.
Important places are Le Sentier and Le Brassus.
Famous watch companies have their headquarters here.
The winters are long and cold.

abschnitte.titel: A high valley in the Jura
abschnitte.text: The Vallée de Joux lies in the **Jura** in the west of the canton of Vaud, at about 1,000 metres above sea level. In the valley lies the **Lac de Joux**, the largest lake of the Jura mountains. Beside it is the small Lac Brenet. The valley belongs to three municipalities: Le Chenit, L'Abbaye and Le Lieu. The best-known villages are **Le Sentier** and **Le Brassus**.

In the past the people of the valley lived from farming. In the long winter there was little to do. So many families began to make **watch parts** at home. In time a great craft grew up. Today well-known **watchmaking manufactures** have their headquarters in the valley. There especially fine watches with complicated movements are built.

A **manufacture** is a workshop in which much is done by hand. The watchmakers assemble tiny gear wheels, springs and screws. Some watches have **complications**, for example a moon phase or a calendar. Such a watch takes a great deal of patience and experience. The watchmaking craft of Switzerland and France is part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.

In winter it is often very cold in the Vallée de Joux. When the **Lac de Joux** freezes, you can skate on it. The valley is also popular with cross-country skiers. In summer many people walk and swim at the lake. Forests and pastures shape the quiet landscape.

gewusst: In winter the Lac de Joux can freeze so thickly that you can skate on it over long distances.
The watchmaking craft of Switzerland and France was added to UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage in 2020.

t1voh0i2.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Zug
