teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Zug is very simple: it is white and has a blue horizontal bar in the middle. Precisely because it is so plain, it is easy to recognise.
wichtigste: The Zug coat of arms is white.
In the middle lies a horizontal blue bar.
White and blue are the cantonal colours of Zug.
The town of Zug and the canton of Zug have the same coat of arms.
Zug has been part of the Confederation since 1352.
The main town is called the same as the canton: Zug.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: On a **white ground** lies a broad **blue bar**. It runs **horizontally** through the middle, from left to right. Experts say: “In silver a blue fess”. There are no other pictures or animals. Such a simple coat of arms is easy to draw and to recognise from far away.

The coat of arms of the town of Zug can already be found on old **seals** from the Middle Ages. Where it comes from exactly is not known for certain. It is often assumed that it has to do with the former lords of the area. Later the town's coat of arms also became the **coat of arms of the whole canton**.

Zug joined the **Confederation** in **1352**. This makes Zug one of the old members of Switzerland. At festivals you see the white and blue flag next to the Swiss flag. On car number plates are the letters **ZG**.

The canton of Zug lies between **Zurich**, **Lucerne** and **Schwyz**. It is one of the **smallest cantons** in Switzerland. In the middle of the canton lies **Lake Zug**, and the highest point is the **Wildspitz**. Many companies have their headquarters in Zug.

gewusst: The cantons of Lucerne and Zurich also have blue and white in their coats of arms, but arranged differently.
The Zug cherry cake is a well-known speciality from the canton with the blue and white coat of arms.

t1we3l07.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Aargau

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Aargau is divided into two halves. On the left a white river flows over a black ground, on the right three white stars stand on a blue ground.
wichtigste: The Aargau coat of arms is divided vertically into two halves.
On the left is a white, wavy river on black.
On the right are three white stars on blue.
The river stands for the Aare.
The coat of arms came about in 1803, when the canton was founded.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: The **coat of arms of the canton of Aargau** is divided vertically into two halves. On the left side a **white, wavy river** flows over a **black** ground. On the right side stand **three white stars** on a **blue** ground. The canton's flag looks exactly the same.

The river stands for the **Aare**, which also gave the canton its name. The three stars are often interpreted as the areas from which the canton was put together. But there are different opinions about the exact meaning. What is clear: the coat of arms was meant to show something new and not to recall old rulers.

The canton of Aargau was founded in **1803**. At that time Napoleon reorganised Switzerland with the Act of Mediation. Areas that had previously belonged to others became a canton of their own. At the same time Aargau received its new coat of arms. The main town is **Aarau**.

gewusst: Together with St Gallen, Graubünden, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud, Aargau is one of the cantons that were newly created in 1803.

teile.einleitung: The Tödi is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus. It is around 3,600 metres high and stands on the border with the canton of Graubünden. Because of its size it is often called the “king of the Glarus Alps”.
wichtigste: The Tödi is around 3,600 metres high.
It is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus.
It lies on the border between Glarus and Graubünden.
There are large glaciers on the Tödi.
The Linth rises near it.

abschnitte.text: The Tödi has several peaks. The highest is called **Piz Russein** and is **3,614 metres** high. The mountain is so broad and massive that you can recognise it from many directions. It belongs to the **Glarus Alps**. Its flanks are covered with **glaciers**, which are getting smaller, as everywhere in the Alps.

The border between the **canton of Glarus** and the **canton of Graubünden** runs over the Tödi. On the Glarus side lies the valley of **Linthal**. On the Graubünden side lies the Surselva with the village of **Disentis**. Very close to the mountain rises the **Linth**, the most important river in the canton of Glarus.

The Tödi was first climbed in **1824**. Even today the ascent is demanding. You have to cross glaciers and need good **mountaineering equipment**. Along the route there are **mountain huts** of the Swiss Alpine Club, where climbers spend the night. Without experience or a mountain guide you should not climb up there.

The meltwater from the glaciers flows down into the valley. In the area around the Tödi, water is also used to generate **electricity**. There are reservoirs and power stations for this. A well-known example is the **Linth-Limmern power station** in the canton of Glarus.

gewusst: For the people of Glarus the Tödi is a landmark of their canton.
The name Tödi is very old, and its origin is not known for certain.

t1wibla4.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Landschaft

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Landschaft shows a red Basel crozier with small projections on a white ground. This clearly distinguishes it from the black Basel crozier of Basel-Stadt.
wichtigste: In the coat of arms of Basel-Landschaft is a red Basel crozier.
The ground is white.
On the staff are small projections, called crockets.
The Basel crozier of Basel-Stadt, by contrast, is black.
The canton of Basel-Landschaft was created in 1833.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Basel-Landschaft** you can see a **red Basel crozier** on a **white** ground. On the curved part of the staff sit small projections. They are called **crockets**. The staff is turned the other way from the one in the coat of arms of Basel-Stadt. This way you can tell at a glance which canton is meant.

In the past the town and the countryside belonged together in the canton of Basel. But the people in the countryside felt disadvantaged because the town had more say. After disputes and fighting, the two separated in **1833**. This is how the half-cantons of **Basel-Stadt** and **Basel-Landschaft** came about. The main town of Basel-Landschaft is **Liestal**.

The **Basel crozier** recalls the staff of the former Bishop of Basel. Basel-Stadt kept the **black** staff. Basel-Landschaft chose a **red** staff with crockets. The coat of arms of the town of Liestal is also red and white. So the coat of arms shows the link with the city of Basel and yet its independence.

gewusst: The crozier in the Basel-Landschaft coat of arms faces the other way from the one of Basel-Stadt, so the two seem to be turning their backs on each other.

t1wjz6a0.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Graubünden

teile.einleitung: The ibex is the well-known heraldic animal of the canton of Graubünden. In the Graubünden coat of arms it stands beside the signs of two other old leagues, and in the Graubünden mountains it also lives in real life.
wichtigste: The well-known heraldic animal of Graubünden is the ibex.
The Graubünden coat of arms has three parts.
The three parts stand for three old leagues.
The ibex belonged to the League of God's House.
The ibex climbs skilfully on steep rocks.
It was almost extinct in Switzerland and was reintroduced.

abschnitte.titel: A coat of arms with three parts
abschnitte.text: The coat of arms of **Graubünden** consists of three parts. Each part stands for one of the three old **leagues**: the **Grey League**, the **League of God's House** and the **League of the Ten Jurisdictions**. These leagues joined together a long time ago. Later the canton of Graubünden grew out of them. It has belonged to Switzerland since 1803.

abschnitte.titel: The ibex in the coat of arms
abschnitte.text: The **ibex** is the sign of the **League of God's House**. It stands upright and black on a white ground. Because it is so striking, it is known as the **heraldic animal** of the whole of Graubünden. You can see it, for example, on car number plates and on the trains of the Rhaetian Railway.

The **Alpine ibex** lives high in the mountains. It has strong legs and hooves with a firm, rough sole. That is why it **climbs** very skilfully on steep rocks. The males have long, curved **horns** with ridges. In summer the animals climb high up, in winter they look for sunny slopes.

In the 19th century the ibex was **wiped out** in Switzerland because it had been hunted too heavily. From **1911** animals were brought back into the Swiss mountains and set free. Today many ibex live in the Alps again, including in Graubünden. Hunting is strictly regulated.

gewusst: Ibex can climb almost vertical rock walls and even dam walls to lick salt from the stone.
The first ibex for the reintroduction in Switzerland came from a wildlife park in St Gallen.

teile.einleitung: In the Swiss mountains there are hundreds of small and large lakes. Many lie in hollows that glaciers shaped in the Ice Age. Mountain lakes are popular walking destinations because the peaks are reflected in them.
wichtigste: The water in mountain lakes is usually very cold.
Many mountain lakes freeze over in winter.
Many mountain lakes formed in hollows that glaciers ground out.
The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein, the Bachalpsee near First above Grindelwald.
The Caumasee near Flims shines turquoise.
On passes there are lakes such as the Daubensee, the Lago Bianco and the Totensee.

abschnitte.text: In the **Ice Age** large glaciers covered the Alps. They ground **hollows** into the rock. When the ice melted, these hollows filled with water. Other lakes came about because moraines or rockslides blocked a valley. A **moraine** is a ridge of stones and debris that a glacier has left behind.

Mountain lakes lie high up, where it is cool. Often **meltwater** from snow and glaciers flows into them. That is why the water is usually very cold, even in summer. In winter a thick **layer of ice** forms on many mountain lakes, and snow often covers them for months.

The **Seealpsee** lies in the Alpstein in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, below the Ebenalp. You reach it on foot from Wasserauen. The **Bachalpsee** lies near the viewpoint First above Grindelwald, at around 2,265 metres above sea level. In its water the mountains of the Bernese Oberland are reflected. In the forest near Flims lies the **Caumasee**, which is fed by underground springs and shines turquoise.

On some passes there are lakes right beside the road or the path. The **Daubensee** lies on the Gemmi Pass between Kandersteg and Leukerbad and has no visible outflow. On the Bernina Pass in Graubünden lies the **Lago Bianco**, which means “white lake”. On the Grimsel, between Bern and the Valais, lies the **Totensee** (“Lake of the Dead”) with its eerie name.

gewusst: Many mountain lakes are so clear that in calm weather you can see the mountains in them as in a mirror.
Some mountain lakes were enlarged with dams in order to produce electricity from hydropower.

teile.einleitung: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the Original Cantons. According to tradition, they were the first to join together in 1291. In time this alliance grew into the Confederation and later into present-day Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Original Cantons are Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden.
Today Unterwalden consists of Obwalden and Nidwalden.
The Federal Charter of 1291 is regarded as an important early alliance.
According to legend, their representatives swore an oath on the Rütli.
The name “Switzerland” comes from the canton of Schwyz.
The Original Cantons are also called the Forest Cantons (Waldstätte).

abschnitte.text: In the **Federal Charter** of **1291** the valley communities of **Uri**, **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden** promised to help one another. They wanted to defend themselves together against foreign rulers and against strife. The Federal Charter is written in **Latin**. Today it is kept in the **Federal Charters Museum** in Schwyz. The 1st of August, the **national holiday**, recalls this alliance.

According to **legend**, representatives of the three valley communities met on the **Rütli meadow** on Lake Uri. There they are said to have sworn an **oath** to stand by one another. This story is called the **Rütli Oath**. Whether it happened exactly like this is not proved. Even so, the Rütli meadow is an important place of remembrance in Switzerland.

The Original Cantons are also called the **Waldstätte** (Forest Cantons). They lie around the lake, which is therefore called **Lake Lucerne** (in German: Vierwaldstättersee, “Lake of the Four Forest Cantons”). Later Lucerne was added as the fourth place. **Unterwalden** was divided into two parts early on: **Obwalden** and **Nidwalden**. Today they are two separate cantons with one seat each in the Council of States.

In time further places joined the alliance, for example **Lucerne**, **Zurich** and **Bern**. This is how the **Old Swiss Confederacy** came about. Other peoples soon called all the Confederates after the canton of **Schwyz**. From this came the name **Switzerland**. The Swiss flag also recalls the red banner of Schwyz.

gewusst: The Federal Charter of 1291 is not the only early alliance, but in the 19th century it was declared the most important founding document.
The coat of arms of Schwyz is red with a small white cross.

teile.einleitung: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Council and Parliament work here. The old town of Bern with its arcades and fountains belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: Bern is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament and is officially called the federal city.
In 1848 Bern was chosen as the seat of the federal authorities.
The Aare flows around the old town in a tight loop.
The heraldic animal of Bern is the bear.
The Zytglogge is a famous clock tower with moving figures.
In November the Zibelemärit takes place.

abschnitte.text: The Federal Constitution names no capital. But Bern is the seat of the **Federal Council** and **Parliament** and is therefore called the **federal city**. After the founding of the federal state in 1848, the Federal Assembly chose Bern in the same year as the seat of the federal authorities. In the **Federal Palace** the National Council and the Council of States meet, and the Federal Council also has its rooms there. The Federal Council is the government of Switzerland and has **seven members**.

abschnitte.titel: An old town in the loop of the Aare
abschnitte.text: The **old town** lies on a rocky ridge. The **Aare** flows in a tight loop almost entirely around it. Typical are the **arcades**: covered pavements under which you can shop in the dry even when it rains. In addition there are many old fountains with colourful figures. Since 1983 the old town of Bern has belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

In the **coat of arms** of Bern a black bear walks on a yellow ground. The bear is the emblem of the city. For centuries Bern has kept live bears. In the past they lived in the **Bear Pit**. Today they live in the larger **Bear Park** right next to it on the bank of the Aare.

The **Zytglogge** is an old tower in the middle of the old town. It used to be a city gate. Today it has an **astronomical clock** that also shows the position of the sun and moon. Shortly before every full hour **figures** move, for example a cockerel and little bears. Many visitors wait in front of it to see the show.

Every year in **November** Bern celebrates the **Zibelemärit**. “Zibele” is Bernese German for onion. Market traders then sell a great many **onions**, often plaited artistically into braids. Onion tart and little confetti battles in the lanes belong to it too.

gewusst: The old town of Bern has over six kilometres of arcades in total.
In summer many people in Bern swim in the Aare and let the current carry them.

teile.einleitung: A biosphere reserve is an area in which people live and work while protecting nature. The title is awarded by UNESCO. In Switzerland there are such areas in the Entlebuch and in the Engadine with the Val Müstair.
wichtigste: Biosphere reserves belong to the UNESCO programme “Man and the Biosphere” (MAB).
They are divided into a core zone, a maintenance zone and a development zone.
The Swiss National Park became the first biosphere reserve in Switzerland in 1979.
The Entlebuch has been a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 2001.
The Biosfera Engiadina Val Müstair was finally recognised in 2017.

abschnitte.text: **UNESCO** is an organisation of the United Nations for education, science and culture. Around 1970 it started the programme **“Man and the Biosphere”**, abbreviated **MAB**. It links biosphere reserves all over the world. The aim: to **protect nature** and at the same time to **farm and work sustainably**, that is, to use nature in such a way that it is preserved.

Every biosphere reserve has three zones. In the **core zone** nature has priority, and it is strictly protected. In the **maintenance zone** the landscape is used gently, for example through alpine farming. In the **development zone** people live and work. There new ideas for sustainable farming, tourism and trades are meant to arise.

In **2001** UNESCO recognised the **Entlebuch Biosphere** in the canton of Lucerne. It was the first under UNESCO's renewed criteria. The Entlebuch is known for its large **bog landscapes**. Local products are sold there with a label of their own.

The **Swiss National Park** was declared the first biosphere reserve in Switzerland in **1979**. Later the **Val Müstair** and areas of the municipality of Scuol were added. Together they form the **Biosfera Engiadina Val Müstair**. The National Park is the strictly protected core zone. Final recognition came in June **2017**.

gewusst: Worldwide there are several hundred biosphere reserves in over a hundred countries.
In the Swiss National Park you must not leave the marked paths.

teile.einleitung: The Zuger Rötel is a fish from Lake Zug and a well-known speciality of the canton of Zug. It belongs to the chars and is easy to recognise by its reddish belly.
wichtigste: The Zuger Rötel is a lake char from Lake Zug.
It gets its name from its reddish belly.
It lives in the cool, deep water of the lake.
It is caught mainly in late autumn and winter.
It is regarded as a delicacy and is a pride of Zug cooking.

abschnitte.text: The Rötel is a **lake char**, that is, a close relative of the trout. Chars like cold, oxygen-rich water. That is why they usually stay at great depth. Especially at spawning time the belly of the fish glows strongly red to orange. That is where the name “Rötel” (from “rot”, red) comes from.

The **professional fishermen** on Lake Zug catch the Rötel with nets, mainly in the cold season. Because there are only a few Rötel, the fish is rare and in demand. In Zug restaurants it is served fried or gently poached. Many people in Zug look forward every year to the **Rötel season**.

In the past many nutrients from sewage and farming got into Lake Zug. As a result **oxygen** is often missing in the depths, and the Rötel finds less good habitat. So that it continues to exist, young Rötel are raised in a **fish hatchery** and released into the lake. Better sewage works also help the lake and its fish.

gewusst: The Zuger Rötel has been known as a fine food fish for centuries.
Without the help of the fish hatchery there would be far fewer Rötel in Lake Zug today.

teile.einleitung: The Uetliberg is the local mountain of the city of Zurich. It lies on the western edge of the city and is just under 870 metres high. From the top there is a wide view over the city, Lake Zurich and the Alps.
wichtigste: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain.
It is just under 870 metres high.
It belongs to the Albis chain.
A railway runs from Zurich main station almost to the summit.
On the summit stands a lookout tower.
A planet trail leads from the Uetliberg to the Felsenegg.

abschnitte.text: A **Hausberg** (“local mountain”) is a mountain so close to a city that many people can visit it quickly. For Zurich that is the **Uetliberg**. It belongs to the **Albis chain**, a chain of hills west of Lake Zurich. Its summit is called **Uto Kulm**. It is covered with forest and is a popular destination for outings.

From **Zurich main station** the **Uetliberg railway** runs in about 20 minutes to just below the summit. It is one of the steepest railways in Switzerland that runs without a rack. From the terminus you are at the top in a few minutes. But many people also walk up from the city.

On the summit stands a **lookout tower**. From there you can see the whole **city of Zurich** and **Lake Zurich**. In clear weather the view reaches far to the **Alps**. In autumn there is often **fog** over the valley while the sun shines at the top. Then it looks as if you were standing above a sea of clouds.

From the Uetliberg the **planet trail** leads along the ridge to the **Felsenegg**. Along the way stand models of the **Sun** and the planets. Their sizes and distances are scaled down accurately. So as you walk you realise how huge our solar system is. From the Felsenegg an aerial cable car runs down to Adliswil.

gewusst: In the Middle Ages there was a castle on the Uetliberg, of which only traces remain.
When there is snow, many people from Zurich go sledging on the Uetliberg.

t4irnpi.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau

teile.einleitung: Every Swiss canton has a coat of arms of its own. The coat of arms of the canton of Thurgau shows two yellow lions on a ground of white and green. It can be seen on the cantonal flag, on buildings and on documents of the canton.
wichtigste: The Thurgau coat of arms is divided diagonally.
The upper field is white, the lower green.
On each field a yellow, that is, golden, lion strides.
The two lions stand one above the other.
The lions recall the Counts of Kyburg, who ruled in Thurgau in the Middle Ages.
Thurgau has been a canton of its own since 1803, and its main town is Frauenfeld.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: The coat of arms is divided into two fields by a **diagonal line**. At the top the field is **white**, at the bottom **green**. In both fields a **yellow lion** strides. Experts in coats of arms often say “golden” instead of yellow and “silver” instead of white. The lions look to the left, that is, towards the flagpole.

In the Middle Ages the area of Thurgau long belonged to the sphere of power of the **Counts of Kyburg**. Their coat of arms also showed **two lions**. When Thurgau became a canton, the lions were taken over as a sign of the long history of the area. So the coat of arms tells something about the past.

Until 1798 Thurgau was a **subject territory**. That means it was ruled by other members of the Confederation and was not allowed to decide for itself. In **1803**, through the **Act of Mediation**, Thurgau became a canton with equal rights. At that time it also received its present coat of arms with the colours white and green.

abschnitte.titel: Where you see the coat of arms
abschnitte.text: The coat of arms can be seen on the **cantonal flag** in Frauenfeld and in many municipalities. It appears on letters and identity papers from the administration and on the canton's **car number plates** with the letters **TG**. At festivals and on 1 August many people in Thurgau hang flags next to the Swiss flag.

gewusst: The canton of Thurgau lies on Lake Constance and, because of its many fruit trees, is often called “Mostindien” (“Cider India”, from “Most”, the German word for apple cider).
The coat of arms of the city of Winterthur also shows two lions, because Winterthur too once belonged to the Counts of Kyburg.

teile.einleitung: The Zentralbahn is a railway in central Switzerland. It links Lucerne by way of Stans with Engelberg and, over the Brünig Pass, with Interlaken. Its trains run on narrow-gauge tracks.
wichtigste: The Zentralbahn runs from Lucerne by way of Stans to Engelberg.
A second line leads from Lucerne over the Brünig to Interlaken.
Its tracks are narrower than on most SBB lines.
This is called narrow gauge or metre gauge.
On steep sections a rack helps.
The Zentralbahn came about in 2005 from two older railways.

abschnitte.text: The **Zentralbahn** has two important lines. One leads from **Lucerne** through the canton of **Nidwalden** by way of **Stans** to **Engelberg** in the canton of Obwalden. The other leads from Lucerne by way of **Sarnen** and the **Brünig Pass** to **Meiringen** and **Interlaken**. Many commuters and day-trippers ride these trains.

The tracks of the Zentralbahn are only **one metre** wide. This is called **metre gauge** or **narrow gauge**. On most SBB lines the tracks are wider. Narrow tracks are good for **mountain lines**, because the trains can take tighter curves. That is why SBB trains cannot run on the tracks of the Zentralbahn.

On some sections it is so **steep** that ordinary wheels would slip. There a **rack** lies between the rails. A **cogwheel** on the train grips into it and pulls the train up the mountain. This is how the train manages the way over the **Brünig** and up to **Engelberg**.

In the past there were two railways: the **Brünig Railway** of the SBB and the railway from **Lucerne by way of Stans to Engelberg**. In **2005** they were merged into the **Zentralbahn**. Since then a lot has been built, for example a new **tunnel** before Engelberg. It makes the journey up faster and flatter.

gewusst: Part of the line in Lucerne runs underground to the station.
In Engelberg you can change from the Zentralbahn straight to the mountain railways up the Titlis.

teile.einleitung: Biel/Bienne is the largest bilingual city in Switzerland. In everyday life people speak German and French here. The city lies on Lake Biel at the foot of the Jura and is a centre of the watch industry.
wichtigste: Biel/Bienne lies at the north-eastern end of Lake Biel.
Behind the city rises the Jura.
In Biel people speak German and French, and the street signs are bilingual.
Biel is a centre of the Swiss watch industry.
The Schüss flows through the city into Lake Biel.
In 2002 Biel was one of the sites of the national exhibition Expo.02.

abschnitte.text: In **Biel/Bienne** many people speak **German**, many others **French**. That is why the city has two names. The **street signs** are written in both languages. In shops and on the street people often switch quite naturally from one language to the other. In 2023, with around 56,000 inhabitants, Biel was the **tenth largest city** in Switzerland.

Biel is an important centre of the **watch industry**. Several well-known watch brands have their seat or their factories here. In the 19th century many watchmakers came to the city from the Jura. As a result Biel grew strongly, and many French-speaking families moved in too.

The city lies at the north-eastern end of **Lake Biel**. Behind it the hills of the **Jura** rise steeply, and in front of the city lies the flatter Central Plateau. The **Schüss** comes from the Jura, flows through Biel and enters the lake. Right next to Biel lies the little town of **Nidau** with its castle close to the lakeshore.

Above Biel lies **Magglingen**, in French Macolin. There the **Federal Office of Sport** has its seat, with a sports university and many training facilities. In **2002** Biel was one of the four sites of the national exhibition **Expo.02**. The others were Neuchâtel, Murten and Yverdon-les-Bains, and each city had an exhibition site of its own on the water.

gewusst: A funicular runs from Biel up to Magglingen.
In Biel many children go to school in their own language, but there are also bilingual classes.

teile.einleitung: The Seerücken is a long, wooded ridge of hills in the canton of Thurgau. It lies between the Untersee, part of Lake Constance, and the valley of the Thur.
wichtigste: The Seerücken is in the canton of Thurgau.
It stretches along the southern shore of the Untersee.
It separates the Lake Constance area from the valley of the Thur.
The ridge is covered with woods, meadows, orchards and small villages.
It was shaped by glaciers in the ice age.

abschnitte.text: The **Seerücken** is a long ridge of hills in the north of the **canton of Thurgau**. On one side it slopes down to the **Untersee**, on the other to the **Thur valley**. Its shape recalls a back, which is where the name comes from (“Rücken” means back, “See” means lake). It is not very high, but you can see it from far away. From its viewpoints you can look across the lake as far as Germany.

The Seerücken was shaped by the **glaciers of the ice age**. At that time the Rhine glacier reached far into Thurgau. It pushed rubble and sand ahead of it and smoothed the landscape. When the ice melted, hills and hollows were left behind. In some hollows small lakes and bogs formed.

On the Seerücken there are many **farms**, **woods** and **orchards**. Thurgau is known for its apples and is often called “**Mostindien**” (“Cider India”). At the foot of the Seerücken, on the Untersee, lie places such as **Steckborn** and **Ermatingen**. On the slope above Mannenbach stands **Arenenberg Castle** with the Napoleon Museum.

gewusst: The Seerücken is good for walking and cycling, with views of Lake Constance.
The Untersee is the smaller, western part of Lake Constance.

teile.einleitung: The Tectonic Arena Sardona is a mountain area in the cantons of Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden. Since 2008 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site, because you can see there especially well how mountains are formed.
wichtigste: The Tectonic Arena Sardona lies in Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden.
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.
There, older layers of rock lie on top of younger ones.
This feature is called the Glarus Main Thrust.
Also well known is the Martinsloch, a hole in a rock wall.

abschnitte.text: Normally **younger layers of rock** lie on top and older ones underneath. In the Tectonic Arena Sardona it is the other way round. There, very old rock was pushed over much younger rock. This line is called the **Glarus Main Thrust**. On many mountains you can see it as a clear line in the rock face.

The Alps were formed because two great **tectonic plates** moved against each other. In the process, layers of rock were pushed together, folded and stacked on top of each other. This movement is called **tectonics**. It lasted for millions of years. In the Tectonic Arena Sardona you can see this process on the surface especially well.

As early as the 19th century, geologists studied these mountains. For a long time they argued about how old rock could end up on young rock. The explanation of the **thrust** helped to give a better understanding of how the Alps were formed. That is why the area is known worldwide for **geology**.

In the **Tschingelhörner** above Elm in the canton of Glarus there is a large hole in the rock, the **Martinsloch**. On a few days in spring and autumn the sun shines through this hole. Its light then falls exactly on the church tower of **Elm**. Many people come to see this spectacle.

gewusst: The name Sardona comes from the Piz Sardona, a mountain in the area.
The Tectonic Arena Sardona was the first UNESCO World Heritage Site in the canton of Glarus.

teile.einleitung: The Alpabzug (descent from the alp) is a festival in autumn. After the summer the cows come back from the alp into the valley. They are beautifully decorated, and many people watch.
wichtigste: At the Alpabzug the cows return from the alp to the valley.
It mostly takes place in September.
The cows wear flowers, ribbons and big bells.
The lead cow goes at the front and is especially beautifully decorated.
In French-speaking Switzerland the Alpabzug is called “Désalpe”.
The cows spend the winter in the barn in the valley.

abschnitte.text: All summer the cows eat fresh grass on the **alp**. In autumn it gets cold in the mountains, snow soon falls, and hardly any grass grows. That is why the cows usually go back down to the valley in **September**. This move is called the **Alpabzug**.

At the Alpabzug many cows wear a **headdress** of flowers and coloured ribbons. At the front goes the **lead cow**, which leads the herd. She often wears the biggest decoration. Some cows wear **Treicheln**, which are large sheet-metal bells with a loud, deep sound.

The **herdsmen** and **alpine women** often wear their fine **traditional costume**. In the village many people wait at the roadside and watch. In some places there is music, food and a market. In French-speaking Switzerland the Alpabzug is called the **“Désalpe”**, and there too some villages hold a big festival.

After the Alpabzug the cows live at the **farm** in the valley again. In winter they stand in the **barn** and eat **hay**, that is, dried grass from the summer. In the next early summer they go up again, at the **Alpaufzug** (the ascent to the alp).

gewusst: Treicheln are forged from sheet metal, whereas bells are cast.

teile.einleitung: The Alpine Rhine Valley is the wide valley through which the Alpine Rhine flows to Lake Constance. It lies between Switzerland, Liechtenstein and Austria. A glacier shaped it in the Ice Age.
wichtigste: The Alpine Rhine flows into Lake Constance between Altenrhein and Hard.
On the Swiss side lies the canton of St Gallen.
Dornbirn in the Austrian part is the largest city in Vorarlberg.
At the mouth lies the Rhine Delta nature reserve.
Ribel is a maize speciality from the Rhine Valley.
Dams and cuttings protect the valley from floods.

abschnitte.titel: A valley from the Ice Age
abschnitte.text: In the Ice Ages the mighty **Rhine Glacier** flowed through the valley to Lake Constance. It planed out a broad, flat **trough valley**. Today the **Alpine Rhine** flows north through this plain. Between **Altenrhein** and **Hard** it flows into **Lake Constance**.

On the Swiss side, from the Sarganserland to Lake Constance, lies the canton of **St Gallen**, with places such as **Buchs** and **Altstätten**. Altstätten has a lovely old town with **arcades**. Further up the valley borders **Liechtenstein**. In the Austrian part lies **Dornbirn**, the largest city of the federal state of Vorarlberg.

In the past the Rhine flooded the valley again and again. That is why in the 19th and 20th centuries it was **straightened** and enclosed with **dams**. At **Diepoldsau** and **Fussach** **cuttings** were made: the river was given a new, straight bed. Switzerland and Austria have worked together on this for a long time.

At the mouth lies the **Rhine Delta** nature reserve. It lies in Vorarlberg between the old and the new mouth of the Rhine. There are reeds, reed meadows and shallow water. For **migratory birds** it is an important resting place.

A speciality of the Rhine Valley is **Ribel**. It is made from **Rheintaler Ribelmais** (Rhine Valley Ribel maize), which is protected as **AOP**. The maize grits are cooked and then roasted in a pan into crumbs. In the past Ribel was a simple everyday meal.

gewusst: Because the Rhine was diverted, there is today an old and a new mouth of the Rhine.
Over long stretches the Alpine Rhine forms the border of Switzerland with Liechtenstein and with Austria.

teile.einleitung: Many Swiss cities have a well-preserved old town from the Middle Ages or the Baroque period. There you find narrow lanes, fountains, towers and old walls. Some old towns even belong to the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: The old town of Bern has been UNESCO World Heritage since 1983.
In Lucerne stands the Museggmauer with nine towers.
The little town of Gruyères gave Gruyère cheese its name.
Aarau is called the “city of beautiful gables”.
The abbey district of St Gallen with its library is World Heritage.
Solothurn is the city of the number 11.

abschnitte.text: The **old town of Bern** lies in a loop of the **Aare**. It has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 1983. Typical are the long **arcades** under which you can shop in the dry. The bilingual city of **Fribourg** has a large old town on a rock above the **Sarine**, with many bridges and houses from the Middle Ages.

In **Lucerne** the **Museggmauer** with nine towers used to protect the old town. You can climb some of the towers. In **Zug** in 1887 houses on the lakeshore slid into the lake, and the disaster is called the **Vorstadt disaster** (“suburb disaster”). In **Zurich** the **Niederdorf** with its narrow lanes and pubs is well known, and people in Zurich also call it the “Dörfli” (little village).

In **St Gallen** stands the **abbey district**, which belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage. Its **Abbey Library** is over 1,000 years old. **Solothurn** has a lovely **Baroque old town**. The city loves the number **11**: there are, for example, 11 churches and chapels and 11 fountains.

The little town of **Gruyères** with its castle lies on a hill in the canton of Fribourg. The cheese **Gruyère** is named after this area. In the old town of **Aarau** the undersides of the roofs are brightly painted. That is why Aarau is called the **“city of beautiful gables”**.

gewusst: In the old town of Bern there are kilometres of arcades, one of the longest covered shopping streets in Europe.
In the Abbey Library of St Gallen you put on felt slippers to protect the old wooden floor.

teile.einleitung: Walchwil is a municipality in the canton of Zug. It lies on a sunny slope on the eastern shore of Lake Zug, at the foot of the Rossberg.
wichtigste: Walchwil is in the canton of Zug.
The municipality lies on the eastern shore of Lake Zug.
It lies at the foot of the Rossberg.
The slope is sunny and the climate mild.
The railway line from Zug to Arth-Goldau runs through Walchwil.

abschnitte.text: **Walchwil** lies on the **eastern shore of Lake Zug**, between the town of Zug and Arth. The village climbs a steep slope from the shore. Above it rise the **Zugerberg** and the **Rossberg**. From the village you can see far across the lake to the Rigi.

Because the slope faces west, the sun shines in Walchwil until the evening. The lake stores warmth and makes the climate **mild**. That is why plants that generally like it warm grow here, for example **sweet chestnuts**. Many people like living here because of the lovely view.

On the lakeshore the **railway line** from Zug to Arth-Goldau runs through Walchwil. A road also runs along the lake. So you can quickly reach Zug or central Switzerland. On the shore there are swimming spots and a small harbour.

gewusst: From Walchwil you can see across Lake Zug to the Rigi.

teile.einleitung: The Tell Plays Altdorf are a theatre in the main town of the canton of Uri. Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell” is performed there, acted mainly by people from the region.
wichtigste: The Tell Plays take place in Altdorf in the canton of Uri.
The play performed is Schiller's “William Tell”.
The Tell Plays have existed since 1899.
They are performed in their own theatre, the Tellspielhaus.
The actors are mostly amateurs from the region.

abschnitte.text: The **Tell Plays Altdorf** were founded in **1899**. Since then Schiller's **“William Tell”** has been staged again and again in Altdorf. The performances do not take place every year but at intervals of a few years. Every new season is staged afresh, that is, newly rehearsed and designed.

For the performances Altdorf has a theatre of its own, the **Tellspielhaus**. It was built in the 1920s. The performers rehearse and play here. Many of them are **amateurs**, that is, not professional actors. They live in the canton of Uri and take part in their free time.

**Friedrich Schiller** was a famous German poet. His play “William Tell” was first performed in **1804**. It tells the legend of the shot at the apple and of the struggle of the people of central Switzerland against the bailiffs. Schiller himself was never in Switzerland. Even so, his play has shaped the image of Tell to this day.

Altdorf is closely linked to the **Tell legend**. According to tradition, the **shot at the apple** took place here. On the village square stands a large **Tell Monument** from 1895. It shows Tell with his crossbow and his son Walter.

gewusst: Schiller's “William Tell” is also performed in other places, for example in Interlaken.
A well-known line from the play is: “Through this hollow way he must come.”

teile.einleitung: The Untersee is the western part of Lake Constance. At its end the Rhine leaves the lake at Stein am Rhein. From Schaffhausen you can travel by boat up the Rhine to the Untersee.
wichtigste: Lake Constance consists of the Obersee and the Untersee.
The Untersee lies between Switzerland and Germany.
On the Swiss shore lies the canton of Thurgau.
At Stein am Rhein the Rhine flows out of the Untersee.
In the Untersee lies the island of Reichenau, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Boats run between Schaffhausen, Stein am Rhein and the Untersee.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Constance** consists of two large parts: the **Obersee** (Upper Lake) and the **Untersee** (Lower Lake). At **Konstanz** they are linked by a short stretch of the Rhine, the **Seerhein**. The Untersee is smaller and less deep than the Obersee. It has many bays and peninsulas. The southern shore belongs to the **canton of Thurgau**, the northern shore to Germany.

From **Schaffhausen** passenger boats travel up the **Rhine**. On the way they pass Diessenhofen and **Stein am Rhein**. Then they reach the **Untersee** and continue as far as **Kreuzlingen** and Konstanz. The journey passes woods, castles and old little towns. It is regarded as one of the most beautiful **river trips** in Europe.

In the Untersee lies the island of **Reichenau**. It belongs to Germany. In the Middle Ages an important **monastery** stood there. Some old churches from that time have survived to this day. That is why the island is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Today a lot of **vegetables** are grown on the Reichenau.

On the Swiss shore lie places such as **Steckborn**, **Ermatingen** and **Berlingen**. They have old houses and small harbours. **Stein am Rhein** is famous for its painted houses in the old town. Above the Untersee, on the Seerücken, stands the **Napoleon Museum at Arenenberg**.

gewusst: Many water birds rest on the Untersee in winter.
The Rhine first flows into Lake Constance and comes out again at the Untersee.

teile.einleitung: The Spreuer Bridge is an old covered wooden bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne. It is famous for its paintings of a dance of death from the 17th century.
wichtigste: The Spreuer Bridge crosses the Reuss in Lucerne.
It is a covered wooden bridge from the Middle Ages.
Besides the Chapel Bridge it is Lucerne's second old wooden bridge.
Under the roof hang paintings of a dance of death from the 17th century.
They were painted by Kaspar Meglinger with his workshop.

abschnitte.text: The **Spreuer Bridge** crosses the **Reuss** just before it leaves Lucerne. It is built of wood and has a **roof**. It was built in the early 15th century and was part of the town's fortifications. The bridge is slightly angled and runs across an old weir. In the middle stands a small **chapel**.

The name has to do with **chaff** (“Spreu”). Chaff is the husks and remains left over when grain is threshed. In the past, chaff and leaves could only be thrown into the Reuss from this bridge. In this way the water carried the waste out of the town. It was forbidden from the other bridges.

Under the roof hang triangular **wooden panels** with paintings. They were painted in the **17th century** by the painter **Kaspar Meglinger** and his workshop. The pictures show a **dance of death**. In them Death appears as a skeleton to people of all ranks: kings, farmers, merchants and children. The message is: in the face of death all people are equal.

abschnitte.titel: The sister of the Chapel Bridge
abschnitte.text: The better-known wooden bridge in Lucerne is the **Chapel Bridge** with its water tower. It largely burned down in **1993** and was rebuilt. The Spreuer Bridge, by contrast, has been preserved in its old form. Both bridges are landmarks of Lucerne and are visited by many tourists.

gewusst: Dances of death were a popular subject for pictures across Europe in the Middle Ages and the early modern period.
The Spreuer Bridge is one of the oldest surviving wooden bridges in Europe.

teile.einleitung: St Moritz is a famous holiday resort in the Upper Engadine in the canton of Graubünden. It twice hosted the Winter Olympic Games and is world-famous for winter sports.
wichtigste: St Moritz lies in the Upper Engadine in the canton of Graubünden.
The resort lies at around 1,800 metres above sea level on Lake St Moritz.
The Winter Olympic Games took place here in 1928 and 1948.
St Moritz is regarded as the birthplace of winter tourism in the Alps.
The natural-ice bobsleigh run and the horse races on the frozen lake are well known.

abschnitte.text: **St Moritz** lies in the **Upper Engadine** in the canton of **Graubünden**. The resort is at around **1,800 metres** above sea level on a lake. High mountains rise all around, and the climate is dry and sunny. In the Engadine people speak **Romansh** as well as German. In Romansh the place is called **San Murezzan**.

abschnitte.titel: The invention of the winter holiday
abschnitte.text: In the past guests only travelled to St Moritz in summer, mainly for the **mineral springs**. In **1864** the hotelier **Johannes Badrutt** invited English guests to come in winter. If they did not like it, they would not have to pay anything, or so the story goes. The guests stayed until spring. Since then St Moritz has been regarded as the **birthplace of winter tourism** in the Alps.

St Moritz hosted the **Winter Olympic Games** in **1928** and **1948**. Few places in the world have hosted the Winter Games twice. Later, **Alpine ski world championships** were also held here several times. The **bobsleigh run** from St Moritz to Celerina is rebuilt every year from **natural ice**. Also well known is the **Cresta Run**, an ice track for sledges that you ride head first.

In winter **Lake St Moritz** freezes over. Then special events take place on the ice. At the **White Turf**, horses gallop across the snow-covered lake. There are also polo matches and other events on the ice. In summer you can walk, cycle and sail on the lakes in the area.

gewusst: In St Moritz there is a leaning church tower that tilts more than some famous towers.
One of the first electric lights in Switzerland burned in St Moritz, in a hotel.

teile.einleitung: By “Bergflucht” (flight from the mountains) we mean that many people move away from the mountain areas, above all young people. They look for work and training in the valley or in the cities. For decades the Confederation, the cantons and foundations have been trying to slow down this development.
wichtigste: Bergflucht is out-migration from mountain areas.
Often jobs, schools and shops are lacking in the village.
When mostly young people leave, the village population gets older.
The Investment Aid Act of 1974 helped mountain municipalities with cheap loans.
Since 2008 there has been the Confederation's New Regional Policy (NRP).
Since 1943 the Swiss Mountain Aid has supported people in the mountain area.
Tourist resorts such as Zermatt or Davos, by contrast, are growing.

abschnitte.text: In remote valleys there are often few **jobs** and long distances. Young people study in the city and find suitable jobs there. When well-educated people leave a region, it is called **brain drain**. If the **village school** then closes as well, children have to make long journeys to school. For young families the village becomes less attractive, and even more people move away.

If mostly older people stay behind, **ageing of the population** results. Fewer children are born, and the village shrinks further. Shops, the post office and inns close because customers are lacking. Clubs and the fire brigade also find it harder to get members.

In 1974 the **Investment Aid Act (IHG)** came into force. It gave mountain municipalities low-interest loans for roads, schools and water supplies. Since **2008** the Confederation has promoted the economy in mountain areas and rural regions with the **New Regional Policy (NRP)**. It supports new ideas and projects that create work and income there.

The foundation **Swiss Mountain Aid** has supported mountain farmers, businesses and municipalities since 1943. In Ticino there is the idea of the **Albergo diffuso**: empty houses are renovated and used as hotel rooms, with a shared reception. In this way guests come into the village, and the houses do not fall into ruin.

In places such as **Zermatt** or **Davos** there are many jobs in hotels, mountain railways and trades. There the population is even growing. A problem, however, is **cold beds**: holiday flats that stand empty for most of the year. **Warm beds**, by contrast, are accommodation such as hotels that are let regularly.

gewusst: The opposite of Bergflucht exists too: some people deliberately move to mountain villages and work from there over the internet.
Since the acceptance of the Second Homes Initiative in 2012, municipalities with many second homes may hardly build any new ones.

teile.einleitung: In the canton of Aargau three large rivers meet: the Aare, the Reuss and the Limmat. Because so much water from half of Switzerland comes together here, the area is called the “Wasserschloss” (“water castle”) of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Wasserschloss lies near Brugg, Windisch and Gebenstorf in the canton of Aargau.
Here the Reuss and the Limmat flow into the Aare.
Together the three rivers bring water from a large part of Switzerland.
The area is a valuable floodplain landscape with many animals and plants.
Not far away lay the Roman legionary camp of Vindonissa.
Later the Aare flows into the Rhine at Koblenz AG.

abschnitte.text: The **Aare** comes from the Bernese Oberland, the **Reuss** from the Gotthard by way of Lake Lucerne and the **Limmat** from Lake Zurich. Within a few kilometres the Reuss and the Limmat flow into the Aare at **Brugg** and **Windisch**. After that the Aare is much bigger. The water comes from a **large part of Switzerland**.

A **Wasserschloss** is really a castle surrounded by water. Here the word is a **picture**: just as in a castle many passages come together, so the great rivers meet here. The name shows how important this spot is for the water of Switzerland.

At the Wasserschloss there are **floodplains**. These are landscapes beside a river that are flooded again and again. Willows and other trees that can cope with wet feet grow there. Many **birds**, **fish** and **amphibians** find a habitat here. That is why the area is under **nature protection**.

The **Romans** already saw how important this place was. In **Windisch** they built the **legionary camp of Vindonissa**, where thousands of soldiers lived. Very close by also stands **Habsburg Castle**, the ancestral castle of the Habsburgs. The rivers were important routes for trade in the past.

gewusst: The Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.
At Koblenz in Aargau the Aare often brings more water into the Rhine than the Rhine itself carries there.

teile.einleitung: The UNESCO Entlebuch Biosphere is a region in the canton of Lucerne. It was recognised as a biosphere reserve in 2001. The aim is to protect nature while living and working well within it.
wichtigste: The Entlebuch lies in the canton of Lucerne, between Lucerne and Bern.
Since 2001 it has been a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
It was the first biosphere reserve in Switzerland under UNESCO's new rules.
Typical features are bogs, forests and mountains such as the Schrattenflue.
Farming and tourism are meant to be in harmony with nature.

abschnitte.text: A **biosphere reserve** is an area honoured by **UNESCO**. Unlike in a national park, many people live and work there. The aim is for them to use nature **sustainably**. That means: in such a way that later generations can still live from it. Some parts of the area are strictly protected.

In the Entlebuch there are especially many **bogs**. Bogs are wet areas in which **peat** forms over a long time. Rare plants grow there, and many animals find a habitat. Also well known is the **Schrattenflue**, a limestone mountain with many grooves and holes in the rock. Such landscapes are called **karst**.

Many people in the Entlebuch work in **farming**, in trades or in **tourism**. Farms produce cheese, meat and other foods. Products from the region are sold with a label of their own. In this way more money stays in the valley, and the routes for the goods are short.

The Entlebuch is a popular area for **hiking**, and in winter for cross-country skiing and downhill skiing. There are themed trails on which you can learn a lot about bogs and nature. Well-known places are **Sörenberg** and **Flühli**. From the top station on the Brienzer Rothorn you have a wide view.

gewusst: Those entitled to vote in the Entlebuch themselves voted on whether their region should become a biosphere reserve.
Bogs store a great deal of carbon and are therefore also important for the climate.

teile.einleitung: The Verzasca Valley is a wild mountain valley in the canton of Ticino. It is known for the crystal-clear, green water of the Verzasca and for the old stone bridge Ponte dei Salti near Lavertezzo.
wichtigste: The Verzasca Valley lies in the canton of Ticino, north of Locarno.
The River Verzasca has very clear, green water.
At Lavertezzo stands the double-arched Ponte dei Salti.
At the entrance to the valley lies the Lago di Vogorno reservoir.
Sonogno is the last village in the valley.
Typical are old stone houses, the rustici.

abschnitte.text: The **Verzasca Valley** lies in **Ticino**, north of Locarno. The **Verzasca** flows through the valley. Its water is so clear that you can see right to the bottom, and it shimmers green. The river has shaped round, smooth rocks. The valley is narrow and steep, with forests and small villages.

At **Lavertezzo** the **Ponte dei Salti** spans the river. It is an old stone bridge with **two arches**. Because it is so beautiful, it is photographed very often. In summer many day-trippers come here. But the water is very cold and can be dangerous, because it can suddenly rise.

In the valley stand many **rustici**. These are old houses of grey stone, often with roofs of stone slabs. In the past people here lived from goats, cows and small fields. Many moved away because life was hard. The last village in the valley is **Sonogno**. Today the villages of the valley together form the municipality of Verzasca.

At the entrance to the valley lies the **Lago di Vogorno** reservoir. It is held back by a high **dam** at Contra. The water is used to generate electricity. The dam is also known because you can make a bungee jump into the depths from it.

gewusst: In a James Bond film a stuntman jumped from the Verzasca dam; since then it has been world-famous.
Corippo in the Verzasca Valley was for a long time the municipality with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Alpine Initiative was a popular initiative to protect the Alps from lorry traffic. It was accepted in 1994. Since then freight traffic through the Alps is meant to be moved onto the railway as far as possible.
wichtigste: The people and the cantons accepted the Alpine Initiative on 20 February 1994.
Freight traffic through the Alps is to be shifted from road to rail.
In Switzerland today the larger part of Alpine freight travels by rail.
The shift target was meant to be reached by 2018 but was missed.
Every two years the Federal Council reports on the state of things in the Modal Shift Report.
Lorries are counted at the Gotthard, San Bernardino, Simplon and Great St Bernard.

abschnitte.text: On 20 February 1994 the **people and the cantons** accepted the Alpine Initiative. Since then the **Federal Constitution** has said that freight traffic through the Alps from border to border is to go by rail. Supporters wanted to protect people and nature in the Alpine valleys from noise and exhaust fumes. Opponents feared disadvantages for the economy and quarrels with the neighbouring countries.

The **Freight Transport Modal Shift Act** sets how many lorry journeys at most are to go through the Alps. The target was meant to be reached at the latest two years after the opening of the **Gotthard Base Tunnel**, that is, by **2018**. The number of journeys did fall, but stayed above the target. Counting takes place at the four crossings **Gotthard**, **San Bernardino**, **Simplon** and **Great St Bernard**. Every two years the Federal Council reports in the **Modal Shift Report**.

In **combined transport**, lorry loads travel part of the way by rail. In **unaccompanied** combined transport only containers, swap bodies or semi-trailers are loaded, while the tractor unit and the driver stay behind. The Confederation pays **compensation** so that such rail services become cheaper. The rail share of freight traffic across the Alps has been around 70 per cent or more for years.

One idea was the **Alpine transit exchange**. In it the number of journeys would be limited, and the rights to drive through would be auctioned or traded. Because of the **Land Transport Agreement** with the EU, however, it was not introduced. What was introduced instead is the performance-related heavy vehicle charge, **LSVA** for short, which lorries pay depending on the route and the weight.

gewusst: In neighbouring countries such as Austria most Alpine freight goes by road, whereas in Switzerland it goes by rail.
By far the largest part of the lorries crossing the Swiss Alps go over the Gotthard.

teile.einleitung: The bear is the heraldic animal of the city of Bern. For centuries Bern has kept live bears in a pit. Today the animals live in the large **Bear Park** on the bank of the Aare, right next to the old **Bear Pit**.
wichtigste: In Bern there have been bear pits for over 500 years.
A first bear pit is known from the year 1441.
The present old bear pit is the fourth and lies by the Nydegg Bridge.
Since 2009 there has been the larger Bear Park on the slope to the Aare.
In the Bear Park live brown bears, which are omnivores.
In winter the bears have a winter rest.

abschnitte.text: The **bear** is the heraldic animal of Bern and also appears in the coat of arms of the canton. An old legend tells that the city was named after a bear. That is why Bern has kept live bears for a long time. A first **bear pit** is already known from the year **1441**. Since then the pit has been moved several times to a new place.

The present old Bear Pit is already the **fourth** in Bern. It lies at the end of the old town, right on the other side of the **Nydegg Bridge**. It is a deep, **round pit** with stone walls. Visitors look down on the bears from above. But for the animals the space was very tight.

So that the bears have more room, the **Bear Park** was built. It opened in **October 2009** and is connected to the old pit. The park lies on the steep slope down to the bank of the **Aare**. There the bears can climb, dig, bathe in the water and also hide for a while.

abschnitte.titel: The life of a brown bear
abschnitte.text: In the Bear Park live **brown bears**. This species also used to live in the forests of Switzerland. Brown bears are **omnivores**: they eat fruit, vegetables, nuts, fish and meat. In winter they sleep a lot and hardly eat. This is called **winter rest**. In spring they become more active again.

gewusst: Bern has kept live bears since the 15th century, that is, for over 500 years.
The present old Bear Pit is already the fourth bear pit of the city.

teile.einleitung: Lake Constance lies between Switzerland, Germany and Austria. It is one of the largest lakes in central Europe and is jokingly called the “Swabian Sea”. The Rhine flows through the lake.
wichtigste: Switzerland, Germany and Austria lie on Lake Constance.
It consists of the large Obersee and the smaller Untersee.
Of Switzerland, Thurgau, St Gallen and Schaffhausen border the lake.
For the Obersee there is no treaty about the borders.
The largest city on the lake is Konstanz.
In the winter of 1963 the whole lake was frozen over.

abschnitte.text: On Lake Constance lie **Germany**, **Austria** and **Switzerland**. The largest part of the Swiss shore belongs to **Thurgau**. St Gallen borders the Obersee, Schaffhausen the end of the Untersee. What is special: for the largest part of the lake, the **Obersee** (Upper Lake), there is **no treaty** about where the borders run. The countries have different views on this.

Lake Constance consists of two main parts: the large **Obersee** and the smaller **Untersee** (Lower Lake). At **Konstanz** they are joined by the **Seerhein**. Konstanz lies in Germany and is the largest city on the lake. It borders directly on the Thurgau town of **Kreuzlingen**. Because the lake is so big, you can sometimes hardly see the other shore. That is why it is called the **Swabian Sea**.

In Lake Constance lie well-known islands that belong to Germany. The **Mainau** is also called the **Flower Island**, because thousands of flowers bloom there. On the **Reichenau** in the Untersee, lettuce, tomatoes and other **vegetables** grow in fields and greenhouses. The monastery island of Reichenau belongs to the UNESCO World Heritage.

In **Friedrichshafen** Count **Ferdinand von Zeppelin** built large airships. They were named **Zeppelins** after him. On the Swiss shore in **Rorschach**, right by the harbour, stands the **Kornhaus** (granary). It was built from 1746 to 1749. Grain that was traded across Lake Constance was stored in it.

In the very cold winter of **1963** the whole of Lake Constance froze over. Such a **Seegfrörni** (a complete freezing of the lake) is very rare. The ice was so thick that people walked across the lake on foot. Some even walked from one country to another.

gewusst: Lake Constance supplies drinking water for several million people in southern Germany.
At the Seegfrörni of 1963 people carried a bust of a saint across the ice from one shore to the other, as an old custom requires.

teile.einleitung: Zermatt is a famous holiday resort in the canton of the Valais at the foot of the Matterhorn. The special thing: Zermatt is car-free. You travel there by train and get around the village in small electric vehicles.
wichtigste: Zermatt lies in the canton of the Valais.
Above the village rises the Matterhorn, 4,478 metres high.
No ordinary cars are allowed to drive in Zermatt.
Visitors travel there by train, and many change in Täsch.
In the village small electric vehicles and electric buses run.
Zermatt is the start or end of the Glacier Express.

abschnitte.titel: At the foot of the Matterhorn
abschnitte.text: **Zermatt** lies at the very end of the **Mattertal** (Matter Valley) in the canton of the **Valais**. Above the village stands the **Matterhorn** at **4,478 metres**. Its pointed shape is known all over the world. Around Zermatt there are many more **four-thousanders**. In winter many visitors come for **skiing**, in summer for **walking**.

In Zermatt **no ordinary cars** are allowed to drive. Anyone who comes by car leaves it in **Täsch** and travels on by **train**. In the village small **electric vehicles** run as taxis and delivery vans. The **buses** also run on electricity. This keeps the air cleaner and it is quieter.

Many **mountain railways** run from Zermatt. The **Gornergrat Railway** is a rack railway up to over 3,000 metres. A cable car goes up to the **Klein Matterhorn**, one of the highest mountain stations in Europe. The famous **Glacier Express** runs from Zermatt to **St Moritz** in the canton of Graubünden.

In **1865** a roped party stood on the summit of the Matterhorn for the first time. It was led by the Englishman **Edward Whymper**. On the descent four of the seven climbers were killed in an accident. The first ascent made Zermatt world-famous. A **museum** in the village tells of this history.

gewusst: On some glaciers above Zermatt you can even ski in summer.
The Matterhorn lies exactly on the border between Switzerland and Italy.

teile.einleitung: In the city of Fribourg runs a very special funicular. Since 1899 it has been operated using waste water as a counterweight, and it is one of the last railways of this kind.
wichtigste: The funicular in Fribourg opened in 1899.
It links the lower town with the upper town.
It runs without a motor, using waste water as a counterweight.
The upper car is filled with water and pulls the lower one up.
It is one of the last railways of this kind in the world.

abschnitte.text: The city of **Fribourg** is divided into a **lower town** on the Sarine and an **upper town**. Between them lies a steep slope. Since **1899** a **funicular** has run here. It links the **Neuveville** district below with the upper town. The ride is short, but it saves a tiring walk.

The special thing is its **drive**. The railway has **no motor**. Both cars hang on the same cable. Under the car at the top there is a **tank**. This is filled with **waste water** from the town. This makes the upper car heavier, so it runs down and in doing so pulls the other car up. At the bottom the water is let out again.

In the past there were many railways that worked with water as a **counterweight**. Almost all of them were later converted or shut down. The funicular in Fribourg is one of the **last of its kind** in the world. It is a **protected monument** and is run by the Fribourg transport company. It is popular with locals and visitors alike.

gewusst: You cannot smell the waste water in the railway, because it is in closed tanks.
The railway shows how energy was saved with simple physics more than 100 years ago.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Path is a hiking trail around Lake Uri. It was laid out in 1991 for the 700th anniversary of the Confederation. Each canton has a stretch of path of its own on it.
wichtigste: The Swiss Path leads from the Rütli to Brunnen.
It is about 35 kilometres long.
It was opened in 1991 for the 700th birthday of the Confederation.
Each canton has a stretch of path of its own.
The length of a stretch depends on the number of inhabitants of the canton.
For each inhabitant there are 5 millimetres of path.

abschnitte.text: The path begins on the **Rütli**, the famous meadow on the shore of Lake Uri. It leads around the lake by way of **Seelisberg**, **Bauen** and **Flüelen**. At the end you reach **Brunnen** in the canton of Schwyz. On the way there are lovely views of the lake and the mountains. You can walk the path in several stages.

In **1991** Switzerland celebrated **700 years of the Confederation**. This recalled the **Federal Charter of 1291**. For the anniversary the cantons built this path together. It was meant to show that all the cantons together form one country.

The path is divided into **sections**, one for each canton. The length depends on the **number of inhabitants**: for each person in the canton there are **5 millimetres** of path. That is why large cantons such as **Zurich** have a long stretch and small cantons such as **Appenzell Innerrhoden** only a short one. The sections follow the order in which the cantons joined the Confederation.

At the boundaries of the sections stand **stones** with the names and coats of arms of the cantons. At the end in Brunnen there is a place for the **Swiss living abroad**. Many school classes walk the path and so learn something about the history of Switzerland.

gewusst: The section of the canton of Zurich is by far the longest.
Between individual stages you can take a boat across Lake Uri.

teile.einleitung: An agglomeration is a city together with the municipalities around it. These municipalities are closely linked to the city, for example through work and transport. In Switzerland the great majority of people live in an agglomeration.
wichtigste: An agglomeration consists of a core city and its suburbs.
In 2022 around three quarters of the Swiss population lived in an agglomeration.
In 2022 the Federal Statistical Office counted 52 agglomerations in total.
The largest agglomeration is Zurich.
Many people commute every day between home and workplace.
The Geneva agglomeration reaches far into France.

abschnitte.text: At the centre of an agglomeration lies the **core city**. Around it lie municipalities that are closely **interwoven** with it. Often you cannot even see where the city ends and the suburb begins. One example: **Köniz** and **Ostermundigen** border directly on the city of Bern and belong to the Bern agglomeration.

The **Federal Statistical Office** (FSO) decides which municipalities belong to an agglomeration. In 2022 it counted **52 agglomerations**. Around **74 per cent** of the population lived in them, that is, about three out of four people. The largest is the **Zurich** agglomeration with well over a million people.

In 2012 the FSO introduced a new definition. As a result the area of the agglomerations grew by about a third compared with 2000, from 8,601 to 11,356 square kilometres. The share of the population, by contrast, rose only slightly. The reason: mainly **thinly populated** areas were added.

Many people live in the agglomeration and work in the core city. They travel there and back every day and are called **commuters**. In Zurich the **S-Bahn** (suburban railway) has linked the city with the suburbs in a dense timetable since 1990. At **Geneva** the agglomeration reaches far into **France**. Many people live there and work in Geneva.

gewusst: Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France, which is why its agglomeration crosses the border.
Only about a quarter of the people in Switzerland live outside an agglomeration.

teile.einleitung: Victorinox is a company from Ibach in the canton of Schwyz. It makes the world-famous red Swiss Army Knife, which in Switzerland is also called a “Sackmesser” (pocket knife).
wichtigste: Victorinox has its headquarters in Ibach near Schwyz.
The company was founded in 1884 by Karl Elsener.
It makes the red Swiss Army Knife.
The knife was originally built for the Swiss Army.
The name combines “Victoria” and “inox”.
The knives are sold all over the world.

abschnitte.text: In **1884** **Karl Elsener** founded a knife workshop in **Ibach** near Schwyz. At that time the Swiss Army still bought its soldiers' knives abroad. Elsener wanted them to be made in Switzerland. From 1891 he supplied knives to the **army**. This is how the well-known **soldier's knife** came about.

After the death of his mother Victoria, Karl Elsener named his company after her. Later the word **“inox”** was added. It stands for stainless steel, in French “inoxydable”. This is how the name **Victorinox** came about. The company emblem is a cross in a shield.

The Swiss Army Knife does not have just one blade. Depending on the model it also has a **screwdriver**, tin opener, scissors, saw or corkscrew. Everything folds away. That is why the knife fits into any trouser pocket. Best known is the red **officer's knife**.

Today Victorinox sells its knives in a great many countries. Besides pocket knives, the company also makes kitchen knives, watches and travel luggage. In 2005 Victorinox took over the company **Wenger** from Delémont, which also made pocket knives. The red Swiss Army Knife has become a symbol of Switzerland.

gewusst: Swiss Army Knives have even flown into space with astronauts.
In German the knife is called “Sackmesser”; in English it is the “Swiss Army Knife”.

teile.einleitung: Lake Zug is the largest lake in the canton of Zug. On its north-eastern shore lies the city of Zug, and at its southern end the Rigi rises.
wichtigste: The city of Zug lies on the north-eastern shore of Lake Zug.
The lake belongs to the cantons of Zug, Schwyz and Lucerne.
At its deepest point it is almost 200 metres deep.
The Lorze flows into the lake and out again at Cham.
At the southern end lie the Rigi and the village of Arth.

abschnitte.text: Lake Zug lies between the city of Zug in the north and the **Rigi** in the south. The largest part belongs to the canton of Zug, smaller parts to **Schwyz** and **Lucerne**. On the shore lie places such as Zug, Cham, Risch, Walchwil, Immensee and Arth. The lake is long and narrow and almost 200 metres deep at its deepest point.

The most important river is the **Lorze**. It comes from Lake Ägeri, flows through the Lorze gorge and enters Lake Zug at Zug. At **Cham** it leaves the lake again and flows on to the Reuss. Because the water is renewed only slowly, it stays in the lake for a long time.

The city of Zug looks west across the lake. That is why you can see lovely **sunsets** there in the evening. The sun sinks behind the water and colours the sky orange and red. The lakeside promenade is then a popular meeting place.

abschnitte.titel: Life on and in the lake
abschnitte.text: On Lake Zug **passenger boats** sail, and in summer people swim, sail and row. In the lake live many fish, including the famous **Zuger Rötel**. In the past too many nutrients got into the water. Since then a great deal has been done to make the water cleaner and to give the depths more **oxygen** again.

gewusst: The Zuger Rötel, a speciality from Lake Zug, is a char with a red belly.
The Lorze first flows into Lake Zug and then leaves it again at Cham.

teile.einleitung: St Peter is a church in the old town of Zurich. Its tower carries the largest church clock face in Europe and can be recognised from far away.
wichtigste: St Peter stands in the old town of Zurich, on the left bank of the Limmat.
It is regarded as the oldest parish church in the city.
The faces of the tower clock have a diameter of around 8.7 metres.
This is the largest church clock face in Europe.
Today St Peter is a Reformed church.

abschnitte.text: The church of **St Peter** stands on a small hill in the **old town of Zurich**, on the left bank of the **Limmat**. There was already a church at this spot in the early Middle Ages. For this reason St Peter is regarded as the **oldest parish church** in Zurich. The present nave was rebuilt in the Baroque style in the 18th century. Since the **Reformation** St Peter has been a Reformed church.

St Peter is famous for its **tower clock**. Its **faces** have a diameter of around **8.7 metres**. This is the **largest church clock face in Europe**. The minute hand alone is several metres long. In this way people all over the city could read the time in the past, including the boatmen on the Limmat.

The tower of St Peter does not belong to the church congregation but to the **city of Zurich**. In the past a **fire watchman** lived at the top of the tower. He kept a lookout for fires day and night. If he saw smoke or flames, he raised the alarm. This was important because many houses were built of wood at that time.

Some well-known pastors worked at St Peter. One of them was **Johann Caspar Lavater** in the 18th century. He was a well-known writer and thinker of his time. Today services, concerts and guided tours take place in the church. Together with the Grossmünster and the Fraumünster, St Peter is one of the well-known churches of Zurich's old town.

gewusst: The clock face of St Peter is larger than the faces of Big Ben in London.
From the Lindenhof, very close by, you have a lovely view of the old town.

tlng9nq.t: Coat of arms of the canton of St Gallen

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of St Gallen shows a white bundle of rods with an axe on a green ground. It stands for the unity of the different parts of the country that were joined together in 1803 to form the canton.
wichtigste: In the St Gallen coat of arms is a white bundle of rods with an axe.
The ground is green.
The bundle is also called a fasces.
It comes from ancient Rome.
It stands for the unity of the parts of the country.
The canton of St Gallen was created in 1803.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **St Gallen** stands a **white bundle of rods** on a **green** ground. Several rods are tied together, and an **axe** is stuck in them. Such a bundle is also called a **fasces**. It is a sign that was already known in ancient times.

In **ancient Rome**, servants called **lictors** carried such bundles in front of important officials. The bundle showed the **power** of the state. Later it became a sign of **unity**: a single rod breaks easily, but many rods tied together are strong. At the time of the French Revolution the sign was very popular.

abschnitte.titel: A canton made of many parts
abschnitte.text: The canton of **St Gallen** was founded in **1803**. It was put together from many different areas, for example from the city of St Gallen, the Toggenburg and the Rhine Valley. These areas had previously had hardly anything to do with one another. The bundle of rods was meant to show that they now **belonged together**. Green was then regarded as the colour of freedom.

gewusst: St Gallen is the only canton with a bundle of rods in its coat of arms.
The city of St Gallen has a quite different coat of arms: a bear, as with the people of Appenzell.

teile.einleitung: Silvesterchlausen is an old custom in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Costumed Chläuse walk from farm to farm with big bells, sing and wish everyone a happy new year.
wichtigste: Silvesterchlausen takes place in Appenzell Ausserrhoden, for example in Urnäsch.
The Chläuse go from house to house in groups called Schuppel.
They wear big bells and cowbells that can be heard from far away.
There are three kinds: the Schöne, the Schö-Wüeschte and the Wüeschte.
The Chläuse sing a Zäuerli, a natural yodel without words.
The Chläusen takes place on 31 December and on 13 January, the “old New Year's Eve”.

abschnitte.text: At **Silvesterchlausen**, groups of costumed men walk through the villages. Such a group is called a **Schuppel**. The Chläuse wear heavy **bells** and **cowbells** on their bodies. When they move in time, the bells ring loudly. The custom is best known in **Urnäsch**, but also in other municipalities in **Appenzell Ausserrhoden**.

There are **three kinds** of Chläuse. The **Schöne** (“beautiful ones”) wear splendid headdresses with little figures and scenes from life in the Appenzell region. The **Wüeschte** (“wild ones”) are dressed in **fir branches**, moss, leaves and other natural materials and wear wild masks. The **Schö-Wüeschte** are a mixture of the two: they are made of natural materials but finely and skilfully designed. The costumes are often made by hand over months.

In front of every house the Schuppel stops and forms a circle. Then the Chläuse sing a **Zäuerli**. This is a **natural yodel without words**, slow and solemn. Afterwards they ring their bells again and wish the residents a **happy new year**. The residents often thank them with a drink or a small gift of money.

The Chläusen takes place on **31 December**. In some places, such as Urnäsch, people set out again on **13 January**. This day is called “**old New Year's Eve**”. It comes from the earlier **Julian calendar**, which ran a few days behind the present calendar. Some municipalities stayed with the old date and still celebrate that way today.

gewusst: A Schuppel is often out and about early in the morning, long before sunrise.
