Silvesterchlausen is one of the living traditions of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Altdorf is the main town of the canton of Uri. The place is closely linked with the legend of William Tell. On the Rathausplatz stands the famous Tell Monument.
wichtigste: Altdorf is the main town of the canton of Uri.
According to legend, Tell shot an apple from his son's head here.
The bronze Tell Monument has stood on the Rathausplatz since 1895.
Since 1899 amateurs have performed the play “William Tell” by Friedrich Schiller.
In 1799 Altdorf almost entirely burned down.
Next to Altdorf lies the harbour village of Flüelen on Lake Uri.

abschnitte.text: According to the legend, the bailiff **Gessler** had his **hat** put on a pole in Altdorf. Everyone had to greet it, but **William Tell** did not. As a punishment Tell had to shoot an **apple** from the head of his son with his **crossbow**. Tell hit the apple. This story is one of the best-known legends of Switzerland.

On the **Rathausplatz** stands the **Tell Monument**. It was put up in 1895 and is cast in **bronze**. The sculptor **Richard Kissling** designed it. It shows Tell with the crossbow and his son **Walter**, who clings to his father.

Since 1899 **amateurs** from Uri have performed the play **“William Tell”** by Friedrich Schiller in Altdorf. Amateurs are people who do not act as a profession. Today the performances take place in the **Tellspielhaus** (Tell Play Theatre).

On 5 April 1799 Altdorf almost entirely burned down. Around 400 buildings were destroyed. Afterwards the place was rebuilt. That is why many houses in the village centre are younger than in other old places.

Altdorf lies in the **Reuss Valley** of Uri, shortly before the lake. To the north **Flüelen** borders Altdorf. There on **Lake Uri** the boats of Lake Lucerne call. The old route to the **Gotthard** also leads through Altdorf.

gewusst: Whether William Tell really lived is not known, the story is a legend.
Schiller, who wrote the famous Tell play, was never in Switzerland himself.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne is a large museum about transport and mobility. It shows locomotives, ships, aeroplanes, cars and space travel and is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Swiss Museum of Transport stands in Lucerne on Lake Lucerne.
It opened in 1959.
It shows transport by rail, road, water and air.
Space travel also has an area of its own.
The museum includes a planetarium and a large cinema.
It is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Museum of Transport** stands in **Lucerne**, close to the shore of Lake Lucerne. It opened in **1959**. Since then it has grown a great deal and today has several large halls. Every year a great many visitors come. This makes it one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.

In the hall for **rail transport** stand real locomotives and carriages, from old steam locomotives to modern trains. You find out how the railway changed Switzerland, for example through the building of the Gotthard tunnel. In the **road transport** area you can see cars, bicycles and PostBuses. You can try out a lot of things yourself.

The **shipping** area is about steamships and ports. In **aviation** there are real aeroplanes and helicopters. A separate part shows **space travel** and how people journey into space. Cable cars and mountain railways also have their place, because they are especially important in Switzerland.

The museum includes a **planetarium**. There you can see the starry sky on a round dome. In the large **cinema**, films are shown on a huge screen. There is also an exhibition about chocolate and a museum with works by the artist **Hans Erni**.

gewusst: In the museum there is a huge walk-on aerial photograph of Switzerland, on which you can walk from canton to canton.
In the museum you can look at real locomotives and aeroplanes close up.

tpmle10.t: Coat of arms of the canton of the Valais

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of the Valais is divided vertically into white and red. On it are 13 stars. They recall the old districts of the Valais, which were called Zenden.
wichtigste: The Valais coat of arms is divided vertically: white on the left, red on the right.
On the coat of arms are 13 stars.
The stars stand for the former Zenden, that is, the districts of the Valais.
Each star has the colour of the other field.
The Valais has been a canton of Switzerland since 1815.
The main town is Sion, in German Sitten.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: The coat of arms is **divided vertically** in the middle. One half is **white**, the other **red**. Spread over both halves are **13 stars**. On the white field the stars are red, on the red field white. This way the colours always go well together.

In the past the Valais was divided into areas that were called **Zenden**. A Zenden was similar to a present-day **district**. For a long time there were **seven Zenden** in the Upper Valais, and so the coat of arms first had seven stars. When the whole Valais was reorganised, more stars were added. Since **1815** there have been **13 stars**.

For a long time the Valais was **allied** with the Confederation but did not quite belong to it. Such partners were called **Associates** (in German “Zugewandte Orte”). Only in **1815** did the Valais become a proper **canton of Switzerland**. Since then the Valais flag and the Swiss flag often fly side by side.

The Valais lies in the valley of the **Rhône** between high mountains. Many **four-thousanders** stand here, for example the **Matterhorn**. In the Upper Valais people speak **German**, in the Lower Valais **French**. On car number plates are the letters **VS** for the Latin name “Vallesia”.

gewusst: The Valais flag with its 13 stars is often seen at ski races and football matches.
The largest glacier in the Alps, the Great Aletsch Glacier, lies in the Valais.

teile.einleitung: On 23 August 2017 huge masses of rock fell into the valley at the Piz Cengalo in the Bergell. Afterwards debris flows rolled as far as the village of Bondo. The Bondo rockslide is one of the biggest natural events of recent decades in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The rockslide happened on the morning of 23 August 2017.
Around 3 million m³ of rock fell from the Piz Cengalo into the Val Bondasca.
The masses of rock reached about 250 km/h.
Eight walkers lost their lives and were never found.
Debris flows reached the village of Bondo and damaged houses.
A catchment basin held back part of the material.

abschnitte.text: Bondo is a village in the **Bergell** in the south of Graubünden, near the border with Italy. Since 2010 it has belonged to the municipality of **Bregaglia**, into which the villages of the Bergell merged. Above Bondo opens the **Val Bondasca**, a side valley. Above it towers the **Piz Cengalo**, a granite peak over 3,300 metres high.

As early as **27 December 2011**, 1.5 to 2 million m³ of rock fell into the Val Bondasca from the north flank of the Piz Cengalo. After that the rock flank was monitored constantly. In 2014 and 2015 a large **catchment basin** with a protective wall was built. It held around 50,000 m³, or about 200,000 m³ with the freeboard. The **freeboard** is the extra space up to the top edge.

On the morning of **23 August 2017** around **3 million m³** of rock broke away. The masses raced through the Val Bondasca at about **250 km/h**. **Eight walkers** who were out in the valley were buried and could never be found. The rock mixed with water and debris to form **debris flows**. A debris flow is a stream of mud, stones and water.

The debris flows ran through the valley as far as **Bondo**. The catchment basin held back part of the material but was filled several times. Houses, roads and bridges were damaged. The village was evacuated. Afterwards the protective works were built larger and stronger.

gewusst: 3 million cubic metres of rock would fill about 3,000 detached houses.
Experts suspect that thawing permafrost in the rock also contributed to the rockslide.

teile.einleitung: Aarau is the main town of the canton of Aargau. The city lies on the Aare in the Central Plateau, between Zurich and Bern. It is known for its old town with painted gables.
wichtigste: Aarau is the main town of the canton of Aargau.
Aarau is called the “city of beautiful gables”.
Albert Einstein took his school-leaving exam (Matura) in Aarau in 1896.
In 1798 Aarau was the capital of the Helvetic Republic for a few months.
In Aarau there is a bell foundry with over 600 years of tradition.
At the end of 2023 around 22,000 people lived in Aarau.

abschnitte.text: In Aarau sit the **government** and the **parliament** of the canton of Aargau. The city lies on the **Aare** in the Central Plateau, on the railway line between **Zurich** and **Bern**. Immediately to the west begins the canton of **Solothurn**. At the end of 2023 around 22,000 people lived in Aarau.

Many houses in the old town have brightly painted **eaves**. These are the underside of the roof, which sticks out beyond the house wall. That is why Aarau is called the **“city of beautiful gables”**. The oldest building is the **Schlössli**, a residential tower from the 13th century. Today the town museum is housed in it.
In 1798 the **Helvetic Republic** came into being. It was a unitary state on the French model. For a few months Aarau was its first **capital**. After that the government moved on to Lucerne.

The famous physicist **Albert Einstein** attended the **Cantonal School of Aarau**. In 1896 he passed his **Matura**, the school-leaving exam, there. Later he became world-famous with his theory of relativity.
In Aarau there is a **bell foundry** with a tradition over 600 years old. There liquid metal is poured into moulds. Bells from Aarau hang in many church towers.

gewusst: Aarau was the first capital of Switzerland as a unitary state, if only for a few months.
Albert Einstein took his Matura not in Zurich or Bern but in Aarau.

teile.einleitung: The Bernese Oberland is the southern, mountainous part of the canton of Bern. Here lie Lake Thun and Lake Brienz, steep valleys and famous peaks such as the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau. The region is one of the best-known holiday areas in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Bernese Oberland belongs to the canton of Bern.
Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
The Lauterbrunnen Valley is known for its many waterfalls.
Near Brienz lies the Ballenberg open-air museum.
In Wengen the Lauberhorn race takes place every year.
On the Schilthorn stands a revolving restaurant.

abschnitte.text: Between **Lake Thun** and **Lake Brienz** lies **Interlaken**. Right above the town a funicular goes up the **Harder Kulm**. From there you can see both lakes and many mountains. On Lake Thun lie the **St Beatus Caves**, a stalactite cave. According to legend, the monk Beatus drove away a dragon here. On the **Schynige Platte** a large number of mountain plants grow in an alpine garden, and an old rack railway goes up to it.

The **Lauterbrunnen Valley** has steep rock walls over which many **waterfalls** plunge. Well known is the **Staubbach Falls**. Special are the **Trümmelbach Falls**: they have eaten into the rock and plunge down inside the mountain. You can visit them by paths and a lift in the mountain. They carry the meltwater of the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau into the valley.

abschnitte.titel: Ski races and a revolving restaurant
abschnitte.text: In **Wengen** the **Lauberhorn race** takes place every year. There the best skiers in the world race. The downhill is regarded as the longest in the World Cup. Above Mürren lies the **Schilthorn**. The restaurant on the summit turns slowly in a circle, so that while eating you see all the mountains around.

Near Brienz lies the open-air museum **Ballenberg**. There stand over a hundred old houses from all over Switzerland. You can see how people used to live and work. From Meiringen the **Brünig Pass** leads to Obwalden. Cars and trains go over it.

gewusst: The Jungfrau Railway runs to the Jungfraujoch, the highest railway station in Europe, at 3,454 metres above sea level.
In the Lauterbrunnen Valley there are so many waterfalls that it is also called the valley of the 72 waterfalls.

teile.einleitung: The World Wide Web, WWW or the Web for short, was invented in 1989 at CERN near Geneva. The British researcher Tim Berners-Lee wanted to help researchers share information with it. Today billions of people use it.
wichtigste: The World Wide Web was invented at CERN in 1989.
CERN is a large research centre near Geneva.
The inventor is Tim Berners-Lee from Britain.
He worked closely with Robert Cailliau on it.
The Web consists of pages that are joined by links.
Since 1993 anyone has been allowed to use the Web free of charge.

abschnitte.text: **CERN** is a large **research centre** for particle physics near **Geneva**. Researchers from many countries work together there. They had a lot of information on different computers. In **1989** the Briton **Tim Berners-Lee** suggested a system with which this information could easily be found and shared. From it came the **World Wide Web**.

The Web consists of **web pages**. Each page has an **address** of its own. Pages can point to other pages with **links**. If you click on one, you jump to the next page. To look at the pages you need a **browser**. Berners-Lee also wrote the first programs for this, and a language of its own for web pages.

Many people mix up the **Web** and the **Internet**. The **Internet** is the worldwide **network** of computers and cables. It existed before 1989. The **Web** is a service that uses the Internet, just like **email**. You could say: the Internet is the road, and the Web is part of the traffic on it.

In **1993** CERN declared that anyone may use the Web **free of charge**. Nobody has to pay money for it. This was very important: afterwards the Web spread quickly all over the world. Today **billions of people** use it for learning, playing, shopping and communicating.

gewusst: The first web page in the world went online in 1991 and explained what the Web is.
The first web server was a computer at CERN with a note stuck on it saying that it should not be switched off.

teile.einleitung: The Sonderbund War was a short civil war in Switzerland in November 1847. It was followed in 1848 by the creation of the modern federal state with a common constitution.
wichtigste: The Sonderbund was an alliance of Catholic-conservative cantons, led by Lucerne.
It included Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden, Zug, Fribourg and the Valais.
In November 1847 war broke out with the other, liberal cantons.
The war lasted only a few weeks, and the Sonderbund was defeated.
General Guillaume Henri Dufour led the troops of the Federal Diet.
In 1848 Switzerland received a new federal constitution and became a federal state.

abschnitte.text: In the first half of the 19th century Switzerland was a loose **confederation of states**. The cantons argued about what the country should look like. The **liberals** wanted a stronger common state. The **Catholic conservatives** wanted to keep the power of the cantons and the Church. Religious questions also played a big part, such as the closing of monasteries in Aargau and the calling of **Jesuits** to Lucerne.

In **1845** seven Catholic cantons joined together in a defensive alliance. They were **Lucerne**, **Uri**, **Schwyz**, **Obwalden** and **Nidwalden**, **Zug**, **Fribourg** and the **Valais**. This alliance was called the **Sonderbund** (“separate alliance”). **Lucerne** was the leading place and the seat of the war council. The majority of cantons in the **Federal Diet** regarded the Sonderbund as illegal and demanded that it be dissolved.

In **November 1847** war broke out. The troops of the Federal Diet were led by General **Guillaume Henri Dufour** from Geneva. First **Fribourg** surrendered, then the troops marched against **Lucerne**. After a battle at **Gisikon**, Lucerne fell too. The war lasted less than a month. Dufour ordered his soldiers to treat prisoners and the wounded well, so there were comparatively few deaths.

abschnitte.titel: The road to the federal state
abschnitte.text: After the war the Sonderbund was dissolved. As early as **1848** Switzerland gave itself a new **federal constitution**. The confederation of states became a **federal state** with a parliament, a **Federal Council** and a common currency. **Bern** became the seat of the federal authorities. The cantons kept many tasks of their own, as is still the case today.

gewusst: The Sonderbund War was the last war fought on Swiss territory.
General Dufour was also a cartographer: he directed the making of the first accurate national map of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Wildkirchli is a group of caves on the Ebenalp in the Alpstein, in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden. There bones of cave bears and stone tools from the Old Stone Age were found. Today it is a popular destination for outings.
wichtigste: The Wildkirchli lies on the Ebenalp in the Alpstein.
It belongs to the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.
Bones of cave bears were found in the caves.
Stone tools from the Old Stone Age were also found.
The finds show that people were here many tens of thousands of years ago.
The researcher Emil Bächler dug here at the beginning of the 20th century.

abschnitte.text: The **Wildkirchli** consists of several **caves** in a steep rock face below the **Ebenalp**. A path leads through the caves. You can ride up to the Ebenalp by **cable car** and then walk down to the caves. Right next to them lies the well-known mountain inn **Aescher**, which is built against the rock.

At the beginning of the 20th century the researcher **Emil Bächler** from St Gallen dug in the caves. He found many **bones of cave bears**. These big bears became **extinct** a long time ago. He also found **tools made of stone**. They show that people came here in the **Old Stone Age**, probably as hunters.

In one of the caves stands a small **chapel**. That is where the name “Kirchli” (“little church”) comes from. From the 17th to the 19th century **hermits** lived here. These are people who live alone and withdrawn in order to pray. Today a small **museum** recalls them and the finds from the Stone Age.

gewusst: The Wildkirchli was one of the first places in Switzerland where such old traces of people were found in the Alps.
The cave bear was clearly bigger than a present-day brown bear.

teile.einleitung: Zurich Zoo lies on the Zürichberg. One of its biggest attractions is the Masoala Hall. In this huge hall a rainforest grows as on the island of Madagascar.
wichtigste: Zurich Zoo lies on the Zürichberg.
It opened in 1929.
The Masoala Hall recreates a rainforest from Madagascar.
In the hall live, for example, lemurs and chameleons.
The zoo also has a large elephant park.
The zoo supports nature conservation in Madagascar and other countries.

abschnitte.text: The **Masoala Hall** opened in **2003**. In it grows a real **rainforest** with plants from **Madagascar**. It is always **warm** and **humid** there. The name comes from the **Masoala National Park** in the north-east of Madagascar. In the hall the animals often move about freely, and sometimes you have to look for them.

In the Masoala Hall live **lemurs**, which are wet-nosed primates found only on Madagascar. In addition there are **chameleons**, **tortoises**, **birds** and **flying foxes**. Many small animals such as frogs and insects also live here. You walk on paths right through the forest.

Zurich Zoo opened in **1929**. In **2014** the large **Kaeng Krachan Elephant Park** was added, named after a national park in **Thailand**. Since **2020** there has been the **Lewa Savannah** with giraffes, rhinoceroses and zebras from Africa. In addition there are enclosures for tigers, penguins and many other animals.

Zurich Zoo wants to **inspire people about nature**. With money from the zoo, **conservation projects** are supported, for example in the Masoala National Park. In this way the zoo helps to protect rainforests and endangered animals in their **homeland**.

gewusst: In the Masoala Hall it rains artificially so that the plants get enough water.
Zurich Zoo is one of the most visited destinations for outings in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Seealpsee is a mountain lake in the Alpstein in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden. It lies below the Ebenalp and is a popular hiking destination with a wonderful view of the rock walls.
wichtigste: The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.
It is below the Ebenalp at over 1,100 metres above sea level.
You reach it on foot, usually from Wasserauen.
Hiking trails lead around the lake, and there are mountain inns.
The lake is one of the best-known photo subjects in eastern Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Seealpsee** lies in the **Alpstein**, the mountain range around the Säntis. Steep limestone cliffs surround the lake on several sides. Above it lies the **Ebenalp**, a popular viewpoint mountain. The water is often green or blue and reflects the mountains. A stream flows out of the lake down into the valley.

There is **no public road** for cars to the Seealpsee. Most hikers start in **Wasserauen**, where the Appenzell railway ends. From there it is about an hour's walk uphill. You can also take the cable car up to the Ebenalp and walk down to the lake. On the way you pass the **Wildkirchli** and the **Aescher** mountain inn.

On the shore of the lake there are **mountain inns** where you can eat and stay overnight. In summer cows graze on the alpine meadows around the lake. The name **Seealp** simply means “alp by the lake”. Many families stop here, have picnics and enjoy the peace.

gewusst: The Seealpsee is a popular destination for photographers, especially at sunrise.
In winter the lake often freezes over and lies still in the snow.

teile.einleitung: The Stockalper Palace in Brig is a large palace with three towers. It was built in the 17th century by the wealthy Valais merchant Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper.
wichtigste: The Stockalper Palace stands in Brig in the canton of the Valais.
It was built in the 17th century by Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper.
Stockalper became very rich through trade over the Simplon Pass.
The palace has three tall towers with onion domes.
It is the landmark of Brig.

abschnitte.text: The **Stockalper Palace** is the **landmark of Brig**. It was built in the 17th century and was at that time one of the largest private buildings in Switzerland. Especially striking are the **three tall towers** with their onion domes. They bear the names of the Three Wise Men: **Kaspar**, **Melchior** and **Balthasar**. Inside lies a large **arcaded courtyard** with arched galleries on several floors.

The builder was **Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper**. He lived in the 17th century and was a very skilful **merchant**. He controlled the trade over the **Simplon Pass** between the Valais and Italy. Especially important was **salt**, which was needed in those days to preserve food. This made Stockalper one of the richest men of his time. He was also called the “**King of the Simplon**”.

So that goods could cross the mountains safely, Stockalper had the mule track over the Simplon improved. Goods were carried back and forth by mules. On the way he had houses built for overnight stays and storage. Today you can walk the **Stockalper Way** in the footsteps of these muleteers.

Stockalper had great influence and held many offices in the Valais. In time he became too powerful for some people. He was removed from office and had to flee for some years to **Domodossola** in Italy. Later he returned to Brig, where he died. His palace now belongs to the municipality of Brig and can be visited.

gewusst: The three towers of the Stockalper Palace are named after the Three Wise Men.
Concerts and festivals are held in the arcaded courtyard of the palace today.

teile.einleitung: An onion tart is a flat tart with a lot of onions on a pastry base. In Schaffhausen it is called “Bölletünne” and is a well-known speciality.
wichtigste: The Bölletünne is the Schaffhausen onion tart.
“Bölle” means onion in dialect.
“Tünne” means a flat tart, similar to a Wähe.
On a pastry base lie sweated onions and a custard topping.
People like to eat onion tart in autumn.

abschnitte.text: The **Bölletünne** is a speciality from the canton of **Schaffhausen**. The name comes from the dialect: **Bölle** is the word for onion, and a **Tünne** is a flat tart. So the Bölletünne is a fine onion tart. In other parts of Switzerland you would probably call it an onion Wähe.

First you roll out a **dough** thinly and lay it in a round tin. Then many onions are cut into rings or strips and sweated soft in butter. The onions go onto the dough. Over them you pour a **custard** of eggs and milk or cream. Often bacon cubes and a little caraway are added. Then the tart is baked golden brown in the oven.

People especially like to eat onion tart in **autumn**, when the onions have been harvested. In wine-growing areas it belongs to the time of the grape harvest. The Schaffhausen region has many vineyards, for example in the **Klettgau**. There the warm tart goes well with a cosy autumn evening.

Onion tart is known not only in Schaffhausen. In **southern Germany**, in Alsace and in other parts of Switzerland there are similar recipes too. In Alsace the very thin **Flammkuchen** is well known, though it is usually made without a custard of eggs. Every area has its own small differences in the recipe.

gewusst: For a single onion tart you often need a whole kilo of onions.
When sweated slowly, onions become sweetish, because their sharp taste changes.

teile.einleitung: Appenzell is an area in eastern Switzerland with two cantons: Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden. Both lie like an island in the middle of the canton of St Gallen. Known are the green hills, the Alpstein and old customs such as the Landsgemeinde.
wichtigste: The two Appenzells are completely surrounded by the canton of St Gallen.
In Innerrhoden the Landsgemeinde still takes place in the open air.
There the sword is traditionally the men's voting pass.
Innerrhoden is divided into districts instead of municipalities.
In 1990 Innerrhoden was the last canton to introduce women's suffrage.
The Appenzeller Sennenhund (Appenzell mountain dog) comes from the Appenzell region.

abschnitte.text: Appenzell **Ausserrhoden** and Appenzell **Innerrhoden** lie like an island in the middle of the canton of **St Gallen**. In the past they were one land, but in 1597 they split after the Reformation. Innerrhoden stayed Catholic, Ausserrhoden became Reformed. The main town of Innerrhoden is also called **Appenzell**. In Ausserrhoden the government and parliament meet in **Herisau**, but the high court in **Trogen**.

In Innerrhoden those entitled to vote meet once a year on the square in the main town for the **Landsgemeinde** (open-air assembly). There people vote by raising a hand. Men traditionally carry a **sword** or a bayonet as a voting pass, while women and others show a **voting card**. Innerrhoden is divided into **districts** that take over the tasks of the municipalities.

Innerrhoden was the last canton to introduce cantonal **women's suffrage**, in 1990. The men at the Landsgemeinde had rejected it several times before. In the end the **Federal Supreme Court** decided that women may also take part in decisions.

In the south lies the **Alpstein** mountain range with the **Säntis**. On the **Hoher Kasten** there is a **revolving restaurant** that turns slowly around itself. So you gradually see into the **Rhine Valley** and the mountains of the Alpstein.

The **Appenzeller Sennenhund** comes from the Appenzell region. It is medium-sized and three-coloured. In the past it helped to drive cattle and guard farms. Also well known are the **Appenzeller cheese** and the colourful farmers' painting.

gewusst: Appenzell Innerrhoden is the canton with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland.
At the Landsgemeinde the vote is not secret, everyone sees who raises a hand.

teile.einleitung: Tête de Moine is a Swiss semi-hard cheese from the Jura Arc. It is not cut into slices but scraped with a crank into fine rosettes.
wichtigste: Tête de Moine means “monk's head” in English.
It originally comes from Bellelay Abbey in the Bernese Jura.
It is made in the Jura Arc, including the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
It is scraped into rosettes with a device called a Girolle.
It carries the protected designation of origin AOP.

abschnitte.text: Tête de Moine goes back to the monks of **Bellelay Abbey** in the Bernese Jura. They were making this cheese centuries ago. The name means **“monk's head”**. How exactly it got this name is told in different ways. Today Bellelay is no longer a monastery, but the cheese has remained.

Tête de Moine is not cut. You put the round cheese on a spindle and turn a blade over it with a **crank**. This device is called a **Girolle** and was invented in 1982. This produces thin, frilly **rosettes** that look like little flowers. Scraping exposes the cheese to a lot of air, and it tastes especially spicy.

Tête de Moine is made in the **Jura Arc**. This includes parts of the **Bernese Jura** and of the **canton of Jura**, such as the **Franches-Montagnes**. **Raw milk** from cows of the region is used. The wheels mature for several months on wooden boards. Since 2001 the name has been protected as **AOP**, which means that only cheese from this area may be called by this name.

The rosettes are often eaten as an **apéritif snack** with bread. On a cheese platter they look especially beautiful. You can also use them to decorate salads. Today Tête de Moine is sold in many countries.

gewusst: Before the Girolle, the cheese used to be scraped thin with a knife.
The rosettes taste different from a thick slice of the same cheese.

teile.einleitung: Lake Lucerne lies in central Switzerland and is one of the largest lakes lying entirely within Switzerland. It has many arms and borders the cantons of Lucerne, Schwyz, Uri, Nidwalden and Obwalden.
wichtigste: The city of Lucerne lies on Lake Lucerne.
The lake covers about 114 square kilometres.
It borders Lucerne, Schwyz, Uri, Nidwalden and Obwalden.
The name comes from the four Forest Cantons.
The Reuss flows through the lake.
Passenger boats and old paddle steamers sail on the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Lucerne** lies in the middle of central Switzerland. It covers about **114 square kilometres** and is over 200 metres deep at its deepest point. The lake has an unusual shape with many **arms** and bays. One of them is Lake Uri in the south. The **Reuss** flows in at Flüelen and out again at Lucerne.

The name comes from the **four Forest Cantons**. This is what the places Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne used to be called. Today five cantons border the lake: **Lucerne**, **Schwyz**, **Uri**, **Nidwalden** and **Obwalden**. On the southern shore lie places in Nidwalden such as **Hergiswil**, **Buochs** and **Beckenried**.

At the north-western end of the lake lies the city of **Lucerne**. From there boats sail to many places on the lake. Around the lake stand well-known mountains such as the **Rigi**, **Pilatus** and the Stanserhorn. On the western shore of Lake Uri lies the **Rütli meadow**, an important place in Swiss history.

On Lake Lucerne there is a large fleet of **passenger boats**. Especially popular are the old **paddle steamers**. They are driven by steam and have large paddle wheels at the sides. Many people use the boats for outings, and some also for getting to work.

gewusst: Five historic paddle steamers still sail on Lake Lucerne, which is one of the largest steamer fleets on a Swiss lake.
With the boat and the rack railway you can travel from Lucerne right up to the Rigi.

teile.einleitung: The University of Fribourg is a university in the city of Fribourg in the canton of Fribourg. It is bilingual: you can study in German, in French or in both languages.
wichtigste: The University of Fribourg was founded in 1889.
It is the only bilingual full university in Switzerland.
You can study in German, French or both languages.
Fribourg lies on the language border between German and French.
There are several faculties, for example law, theology and natural sciences.

abschnitte.text: The city of **Fribourg** lies exactly on the **language border**. Part of the population speaks French, another part German. The university too is **bilingual**. Students can attend their courses in **German**, in **French** or in both languages. Anyone who studies in both languages can receive a bilingual degree.

The university was founded in **1889**. It has a long **Catholic** tradition and is still known today for its faculty of **theology**. In time many other subjects were added. Today it is a university for people of all religions and backgrounds.

The university has several **faculties**. These are large departments for different fields of knowledge. They include **law**, **theology**, the humanities, economics and **natural sciences** with medicine. There are buildings in different parts of the city, for example **Miséricorde** and **Pérolles**.

Students come to Fribourg from **all over Switzerland** and from many other countries. The university is especially popular with young people who want to learn a second national language. So **German-speaking Switzerland** and **French-speaking Switzerland** meet here. The city of Fribourg is therefore also a lively student town.

gewusst: In French the city is called Fribourg and the university Université de Fribourg.
The old town of Fribourg lies high above the Sarine, which flows through a deep gorge.

tvwrptf.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows an upright black bear on a white ground. The bear is the heraldic animal of both Appenzells.
wichtigste: In the coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden stands a bear.
The bear is black and stands upright.
The ground of the coat of arms is white.
Unlike in Ausserrhoden, there are no letters next to it.
The bear recalls the Abbey of St Gallen and Saint Gallus.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Appenzell Innerrhoden** a **black bear** stands upright on its hind legs. The ground is **white**. The bear has red claws and sticks out a red tongue. In contrast to the coat of arms of Ausserrhoden, there are **no letters** next to it.

In the Middle Ages the Appenzell region belonged to the **Abbey of St Gallen**. The bear comes from the abbey's coat of arms. It recalls a legend about **Saint Gallus**. A bear is said to have helped him fetch wood for the fire. That is why the bear became the heraldic animal.

In **1597** Appenzell split into two parts for reasons of faith. **Innerrhoden** stayed Catholic, Ausserrhoden became Reformed. Both kept the bear. Innerrhoden has the main town **Appenzell** and is the canton with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland.

gewusst: Appenzell Innerrhoden is one of the few cantons that still pass their laws at a Landsgemeinde in the open air.

teile.einleitung: A rock glacier looks like a giant heap of boulders. Inside, however, there is ice that holds the debris together. Very slowly the whole mass creeps down the slope.
wichtigste: A rock glacier is a creeping mixture of debris and ice.
Under the layer of blocks it often contains 40 to 70 per cent ice.
Active rock glaciers usually move 0.1 to 1 m per year.
They show that permafrost is present in the ground.
At Murtèl-Corvatsch in the Upper Engadine, measurements have been made in a borehole since 1987.
Fossil rock glaciers no longer contain ice and do not move.

abschnitte.text: A **rock glacier** consists of frozen **debris**. In the spaces between the stones there is **ice** that cements everything together. Under the coarse top layer there is often a body with **40 to 70 per cent ice**. This ice belongs to the **permafrost**. Permafrost is ground that stays frozen all year round. Rock glaciers are usually 30 to 50 m thick, a few hundred metres long and 100 to 200 m wide.

Active rock glaciers **creep** down the slope, usually only **0.1 to 1 m per year**. Because the permafrost has become warmer, many have become faster in recent decades. An active rock glacier has a **steep, unstable front**. Its surface is lumpy, with ridges and furrows, like a solidified lava flow.

Although it is called that, a rock glacier is not counted by experts among true glaciers. On the surface you see **no ice**, only coarse blocks. It usually forms from frozen **slope debris**, but can also develop from a debris-covered **cirque glacier** or from debris-rich moraines. Rock glaciers belong to the field of **geomorphology**, the study of the forms of the Earth's surface.

Active rock glaciers need permanently frozen ground. That is why they show where there is **permafrost**. Their lower limit corresponds roughly to the lower limit of patchy permafrost. On the **Murtèl-Corvatsch** rock glacier in the **Upper Engadine** a borehole was made in 1987. It is one of the oldest permafrost measuring sites in the Alps.

Not all rock glaciers still move. **Inactive** forms have flatter fronts and are often already covered with plants. **Fossil** rock glaciers lie outside today's permafrost. They no longer contain ice and are only debris deposits of former rock glaciers.

gewusst: Some rock glaciers reach several kilometres in length.
When rock glaciers become faster, more debris can get into streams and set off debris flows.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is not on the sea, but it still has ports. The Swiss Rhine Ports in Basel and in Basel-Landschaft link the country with the North Sea by way of the Rhine.
wichtigste: The Swiss Rhine Ports belong to the cantons of Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft.
There are port facilities in Basel-Kleinhüningen, in Birsfelden and in the Auhafen in Muttenz.
From Basel the Rhine flows through Germany and the Netherlands to the North Sea.
Fuel, grain and containers in particular come into Switzerland through the ports.
The Basel Rhine ports are considered Switzerland's gateway to the sea.

abschnitte.titel: Ports in the middle of the country
abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Rhine Ports** are a joint institution of the cantons of **Basel-Stadt** and **Basel-Landschaft**. The largest port is in **Kleinhüningen** in the north of Basel. In the canton of Basel-Landschaft there are facilities in **Birsfelden** and in the **Auhafen** in **Muttenz**. Long Rhine ships dock there and are loaded and unloaded. Cranes, warehouses and railway tracks are part of every port.

abschnitte.titel: To the sea by the Rhine
abschnitte.text: From Basel, large ships can sail on the **Rhine** all the way to the **North Sea**. The river flows through Germany and the Netherlands. Important ports at the end of the route are **Rotterdam** and **Antwerp**. There goods are transferred to ocean-going ships. In this way Switzerland is linked by water to the whole world.

Many goods that people need in everyday life arrive through the Rhine ports. They include **heating oil**, **petrol** and **diesel**, but also **grain**, animal feed, gravel and metals. **Containers**, standardised steel boxes for all kinds of goods, are becoming more and more important. A single Rhine ship can carry as much as a great many lorries. That spares the roads.

The Rhine ports are important for Switzerland's **national supply**. If roads or railway lines are disrupted, the route along the Rhine remains. **Compulsory stockpiles**, for example of fuel, are also kept in stores at the ports. At the **Dreiländereck** (Three Countries Corner) in Kleinhüningen, Switzerland, Germany and France meet.

gewusst: The ships of the Swiss ocean-going fleet, which sail the world's seas, have Basel as their home port.
When the Rhine is low, ships can only sail with half a load.

teile.einleitung: The Stanserhorn is a viewpoint mountain directly above the village of Stans in Nidwalden. It is known for its CabriO cable car with an open upper deck and for its wide views.
wichtigste: The Stanserhorn rises directly above Stans in the canton of Nidwalden.
The mountain is 1,898 metres high.
First you go up on an old funicular.
Then you continue on the CabriO cable car, which has an open upper deck.
From the summit you can see many lakes and mountains of central Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Stanserhorn** rises just behind the village of **Stans**. Stans is the main town of the canton of **Nidwalden**. The mountain is **1,898 metres** high. From the summit there is a wide **view** over central Switzerland. You can see many lakes, including **Lake Lucerne**, and a long chain of Alpine peaks.

The journey up the Stanserhorn begins with a **funicular**. It was built as early as the end of the **19th century**. The wooden cars still look almost as they did in the past. The railway runs from Stans to a middle station. There you change to a modern cable car.

The **CabriO** is a special **aerial cable car** with **two storeys**. Below, passengers sit in a closed cabin. Above there is an **open upper deck** without a roof. There you ride up the Stanserhorn under the open sky. The CabriO opened in **2012** and was the first cable car of its kind in the world. Its name recalls a cabriolet, a car with an open roof.

At the summit stands a **revolving restaurant**. It turns slowly in a circle, so you can enjoy the whole panorama while you eat. A short circular path leads around the summit. **Marmots** live there and can often be watched. Many families go on an outing here.

gewusst: On the open upper deck of the CabriO you feel the wind as if you were flying.
The Stanserhorn is exactly as high as the Grosser Mythen in the canton of Schwyz.

twlyq06.t: Economy of the canton of Basel-Stadt

teile.einleitung: The canton of Basel-Stadt is small but economically very strong. The pharmaceutical and chemical industry is especially important. Large companies such as Roche and Novartis have their headquarters here.
wichtigste: The pharmaceutical and chemical industry is especially important for Basel.
Roche and Novartis have their headquarters in Basel.
They make medicines for the whole world.
Basel is also a well-known trade fair city.
Many goods come into Switzerland by way of the Rhine and the Rhine port.
Many people from France and Germany work in Basel.

abschnitte.text: In Basel the big **pharmaceutical companies** **Roche** and **Novartis** have their **headquarters**. They research new **medicines** and sell them all over the world. Thousands of people work for these companies, for example in **laboratories** or offices. The Roche tower is one of the **tallest buildings in Switzerland**.

In the 19th century **silk ribbons** were made in Basel. For this, **dyes** were needed. So factories came about that made **dyestuffs** using chemistry. From these firms the **chemical industry** later grew. From it the **pharmaceutical industry** developed, which is so important today.

Basel is a well-known **trade fair city**. Large exhibitions take place on the fairgrounds, for example the art fair **Art Basel**. The **Bank for International Settlements** also has its seat in Basel. It is often called the “bank of the central banks”. In addition there are many firms in **trade** and **logistics**.

abschnitte.titel: On the Rhine and at the border
abschnitte.text: In Basel lie the **Swiss Rhine ports**. Here ships arrive from the **North Sea** and bring, for example, fuel, grain and containers. Basel borders **France** and **Germany**. Every day many **cross-border commuters** from these countries come to work in Basel.

gewusst: Basel-Stadt is the smallest canton in Switzerland by area.
The Rhine divides the city of Basel into Grossbasel (Greater Basel) and Kleinbasel (Lesser Basel).

tx04wdm.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Ticino

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Ticino is divided vertically into two halves: red on the left and blue on the right. It came about when Ticino became a canton of its own in 1803.
wichtigste: The Ticino coat of arms is divided vertically.
The left half is red.
The right half is blue.
Ticino has been a canton of its own since 1803.
The main town is Bellinzona.

abschnitte.text: The **coat of arms of the canton of Ticino** is very simple. It is divided **vertically** into two halves. The **left** half is **red**, the **right** half is **blue**. On the flag the colours are arranged side by side or one above the other. Where the two colours come from exactly is not known for certain.

In the past Ticino was not a canton of its own. It was ruled by other members of the Confederation, above all by Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden. Such areas are called **subject territories**. Only in **1803** did Ticino become a canton with **equal rights**. At that time it also received its coat of arms.

Ticino lies south of the Alps. People speak **Italian** here. The main town is **Bellinzona** with its three medieval castles. Larger towns also include **Lugano** and **Locarno**. In Ticino you can see the red and blue colours on many flags and buildings.

gewusst: Ticino is the only canton in which Italian is the only official language.
The three castles of Bellinzona are part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland more than a quarter of the population lives without a Swiss passport. Many of them were born here or have lived here for a long time. The subject of immigration is discussed in politics again and again.
wichtigste: At the end of 2024 around 27 per cent of the resident population did not have a Swiss passport.
The largest foreign group comes from Italy.
Geneva has the highest share of foreigners of all the cantons.
Free movement of persons with the EU has applied since 2002.
For ordinary naturalisation you need ten years of residence in Switzerland.
Citizenship is passed on mainly through the parents.

abschnitte.text: At the end of 2024, according to the **Federal Statistical Office**, around 2.48 million people without a Swiss passport lived in Switzerland. That is **27.4 per cent** of the permanent resident population. The largest group comes from **Italy**, just ahead of **Germany**. Portugal and France follow. In the canton of **Geneva** around 40 per cent of the population has no Swiss passport, partly because of the international organisations and the border location.

As early as 1910 the share of foreigners was around 15 per cent. Many workers from Germany and Italy built railway lines or worked in factories. After the Second World War many **workers** came from Italy. For a long time the **seasonal worker status** applied to many: you were allowed to stay for at most nine months a year and could not bring your family. It was abolished in 2002.

Switzerland voted on immigration several times. In 1970 the **Schwarzenbach Initiative** wanted to limit the share of foreigners in most cantons to 10 per cent. It was rejected with around 54 per cent No. On 9 February 2014 the **Mass Immigration Initiative** was accepted very narrowly with 50.3 per cent Yes. Supporters want to control immigration more strongly, opponents stress the importance of workers and of relations with the EU.

The agreement on **free movement of persons** was signed in 1999 as part of the **Bilaterals I**. It came into force on 1 June 2002. Since then citizens of the EU with an employment contract can move to Switzerland more easily. Conversely, Swiss people can also work in the EU more easily.

In Switzerland you get citizenship mainly through **descent**, that is, through your parents. Experts call this **ius sanguinis**. People born in Switzerland do not automatically become Swiss. For **ordinary naturalisation** you have needed ten years of residence and a **settlement permit C** since 2018. The Confederation, the canton and the municipality all have a say.

gewusst: Many people who count statistically as foreigners were born and brought up in Switzerland.
In Switzerland the municipality often also has a say in whether someone is naturalised.

teile.einleitung: Ascona is a holiday resort in Ticino on Lake Maggiore. It lies right next to Locarno. Known are the lakeside promenade, the old town and the Monte Verità.
wichtigste: Ascona lies on Lake Maggiore in the canton of Ticino.
Right next to it lies the city of Locarno.
From 1900 drop-outs and artists lived on the Monte Verità.
Every summer there is the JazzAscona festival.
Next to Ascona the Maggia has built up a large delta.
Ascona is a popular holiday resort with a mild climate.

abschnitte.text: Ascona lies in the **district of Locarno** in the canton of **Ticino**, right on **Lake Maggiore**. Right next to it lies the city of **Locarno**, and you can go across on foot or by bicycle. Because of the lake and the **mild climate**, Ascona is very popular with tourists. On the **lakeside promenade** there are cafés and palms.
The **old town** of Ascona has narrow, winding **lanes** with old houses. Many buildings have inner courtyards and stone walls. In between there are small shops, galleries and restaurants.

On the hill **Monte Verità**, from 1900, people lived who were looking for a simple, **nature-close life**. They ate no meat and lived in simple huts. Later many **artists**, dancers and writers came. The name means “Mountain of Truth”.
Every summer the festival **JazzAscona** takes place. Then bands play in the lanes and by the lake. Many visitors come to Ascona especially for the music.

The river **Maggia** comes from the Maggia Valley and flows into Lake Maggiore. Over a long time it carried sand and gravel into the lake. In this way a flat **delta** came about between Ascona and Locarno. Today housing districts and fields lie on it.

gewusst: The Maggia delta juts so far into the lake that Ascona and Locarno lie on two sides of it.
On the Monte Verità people were already looking for a healthier life over 100 years ago.

teile.einleitung: The Zentrum Paul Klee is a museum on the edge of Bern. It is dedicated to the painter Paul Klee. Its wavy roof looks like three hills.
wichtigste: The Zentrum Paul Klee stands on the edge of Bern.
It opened in 2005.
The architect is Renzo Piano from Italy.
The roof looks like three waves of hills.
The museum has the largest collection of works by Paul Klee.
For children there is a children's museum of its own for painting and making things.

abschnitte.text: **Paul Klee** was a well-known **painter**. He was born in **1879** in **Münchenbuchsee** near Bern and grew up in Bern. He often painted with strong **colours**, simple **shapes** and funny figures. He also taught at the famous art school **Bauhaus** in Germany. He died in **1940** in Ticino.

The museum was designed by the Italian architect **Renzo Piano**. Its **roof** consists of **three waves** that look like hills. In this way the building fits into the landscape on the edge of the city. The museum opened in **2005**. The idea for it came from the Bernese doctor **Maurice E. Müller**, who also helped to pay for it.

In the Zentrum Paul Klee there are **about 4,000 works** by Paul Klee. That is the **largest collection** of his pictures in the world. Because many works are painted on paper, they are **sensitive to light**. That is why the museum always shows only part of them and changes the exhibitions regularly.

In the museum there is the **children's museum Creaviva**. There children can **paint**, **draw** and **make things** themselves. They learn how Paul Klee played with colours and shapes. Around the museum there are meadows and paths where you can go for a walk.

gewusst: In his life Paul Klee created almost 10,000 works of art.
Klee played the violin very well and could almost have become a musician.

teile.einleitung: St Gallen is the main town of the canton of the same name in eastern Switzerland. The city is famous for its abbey district with the old library, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: The main town of the canton of St Gallen is also called St Gallen.
The city goes back to the monk Gallus, who lived here around 1,400 years ago.
The abbey district with the cathedral and the Abbey Library is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In the past St Gallen was world-famous for its embroidery.
The city has a well-known university and, every year, the OLMA trade fair.

abschnitte.text: The main town has the same name as the canton: **St Gallen**. The **cantonal government** and the **cantonal parliament** work here. They have their seat in the building of the old **Pfalz** (palace) in the abbey district. St Gallen is the largest city in eastern Switzerland. It lies in a high valley between Lake Constance and the Alpstein.

The city goes back to the Irish monk **Gallus**. He settled on the Steinach in the 7th century. A large **monastery** later grew up at this spot. The town grew around the monastery. The **abbey district** with the Baroque **cathedral** has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since **1983**.

A special treasure is the **Abbey Library**. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world. The Baroque hall is splendidly decorated with woodwork and paintings. Here lie very old **books** written by hand. Visitors have to put on felt slippers to protect the wooden floor.

In the past St Gallen was world-famous for **embroidery** and fine fabrics. Around 1900 embroidery was even one of Switzerland's most important exports. Today the city is also known for its **university**. Every autumn the **OLMA** takes place, a big trade fair for farming and food. Of course that includes the **St Gallen bratwurst**.

gewusst: In the Abbey Library lies the Plan of St Gall, a drawing of a monastery that is more than 1,000 years old.
In the city of St Gallen many houses have painted and decorated oriel windows.

teile.einleitung: The Susten Pass is an Alpine pass between the canton of Uri and the canton of Bern. The pass road runs from Wassen in the Reuss valley to Innertkirchen in the Bernese Oberland.
wichtigste: The Susten Pass links Uri with Bern.
On the Uri side lies the Meiental, on the Bern side the Gadmertal.
The top of the pass is over 2,200 metres above sea level.
The road was built between 1938 and 1946.
In winter the pass is closed.
Near the top of the pass lies the Stein Glacier.

abschnitte.text: The road begins in **Wassen** in the canton of Uri. It climbs through the **Meiental** to the top of the pass. Then it runs down through the **Gadmertal** to **Innertkirchen** in the canton of Bern. On the way there are many bends, tunnels and bridges. Together with the Grimsel Pass and the Furka Pass, the Susten forms a well-known round trip.

A mule track for people and animals had long led over the Susten. The present road was built from **1938 to 1946**. It was one of the first pass roads in Switzerland that was planned for **cars** from the start. Today it is very popular with motorcyclists and cyclists. PostBuses also run over the pass in summer.

On the Bern side, close to the road, lies the **Stein Glacier**. A small lake, the **Steinsee**, has formed in front of it. All around the pass rise high mountains of the **Uri Alps**. Like almost all glaciers in the Alps, the Stein Glacier has melted a great deal in recent decades.

At over 2,200 metres there is a great deal of **snow** in winter. That is why the Susten Pass is usually **closed** from autumn until early summer. In spring large snowblowers clear the road. Only then can you drive over it again.

gewusst: The name Susten comes from an old word for a storehouse, where goods used to be stored on their way over the mountains.
The round trip over the Susten, Grimsel and Furka is one of the best-known pass journeys in Switzerland.

tzjj5cc.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt shows a black Basel crozier on a white ground. The staff looks like a bishop's crook and recalls Basel's long history as a bishop's city.
wichtigste: In the Basel coat of arms is a black Basel crozier.
The ground is white.
The staff looks like a bishop's crozier.
It recalls the bishops of Basel.
Basel-Landschaft, by contrast, has a red staff.

abschnitte.text: The coat of arms of **Basel-Stadt** is very simple. On a **white** ground stands a **black Basel crozier**. At the top the staff is curved like a hook, at the bottom it tapers to a point. You see this emblem everywhere in Basel: on flags, fountains, trams and street signs.

The staff is a simplified **bishop's crozier**. A bishop carries a curved staff of this kind, which recalls a shepherd's crook. In the Middle Ages Basel was an important **bishop's city**. That is why the city chose this emblem. The **Basel Minster** used to be the bishop's church.

Since the separation of **1833** there have been two Basel cantons. **Basel-Stadt** kept the **black** staff. **Basel-Landschaft** received a **red** staff with small projections. So both cantons have a similar emblem, but one that is easy to tell apart.

gewusst: Basel-Stadt is the smallest canton in Switzerland by area.
The Basel crozier can be found on old seals and coins from the Middle Ages.
